signals.title: Segmentation guard gated on `balance > 0` drops the old unconditional size cap
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **Feeding non-JSON bytes containing no opening bracket to `JSONEachRow` with `input_format_parallel_parsing=1` buffers the entire input into a single segmentation `Memory<>` before failing. The old code threw as soon as the segment exceeded `10 * min_chunk_bytes_for_parallel_parsing`.** - **Root cause:** [`src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp:53`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp#L53) — the `balance > 0` conjunct. The check it replaced (`min_bytes != 0 && current_object_size > 10 * min_bytes`) was unconditional, so it also bounded bytes accumulated outside any object. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `ParallelParsingInputFormat` segmentator -> `JSONUtils::fileSegmentationEngineJSONEachRow` -> `fileSegmentationEngineJSONEachRowImpl` ([`src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp:53`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp#L53)). The size check is now inside `if (max_row_size && balance > 0)`. While no opening bracket has been seen `balance` stays 0, `find_first_symbols` scans to the buffer end, `continue` re-enters `loadAtPosition`, and the segment grows with no bound until EOF. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp:53`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp#L53) — size check gated on balance > 0 - [`src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp:111`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp#L111) — object_start_bytes updated only when balance reaches 0 **Impact:** The DoS protection that `01701_parallel_parsing_infinite_segmentation.sh` was written to guard is weakened: malformed input that never opens a bracket (truncated files, an HTML error page piped into `JSONEachRow`, JSONEachRow data sent to `JSONCompactEachRow` where the searched bracket is `[`) is buffered in full instead of being rejected at `10 * min_chunk_bytes_for_parallel_parsing` (100 MiB with defaults). Transient memory per malformed request grows from a bounded 100 MiB to the full input size. Because `input_format_json_max_object_size` is also not consulted anywhere on the non-parallel `JSONEachRow` data path, the segmentation engine is the only enforcement point for this format. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `da67f74224255`). ### How to reproduce _See root cause description and affected locations above._ ### Expected behavior ``` Code: 117. DB::Exception: Size of JSON object at position ... is extremely large. Expected not greater than 1048576 bytes, but current is ... bytes per object. Increase the value of setting 'input_format_json_max_object_size' or check your data manually, most likely JSON is malformed. (INCORRECT_DATA) ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` Code: 117. DB::Exception: Unexpected eof: (at row 0) : (in file/uri (fd = 0)): While executing JSONEachRowRowInputFormat: While executing File. (INCORRECT_DATA) ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Drop the `balance > 0` conjunct and keep `object_start_bytes` as the anchor: `if (max_row_size)` still measures bytes since the last completed object, which is the intended semantics and additionally bounds inter-object garbage. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - `input_format_json_max_object_size` is never read on the non-parallel `JSONEachRow`/`JSONCompactEachRow` data-parsing path with a known schema (verified: with `--input_format_json_max_object_size=1000 --structure='a String'`, a 50007-byte object is accepted at `input_format_parallel_parsing=0` and rejected at `=1`), which contradicts the setting description in `src/Core/FormatFactorySettings.h` ("The same limit is applied in both parallel and non-parallel parsing paths"). Found during automated review of [PR #107669](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107669). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr107669_002` </details> cc @Avogar @Manerone (from #107669)
signals.author: clickgapai

signals.title: New 1 GiB JSON guard measures the whole column chars buffer, not one value
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **Valid JSON input is rejected with `Code: 131. DB::Exception: JSON string is too large, maximum size is 1073741824 bytes` even though no individual string comes close to 1 GiB. Whether the same file is accepted or rejected depends on `max_block_size`.** - **Root cause:** [`src/IO/ReadHelpers.cpp:1298`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/IO/ReadHelpers.cpp#L1298) uses `s.size()` as a proxy for the current value's length. `s` is an append-target that callers pre-populate; the correct quantity is `s.size()` minus the size recorded at function entry. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `JSONEachRowRowInputFormat::readRow` -> `SerializationString::deserializeTextJSON` ([`src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationString.cpp:536`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationString.cpp#L536)) passes `ColumnString::Chars & data` — the destination column's whole chars buffer, which already holds every previous row of the current block — as the `Vector & s` argument of `readJSONStringInto`. The new check at [`src/IO/ReadHelpers.cpp:1298`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/IO/ReadHelpers.cpp#L1298) tests `s.size()`, i.e. the accumulated column size, not the size of the value being read. **Affected locations:** - [`src/IO/ReadHelpers.cpp:1298`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/IO/ReadHelpers.cpp#L1298) — readJSONStringInto: check on cumulative destination vector size - [`src/IO/ReadHelpers.cpp:1356`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/IO/ReadHelpers.cpp#L1356) — readJSONObjectOrArrayPossiblyInvalid: identical cumulative check - [`src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationString.cpp:536`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationString.cpp#L536) — passes ColumnString::Chars (whole block) as the append target - [`src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationString.cpp:502`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationString.cpp#L502) — same for readJSONObjectPossiblyInvalid under input_format_json_read_objects_as_strings - [`src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationFixedString.cpp:292`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationFixedString.cpp#L292) — passes ColumnFixedString::Chars as the append target **Impact:** Any `JSONEachRow` ingest whose String/FixedString column accumulates more than 1 GiB within a single block now fails with `TOO_LARGE_STRING_SIZE` on perfectly valid data. `input_format_max_block_size_bytes` defaults to 0, so blocks are row-bounded only (`max_insert_block_size` ~ 1048449 rows for INSERT), i.e. ~1 KB average string length is enough. The limit is hardcoded and cannot be raised or disabled by any setting. The same check also fires inside the `ReturnType = bool` instantiations (`tryReadJSONStringInto`, `readJSONObjectPossiblyInvalid<..., bool>`), throwing where the try-contract requires returning `false`, so `Variant`/`Dynamic` fallbacks turn into query errors. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `da67f74224255`). ### How to reproduce _See root cause description and affected locations above._ ### Expected behavior ``` 3 1258291200 in both arms - no individual JSON string exceeds 1 GiB, so neither arm should be rejected, and the outcome must not depend on max_block_size. ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` Arm A (default max_block_size): Code: 131. DB::Exception: JSON string is too large, maximum size is 1073741824 bytes: (while reading the value of key a): (at row 3) : (in file/uri (fd = 0)): While executing JSONEachRowRowInputFormat: While executing File. (TOO_LARGE_STRING_SIZE) Arm B (max_block_size=2, identical data): 3 1258291200 Object variant (input_format_json_read_objects_as_strings=1), d ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Record `const size_t initial_size = s.size();` at function entry and compare `s.size() - initial_size` against the limit in both `readJSONStringInto` and `readJSONObjectOrArrayPossiblyInvalid`. Also route the `ReturnType = bool` instantiations through the existing `error()` lambda instead of an unconditional `throw`, and consider making the cap configurable rather than hardcoded. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - `NullOutput::size()` was added returning 0, so the skip path is exempt — intentional, but it means the same input is bounded or unbounded depending on whether the column is materialized. Found during automated review of [PR #107669](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107669). Severity P1 · Finding `h_pr107669_001` </details> cc @Avogar @Manerone (from #107669)
signals.author: clickgapai

signals.title: Adaptive learning phase returns before the external-spill branch, ignoring `max_bytes_before_external_group_by`
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **With `enable_adaptive_aggregator = 1` (the new default) a producer that is still in the adaptive learning phase never spills: `max_bytes_before_external_group_by` (and `max_bytes_ratio_before_external_group_by`, which resolves into the same field) is silently a no-op for the whole learning window. Raising `adaptive_aggregator_freeze_threshold` widens that window over the entire query, so a `GROUP BY` that used to spill to disk now runs fully in RAM and dies with MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (or OOMs when no limit is set).** - **Root cause:** [`src/Interpreters/Aggregator.cpp:1949-1955`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Interpreters/Aggregator.cpp#L1949-L1955) — the learning-phase early return leaves `executeOnBlock` before the external-aggregation spill branch. The learning table is bounded only in KEYS (`adaptive_aggregator_freeze_threshold`) and only leaves the phase after `adaptive_freeze_give_up_row_multiple` (16) times that many rows, so with a raised threshold neither bound fires within the query and there is no byte bound at all. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `AggregatingTransform::consume` ([`src/Processors/Transforms/AggregatingTransform.cpp:1248`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Processors/Transforms/AggregatingTransform.cpp#L1248)) -> `Aggregator::executeOnBlock` -> the adaptive block at [`src/Interpreters/Aggregator.cpp:1888`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Interpreters/Aggregator.cpp#L1888). A producer that is neither frozen nor stood down falls to `if (!adaptive->isBaseline())` at [`src/Interpreters/Aggregator.cpp:1949`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Interpreters/Aggregator.cpp#L1949) and returns `true` at :1955, skipping `worthConvertToTwoLevel` / `convertToTwoLevel` and the `max_bytes_before_external_group_by` -> `writeToTemporaryFile` branch that follows at :1960+. The frozen arm at :1910-1929 at least calls `drainStagedChunksUnderMemoryPressure`; the learning arm has no memory check of any kind. `checkLimits` only enforces `max_rows_to_group_by`, which `AggregatingStep::adaptiveAggregatorRejectionReason` ([`src/Processors/QueryPlan/AggregatingStep.cpp:395`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Processors/QueryPlan/AggregatingStep.cpp#L395)) requires to be 0 for the adaptive path to be admitted at all. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Interpreters/Aggregator.cpp:1949`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Interpreters/Aggregator.cpp#L1949) — learning-phase early return, before the two-level conversion and the external spill branch - [`src/Interpreters/Aggregator.cpp:1929`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Interpreters/Aggregator.cpp#L1929) — frozen-phase early return; its only relief is the pressure sweep, whose floors do not scale with the external threshold - [`src/Interpreters/AdaptiveAggregationImpl.h:76`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Interpreters/AdaptiveAggregationImpl.h#L76) — `adaptive_pressure_spill_min_keys = 1'000'000` — a drained table is written only past this key count, regardless of `max_bytes_before_external_group_by` - [`src/Interpreters/AdaptiveAggregationImpl.h:82`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Interpreters/AdaptiveAggregationImpl.h#L82) — `adaptive_pressure_detached_bytes_budget = 256 << 20` — up to 256 MiB of detached tables in flight, regardless of the configured external threshold - [`src/Core/Settings.cpp:4325`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Core/Settings.cpp#L4325) — `enable_adaptive_aggregator` documentation claims the external aggregation settings are honored **Impact:** `max_bytes_before_external_group_by` / `max_bytes_ratio_before_external_group_by` stop bounding aggregation memory. Measured on this build with `max_bytes_before_external_group_by = 20000000` over `numbers_mt(3000000)` grouped by a 1..40-byte string key: `ExternalAggregationWritePart` = 46 with `enable_adaptive_aggregator = 0`, 7 at the default freeze threshold, and 0 once `adaptive_aggregator_freeze_threshold >= 1000000`. With `max_memory_usage = 200000000` and the same external threshold the baseline completes 5/5 while the default adaptive path fails 5/5 with MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED; a `max_memory_usage` sweep puts the baseline at ~150 MB and the adaptive path at ~300 MB for the same query. Without a memory limit this is an OOM instead of an exception. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `5c9f28ed5a2c5`). ### How to reproduce ```sql clickhouse local --query "SET max_threads=4, group_by_two_level_threshold=1000, collect_hash_table_stats_during_aggregation=0, enable_sharding_aggregator=0, max_bytes_before_external_group_by=20000000, max_bytes_ratio_before_external_group_by=0, enable_adaptive_aggregator=1, adaptive_aggregator_freeze_threshold=4000000; SELECT count() FROM (SELECT concat(toString(number), repeat('x', number % 40)) AS k, count() AS c FROM numbers_mt(3000000) GROUP BY k) FORMAT Null; SELECT coalesce(sum(value), 0) FROM system.events WHERE event = 'ExternalAggregationWritePart';" -- prints 0; the same command with enable_adaptive_aggregator=0 prints 46. ``` ### Expected behavior ``` baseline spills 1 adaptive spills with a raised freeze threshold 1 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` baseline spills 1 adaptive spills with a raised freeze threshold 0 ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Give the learning arm the same memory valve the frozen arm has, or simply let a learning producer fall through to the ordinary `worthConvertToTwoLevel` + `writeToTemporaryFile` branch (it has no frozen local table to preserve, so the two-level conversion is harmless — it just stands the producer down). Independently, scale `adaptive_pressure_spill_min_keys` / `adaptive_pressure_detached_bytes_budget` to `max_bytes_before_external_group_by` instead of hardcoding them, so a small external threshold is not overshot by a fixed ~150 MB. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - The frozen local tables themselves are never spillable by design (Aggregator.cpp:1910-1929). At the default threshold that is 16384 states per producer, which is unbounded in bytes for growing states such as `groupArray` or `quantiles` — worth a maintainer opinion even though the learning-phase hole is the provable part. Found during automated review of [PR #111459](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111459). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr111459_001` </details> cc @nihalzp @alexey-milovidov (from #111459)
signals.author: clickgapai

signals.title: Absent-column refusal disables a freshly materialized skip index with no ALTER MODIFY
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **On a wide part, `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN c ... DEFAULT ...` is metadata-only, so the part's `columns.txt` never lists `c`. A subsequent `ADD INDEX idx c` + `MATERIALIZE INDEX idx` writes correct granules into that part, but the new gate refuses the index at read time forever after. Pruning drops from 1/16 granules to 16/16 - the index is built, occupies disk, and never skips anything. Results stay correct.** - **Root cause:** `MergeTreeIndices.cpp:299` - the `return false` for a required column the part does not carry treats 'no part-side type to compare' as 'incompatible'. The granule was in fact built from the metadata type in force at `MATERIALIZE INDEX` time, so it is compatible whenever no `MODIFY COLUMN` happened in between; the code has no way to tell the two apart and fails closed on both. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor.cpp:2533` (and every other read path) -> `IMergeTreeIndex::getDeserializedFormat` (`MergeTreeIndices.cpp:365`) -> `IMergeTreeIndex::isPartTypeCompatible` (`MergeTreeIndices.cpp:292`) -> `part.tryGetColumn("c")` is nullopt because the wide part holds no `c`, `isSerializationDefinedSubcolumn` is false (`c` is a plain physical column), so the loop returns false and the format is reported as `{0, {}}` = not materialized. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeIndices.cpp:292`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeIndices.cpp#L292) — `if (!part_column)` branch in `isPartTypeCompatible` refusing a column absent from the part - [`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeIndices.cpp:365`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeIndices.cpp#L365) — `getDeserializedFormat` returns `{0, {}}` when `isPartTypeCompatible` is false **Impact:** Any skip index backfilled with `MATERIALIZE INDEX` over a column added by a metadata-only `ALTER ADD COLUMN` is silently inert on every wide part that predates the ADD COLUMN. Measured: `Granules: 1/16` before the PR vs `Granules: 16/16` after, i.e. the whole part is scanned instead of one granule (16x granule read amplification on this fixture; in general the index stops pruning entirely). The part recovers only when it is merged, which for parts above `max_bytes_to_merge_at_max_space_in_pool` may never happen. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `5c9f28ed5a2c5`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/d2f78ba3-4ea6-4ddc-8996-4faf9f33f308) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Test: a skip index materialized over a column that a wide part does not physically hold must still prune. DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_absent; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_present; SET use_skip_indexes = 1; SELECT '-- column absent from the part (ADD COLUMN with DEFAULT is metadata-only for wide parts)'; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_absent; CREATE TABLE t_absent (k UInt64, other String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k SETTINGS index_granularity = 4, index_granularity_bytes = 0, min_bytes_for_wide_part = 0, min_rows_for_wide_part = 0; INSERT INTO t_absent SELECT number, toString(number) FROM numbers(64); ALTER TABLE t_absent ADD COLUMN c UInt64 DEFAULT k * 3 SETTINGS mutations_sync = 2, alter_sync = 2; ALTER TABLE t_absent ADD INDEX idx c TYPE set(100) GRANULARITY 1 SETTINGS alter_sync = 2; ALTER TABLE t_absent MATERIALIZE INDEX idx SETTINGS mutations_sync = 2, alter_sync = 2; SELECT count() = 0 FROM system.parts_columns WHERE database = currentDatabase() AND table = 't_absent' AND active AND column = 'c'; SELECT sum(secondary_indices_uncompressed_bytes) > 0 FROM system.parts WHERE database = currentDatabase() AND table = 't_absent' AND active; SELECT count() > 0 FROM (EXPLAIN indexes = 1 SELECT count() FROM t_absent WHERE c = 150) WHERE explain ILIKE '%Granules: 1/16%'; SELECT count() FROM t_absent WHERE c = 150; SELECT '-- control: same index, column present in the part'; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_present; CREATE TABLE t_present (k UInt64, other String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k SETTINGS index_granularity = 4, index_granularity_bytes = 0, min_bytes_for_wide_part = 0, min_rows_for_wide_part = 0; INSERT INTO t_present SELECT number, toString(number) FROM numbers(64); ALTER TABLE t_present ADD COLUMN c UInt64 DEFAULT k * 3 SETTINGS mutations_sync = 2, alter_sync = 2; ALTER TABLE t_present MATERIALIZE COLUMN c SETTINGS mutations_sync = 2, alter_sync = 2; ALTER TABLE t_present ADD INDEX idx c TYPE set(100) GRANULARITY 1 SETTINGS alter_sync = 2; ALTER TABLE t_present MATERIALIZE INDEX idx SETTINGS mutations_sync = 2, alter_sync = 2; SELECT count() > 0 FROM (EXPLAIN indexes = 1 SELECT count() FROM t_present WHERE c = 150) WHERE explain ILIKE '%Granules: 1/16%'; SELECT count() FROM t_present WHERE c = 150; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_absent; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_present; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` -- column absent from the part (ADD COLUMN with DEFAULT is metadata-only for wide parts) 1 1 1 1 -- control: same index, column present in the part 1 1 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` -- column absent from the part (ADD COLUMN with DEFAULT is metadata-only for wide parts) 1 1 0 1 -- control: same index, column present in the part 1 1 ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Do not treat 'required column absent from the part' as incompatible on its own. Options, in increasing cost: (a) restore the pre-PR verdict for this branch and rely on the type comparison only for columns the part actually records - the granule of an absent column was built from the metadata type at MATERIALIZE time, so it is only stale if a later `MODIFY COLUMN` touched that column, which the existing `canUseIndex` pending-mutation check already covers for the un-killed case; (b) record the index's build-time column types in the part (checksums or a small sidecar) so the question can be answered instead of guessed. Trade-off for (a): the killed-mutation sequence in the PR's case 11 would again prune with a stale granule, so it trades this pruning regression back for that narrower correctness hole. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - The same refusal applies to text indexes, where `MergeTask::addBuildTextIndexesStep` (`MergeTask.cpp:3076`) then rebuilds the index on every merge instead of carrying the existing segments forward - extra merge CPU on top of the lost pruning. Not measured. Found during automated review of [PR #112484](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112484). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr112484_001` </details> cc @groeneai @alexey-milovidov @shankar-iyer (from #112484)
signals.author: clickgapai

signals.title: Positional Tuple hint over Parquet: tupleElement rewrite yields default values
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **`SELECT tupleElement(t, 1) FROM file('x.parquet', Parquet, 't Tuple(UInt64, String)')` returns zeros/empty strings instead of the file's values once the tuple-element rewrite is enabled for `StorageFile`. `WHERE tupleElement(t, 1) = 1` matches 0 rows instead of 1. With `input_format_parquet_allow_missing_columns = 0` the same query throws `THERE_IS_NO_COLUMN: Column t.1 was not found in parquet schema`.** - **Root cause:** For an unnamed `DataTypeTuple` the element name produced by `getSubcolumnForElement` is the ordinal (`"1"`, `"2"`), so `optimizeTupleOrVariantElement` builds the subcolumn name `t.1`. Its guards check the DECLARED structure only (`canOptimizeToSubcolumn` queries the storage snapshot built from the structure argument), which of course contains `t.1`. Nothing checks whether the format resolves that element by name or by position — and Parquet resolves the tuple type positionally (`SchemaConverter.cpp:723-731`) but the flattened subcolumn name by string. The PR's opt-in comment 'a tuple element is a real leaf in the file, so the format can serve `t.x` on its own' is false for a positional tuple hint. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `getTypedNodesForOptimization` (FunctionToSubcolumnsPass.cpp:858) now admits `StorageFile` via `storageAllowsTransformer` -> `supportsOptimizationToTupleElementSubcolumns` (StorageFile.h:132) -> `optimizeTupleOrVariantElement` (FunctionToSubcolumnsPass.cpp:428) replaces the function with a `ColumnNode` named `t.1` -> the Parquet reader resolves that flattened name by string lookup (`SchemaConverter.cpp:232`, `sample_block->findPositionByName(node.name, ...)`) against the file's real field names `t.x`/`t.y` -> no match -> synthetic missing column filled with defaults. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Analyzer/Passes/FunctionToSubcolumnsPass.cpp:428`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Analyzer/Passes/FunctionToSubcolumnsPass.cpp#L428) — builds `t.<element>` subcolumn name; new guards do not check `hasExplicitNames` - [`src/Storages/StorageFile.h:132`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Storages/StorageFile.h#L132) — `supportsOptimizationToTupleElementSubcolumns` returns true unconditionally - [`src/Storages/StorageURL.h:374`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Storages/StorageURL.h#L374) — same opt-in for `url()` - [`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorage.h:106`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorage.h#L106) — same opt-in for `s3()`/`azure()` - [`src/Processors/Formats/Impl/Parquet/SchemaConverter.cpp:232`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5c9f28ed5a2c5/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/Parquet/SchemaConverter.cpp#L232) — flattened subcolumn name resolved by string lookup, never positionally **Impact:** Silent wrong results for any `file()`/`s3()`/`url()` Parquet read that declares a positional (unnamed) `Tuple` in the structure argument — a documented, supported way to read a struct written by an external writer (Spark, pandas, Arrow) without repeating its field names. Affects both the v3 and the legacy Parquet reader. With `input_format_parquet_allow_missing_columns = 0` the query is rejected instead. ORC is not affected. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `5c9f28ed5a2c5`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/43170dc7-eed8-4aac-9ac4-ab16ab01d90b) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Test that a positional (unnamed) Tuple structure hint still returns the file's values. SET enable_analyzer = 1; SET optimize_functions_to_subcolumns = 1; INSERT INTO FUNCTION file(currentDatabase() || '_04907.parquet', Parquet, 't Tuple(x UInt64, y String)') SELECT tuple(number, toString(number)) FROM numbers(3) SETTINGS engine_file_truncate_on_insert = 1; SELECT tupleElement(t, 1), tupleElement(t, 2) FROM file(currentDatabase() || '_04907.parquet', Parquet, 't Tuple(UInt64, String)') ORDER BY 1; SELECT count() FROM file(currentDatabase() || '_04907.parquet', Parquet, 't Tuple(UInt64, String)') WHERE tupleElement(t, 1) = 1; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` 0 0 1 1 2 2 1 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` 0 0 0 0 ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> In `optimizeTupleOrVariantElement`, refuse the rewrite when `!data_type_concrete.hasExplicitNames()` and the storage only opted in through `supportsOptimizationToTupleElementSubcolumns` (the element name is an ordinal that no file schema carries). Alternatively make `SchemaConverter` resolve an ordinal-named subcolumn positionally when the parent tuple hint is unnamed, matching what it already does for the whole tuple. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - The same declared-vs-physical name mismatch may exist for other formats reached through `StorageFile`/`StorageObjectStorage` that resolve subcolumns by name; only Parquet, ORC, CSV and JSONEachRow were probed here (CSV and JSONEachRow behave identically with and without the rewrite). Found during automated review of [PR #113383](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113383). Severity P1 · Finding `h_pr113383_001` </details> cc @groeneai @alexey-milovidov (from #113383)

signals.title: Hudi Merge-on-Read: uncompacted log files are silently ignored, returning stale rows
signals.text: ### Company or project name ClickHouse QA (data-lake durability testing) ### Describe what's wrong Reading an Apache Hudi **Merge-on-Read** (MoR) table that has uncompacted log files returns **stale rows silently** — no error, no warning. ClickHouse's Hudi reader parses only the base Parquet files per file group and never reads the Avro `.log.*` delta files that a MoR upsert writes, so any row updated after the last compaction is served at its **superseded** value. `HudiMetadata.cpp` states this directly: ```cpp /* There can be two types of data files * 1. base files (columnar file formats like Apache Parquet/Orc) * 2. log files * Currently we support reading only `base files`. ``` The problem is not the limitation itself but that it is **silent**: the row count is correct and the query succeeds, so a user cannot tell that the values are out of date. Every other Hudi reader (Spark, Presto/Trino, Hive) merges the log files and returns the current values, so ClickHouse and every reference engine disagree on the same table with no indication that ClickHouse is wrong. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes — the code path (`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/HudiMetadata.cpp`, `getDataFilesImpl`) is unchanged on current master. Verified on 26.8.1.1. ### How to reproduce 1. With Apache Spark + `hudi-spark3.5-bundle`, write a Merge-on-Read table to S3, then upsert a few existing keys **without compaction** (so the updates land in `.log` files, not a new base file): ```python opts = { "hoodie.table.name": "h_mor", "hoodie.datasource.write.table.type": "MERGE_ON_READ", "hoodie.datasource.write.recordkey.field": "id", "hoodie.datasource.write.precombine.field": "ts", "hoodie.datasource.write.operation": "upsert", "hoodie.compact.inline": "false", "hoodie.compact.inline.max.delta.commits": "999", } # base: id 0..29, v = id*7 spark.createDataFrame([(i, i*7, 1) for i in range(30)], ["id","v","ts"]) \ .write.format("hudi").options(**opts).mode("overwrite").save(path) # uncompacted update: ids 0..4 get a new value 999000..999004 spark.createDataFrame([(i, 999000+i, 2) for i in range(5)], ["id","v","ts"]) \ .write.format("hudi").options(**opts).mode("append").save(path) ``` 2. Spark (the reference reader) returns the **updated** values: ``` spark.read.format("hudi").load(path) # ids 0..4 -> v = 999000..999004 ``` 3. ClickHouse returns the **old base** values for the same keys, with the same row count and no error: ```sql SELECT id, v FROM hudi('http://<endpoint>/<bucket>/h_mor', '<key>', '<secret>') WHERE id < 5 ORDER BY id; -- 0 0 -- 1 7 -- 2 14 -- 3 21 -- 4 28 -- stale; the committed values 999000..999004 are ignored SELECT count() FROM hudi(...); -- 30 (correct count, wrong values) ``` Running Hudi compaction (so the updates are merged into a new base file) makes ClickHouse return the correct values — confirming the divergence is specifically the ignored log files, not a general read failure. ### Expected behavior Reading a Merge-on-Read table should return the current merged values (base + log files), matching every other Hudi reader. If merging log files is genuinely unsupported, ClickHouse should **fail loudly** (throw) when a queried MoR table has uncompacted log files, rather than silently returning stale rows. ### Error message and/or stacktrace None — the query succeeds and returns a correct row count with stale values. That silence is the core of the report. ### Additional context Copy-on-Write Hudi tables are unaffected (every update rewrites the base file). The issue is specific to Merge-on-Read tables with uncompacted deltas, which is the default write path for streaming/upsert Hudi ingestion.

signals.title: Concurrent `ALTER NAMED COLLECTION` on a Keeper-backed store silently loses one update: both ALTERs report success, one change vanishes
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong With `named_collections_storage.type = zookeeper` (or `keeper`), named-collection metadata is a single SQL blob per collection stored in one Keeper znode. `ALTER NAMED COLLECTION` is a read-modify-write of that blob with **no optimistic-concurrency (version) check**, so two concurrent ALTERs issued on different replicas both return success while only one survives in the durable Keeper state. The other change is silently discarded — no error, no warning, no log line. `NamedCollectionsMetadataStorage::update` reads the current CREATE query (`readCreateQuery`), applies the ALTER delta in memory, and writes the whole blob back with `replace = true` (`src/Common/NamedCollections/NamedCollectionsMetadataStorage.cpp:578-586`). `ZooKeeperStorage::write` (`:308-315`) calls `zkutil::ZooKeeper::createOrUpdate`, which is `trySet(path, data, /* version */ -1)` (`src/Common/ZooKeeper/ZooKeeper.cpp:906-914`) — version `-1` means "any version", i.e. no CAS. The per-process `NamedCollectionFactory` mutex (`src/Common/NamedCollections/NamedCollectionsFactory.cpp:333`) serializes ALTERs within one server, but two servers hold two independent mutexes, so their reads race and the later `set` overwrites the earlier one: ``` A: read {base} B: read {base} A: write {base, keyA} B: write {base, keyB} <- keyA is gone; both ALTERs acked ``` This is a metadata durability loss. Because `S3`, `IcebergS3`, and `DeltaLakeS3` tables re-resolve the collection at query/attach time (`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorageConfiguration.cpp:98-130`) rather than inlining its values, a concurrently-lost credential or endpoint rotation is then used with no indication that it was dropped. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes. Reproduced on `26.8.1.1` (master). The code path is present in current master. ### How to reproduce Two servers sharing one Keeper, both configured with a Keeper-backed named-collection store: ```xml <!-- both servers --> <named_collections_storage> <type>zookeeper</type> <path>/named_collections</path> </named_collections_storage> <zookeeper> <node><host>127.0.0.1</host><port>KEEPER_PORT</port></node> </zookeeper> ``` ```sql -- on server A CREATE NAMED COLLECTION coll AS base = 'b'; -- (wait a moment for it to appear on server B) ``` Then fire one ALTER on each server concurrently, e.g.: ```bash clickhouse client --port PORT_A -q "ALTER NAMED COLLECTION coll SET keyA = '1'" & clickhouse client --port PORT_B -q "ALTER NAMED COLLECTION coll SET keyB = '1'" & wait ``` Both commands succeed. Inspect the durable collection (after both replicas converge): ```sql SELECT arraySort(mapKeys(collection)) FROM system.named_collections WHERE name = 'coll'; ``` Observed: only one of `keyA` / `keyB` is present (e.g. `['base','keyB']`). Repeating the concurrent pair loses one key on essentially every iteration. Controls that show it is specifically the cross-node, un-versioned write: - Running the two ALTERs **sequentially** (A, then B after it propagates) keeps both keys. - Running the two ALTERs **concurrently against the same server** keeps both keys (the factory mutex serializes them). ### Expected behavior Two concurrent `ALTER NAMED COLLECTION` statements that both report success must both be reflected in the durable state — or one must fail loudly (e.g. a ret/version conflict) rather than being silently discarded. The keeper-backed store should use an optimistic-concurrency check (`set` with the observed version, retrying the read-modify-write on `ZBADVERSION`) instead of an unconditional `createOrUpdate`. ### Error message and/or stacktrace None. Both ALTERs return success; the loss is silent. ### Related issues and pull requests - #107593 — `ALTER NAMED COLLECTION` changes not picked up by Kafka engine tables (a same-node engine cache; different root cause — there the durable collection is correct). - #113455 — `ENGINE = Backup` storage-policy cache key ignores the resolved destination after `ALTER NAMED COLLECTION` (also a same-node cache). ### Additional context Only the Keeper-backed store (`type = zookeeper`/`keeper`) is affected; the `local` store is single-node and serialized by the in-memory factory mutex. The scenario is a normal multi-replica deployment where two operators or two automated jobs rotate different keys of the same collection at about the same time.

signals.title: DataLakeCatalog: aws_external_id setting leaks in plaintext in SHOW CREATE DATABASE / system.databases.engine_full (masked everywhere else)
signals.text: **Describe what's wrong** A `DataLakeCatalog` database masks every credential-bearing setting in `SHOW CREATE DATABASE` and `system.databases.engine_full` **except `aws_external_id`**, which is shown in plaintext — at the default `format_display_secrets_in_show_and_select = 0` and without the `displaySecretsInShowAndSelect` privilege. Any user who can run `SHOW CREATE DATABASE` or read `system.databases` sees it. `aws_external_id` is the external ID passed to AWS STS `AssumeRole`, matching the `sts:ExternalId` condition on the role's trust policy (its own setting description in `src/Databases/DataLake/DatabaseDataLakeSettings.cpp` notes it is for roles owned by a third party, such as ClickHouse Cloud). ClickHouse already treats this value as a secret in the *inline* `s3()` / `extra_credentials` form: `external_id` is a member of `s3_secret_keys` in `src/Parsers/FunctionSecretArgumentsFinder.h`, whose own comment calls it "the shared secret of the assume-role triple". So the identical value is masked in one surface and leaked in another. The cause is that the `SETTINGS_TO_HIDE` masking map in `src/Databases/DataLake/DataLakeConstants.h` lists `catalog_credential`, `auth_header`, `aws_access_key_id`, `aws_secret_access_key`, the `storage_*` variants, `onelake_*`, `google_adc_client_secret` / `google_adc_refresh_token`, and `dlf_*`, but has no entry for `aws_external_id`. (`aws_role_session_name` is likewise absent from the map, but that is an operator-chosen session label rather than a secret; the concern here is `aws_external_id`.) **How to reproduce** Any ClickHouse build with the Glue `DataLakeCatalog` backend. The Glue catalog is constructed lazily, so no live endpoint is needed to observe the masking: ```sql SET allow_database_glue_catalog = 1; CREATE DATABASE ge ENGINE = DataLakeCatalog('https://glue.us-east-1.amazonaws.com') SETTINGS catalog_type = 'glue', region = 'us-east-1', aws_access_key_id = 'AKIAEXAMPLE', aws_secret_access_key = 'SECRET', aws_role_arn = 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/r', aws_external_id = 'my-external-id-value'; SELECT engine_full FROM system.databases WHERE name = 'ge'; ``` Output (note `aws_secret_access_key` is `[HIDDEN]` but `aws_external_id` is verbatim): ``` DataLakeCatalog('https://glue.us-east-1.amazonaws.com') SETTINGS catalog_type = 'glue', region = 'us-east-1', aws_access_key_id = '[HIDDEN]', aws_secret_access_key = '[HIDDEN]', aws_role_arn = 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/r', aws_external_id = 'my-external-id-value' ``` `SHOW CREATE DATABASE ge` shows the same unmasked value. **Expected behavior** `aws_external_id` should be masked as `'[HIDDEN]'` in `SHOW CREATE DATABASE`, `system.databases.engine_full`, and any other formatted-with-secrets-hidden surface, consistent with how the inline `external_id` argument is masked via `s3_secret_keys` and with the other credential settings in `SETTINGS_TO_HIDE`. **Which ClickHouse server versions are incompatible** Reproduced on master (26.8). By code inspection the gap exists on every version whose `SETTINGS_TO_HIDE` map omits `aws_external_id`.

signals.title: Arrow Flight SQL: CommandGetXdbcTypeInfo is not implemented
signals.text: ### Company or project name _No response_ ### Describe the unexpected behaviour ## Describe the issue [`CommandGetXdbcTypeInfo`](https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/f64e90ac8305c2cab5abd849f02abac305d7a955/format/FlightSql.proto#L1075-L1138) - the standard Flight SQL command that returns the server's data-type catalog - is not handled by the Arrow Flight SQL server. The [command dispatch](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Server/ArrowFlight/commandSelector.cpp#L626-L718) covers GetSqlInfo / GetCatalogs / GetDbSchemas / GetTables / GetTableTypes / GetPrimaryKeys and the statement commands, but has no branch for `CommandGetXdbcTypeInfo`, so it falls into the [`NotImplemented` catch-all](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Server/ArrowFlight/commandSelector.cpp#L713-L718): ```Command is not implemented: [type.googleapis.com/arrow.flight.protocol.sql.CommandGetXdbcTypeInfo]``` ## Impact Generic clients rely on this catalog to interpret column types: - **Power BI**'s built-in ADBC Flight SQL path fails to load **every** table - even a single `String` column - with `Expression.Error: Unable to understand the type for column` (Verified: the identical connector works once type metadata is supplied client-side.) - The Flight SQL **JDBC** driver's `DatabaseMetaData.getTypeInfo()` has the same dependency. Related: the `CommandGetTables` `include_schema` path serializes schemas without any `ARROW:FLIGHT:SQL:*` field metadata (e.g. `TYPE_NAME`), so per-column type names are unavailable there as well. ### How to reproduce ```python # pip install pyarrow import pyarrow.flight as flight client = flight.FlightClient("grpc://localhost:9006") tok = client.authenticate_basic_token(b"default", b"clickhouse") url = b"type.googleapis.com/arrow.flight.protocol.sql.CommandGetXdbcTypeInfo" any_msg = bytes([0x0A, len(url)]) + url # google.protobuf.Any{type_url}, empty message desc = flight.FlightDescriptor.for_command(any_msg) client.get_flight_info(desc, flight.FlightCallOptions(headers=[tok])) # -> ArrowNotImplementedError: Command is not implemented: ...CommandGetXdbcTypeInfo ``` Reproduced on 26.5.1.882 and 26.6.1.1193 (official Docker images). ### Expected behavior _No response_ ### Error message and/or stacktrace _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_

signals.title: Histogram metric `keeper_read_wait_for_write_time_milliseconds` is never recorded with the new request dispatcher
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong The Prometheus histogram `keeper_read_wait_for_write_time_milliseconds` ("Time read request waits for the write request it depends on to complete") is still registered and exported, but it is never observed when `use_new_dispatcher` is enabled (the default). The new dispatcher still parks read requests behind in-flight same-session writes (`LateReads` in `KeeperRequestDispatcher`), so the wait the metric is supposed to measure still happens — it is just no longer instrumented. Consumers of the metric see a histogram that is present but permanently empty, which reads as "reads never wait for writes" instead of "not measured". The Keeper stress-test nightlies confirm it: on `prod-mix-no-fault` the histogram recorded ~875k observations per run (average wait ~65 ms) up to the 2026-05-21 nightly, and exactly 0 from the 2026-05-23 nightly onward — the first nightly containing the new dispatcher. All sibling Keeper span histograms (`keeper_read_process_*`, `keeper_write_commit_*`, `keeper_receive_request_*`, ...) kept reporting across the same boundary. ### How to reproduce * Which ClickHouse server version to use: any build after 2026-05-22 (master) Run a 3-node `clickhouse-keeper` ensemble with the Prometheus endpoint enabled, drive a mixed read/write workload that issues reads while writes from the same session are in flight (e.g. `keeper-bench` with a prod-mix workload), and watch `keeper_read_wait_for_write_time_milliseconds_count`: it stays at 0. With `<use_new_dispatcher>0</use_new_dispatcher>` in `coordination_settings` it advances as before. Public data from the Keeper stress warehouse showing the flatline (per-nightly max of the exported `_count`): ```sql SELECT toDate(ts) AS d, max(value) AS cnt FROM keeper_stress_tests.keeper_metrics_ts WHERE scenario = 'prod-mix-no-fault[default]' AND branch = 'master' AND name = 'ClickHouseHistogramMetrics_keeper_read_wait_for_write_time_milliseconds_count' AND ts >= '2026-05-19' GROUP BY d ORDER BY d -- 2026-05-19: 874616, 2026-05-21: 886896, 2026-05-23 and later: 0 ``` (run on https://play.clickhouse.com/ with user `play`) Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/101757

signals.title: Arrow Flight SQL: CloseSession action not implemented - errors instead of closing
signals.text: ### Company or project name _No response_ ### Describe the unexpected behaviour The Flight session-management spec defines three actions: [`SetSessionOptions`, `GetSessionOptions`, `CloseSession`](https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/f64e90ac8305c2cab5abd849f02abac305d7a955/format/Flight.proto#L600-L660). ClickHouse implements the first two ([Set](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Server/ArrowFlight/ArrowFlightServer.cpp#L1342), [Get](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Server/ArrowFlight/ArrowFlightServer.cpp#L1425)) but `CloseSession` falls into the [DoAction catch-all](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Server/ArrowFlight/ArrowFlightServer.cpp#L1614-L1615): ```<Error> ArrowFlightServer: DoAction failed: NotImplemented: CloseSession is not supported``` So spec-compliant clients cannot tear down sessions cleanly, and every attempt logs an Error-level entry. (A close path exists, but only via the nonstandard [`x-clickhouse-session-close` header](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Server/ArrowFlight/AuthMiddleware.cpp#L252-L254).) ### Related: bearer-token TTL Each basic-auth call mints a bearer token returned in the[`authorization` response header](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Server/ArrowFlight/AuthMiddleware.cpp#L25-L29), expiring on a [60-second sliding TTL (`default_session_timeout`)](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Server/ArrowFlight/AuthMiddleware.cpp#L152). On a failed RPC the response header (and rotated token) may never reach the client, and BI tools routinely idle >60 s between user interactions - the result is spurious `Session expired or not authenticated` failures that surface in Power BI as **"We couldn't authenticate with the credentials provided"** with valid credentials. ### How to reproduce ```python # pip install pyarrow import pyarrow.flight as flight client = flight.FlightClient("grpc://localhost:9006") tok = client.authenticate_basic_token(b"default", b"clickhouse") opts = flight.FlightCallOptions(headers=[tok]) list(client.do_action(flight.Action("CloseSession", b""), opts)) # -> ArrowNotImplementedError: CloseSession is not supported ``` Reproduced on 26.5.1.882 and 26.6.1.1193 (official Docker images). ### Expected behavior CloseSession returns CloseSessionResult{CLOSED} and releases the session, or at minimum succeeds as a no-op, so clients can recycle pooled connections without error noise. ### Error message and/or stacktrace _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_

signals.title: Arrow: unsupported-types-as-binary fallback crashes on JSON/Dynamic columns
signals.text: ### Company or project name _No response_ ### Describe the unexpected behaviour Exporting a `JSON` (or `Dynamic`) column to Arrow fails the whole query: ```Code: 48. DB::Exception: Method getDataAt is not supported for Object(max_dynamic_paths=1024, max_dynamic_types=32): While executing Arrow. (NOT_IMPLEMENTED)``` The safety net for types without an Arrow mapping - `output_format_arrow_unsupported_types_as_binary` (**default 1**) - correctly classifies these types and maps them to `arrow::binary()` on the schema side, but the **data-side fallback is broken**: 1. [`getArrowType` maps the unsupported type to binary](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/CHColumnToArrowColumn.cpp#L1735-L1739) - schema conversion succeeds. 2. [`fillArrowArray`'s default case routes data into the fallback](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/CHColumnToArrowColumn.cpp#L1451-L1454). 3. [`fillArrowArrayWithRawColumnData` fetches each row via `IColumn::getDataAt`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/CHColumnToArrowColumn.cpp#L200) — 4. which [`ColumnObject` does not implement](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Columns/ColumnObject.cpp#L429-L431) (nor does [`ColumnVariant`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Columns/ColumnVariant.cpp#L454-L456), which `Dynamic` delegates to). So the fallback crashes on precisely the modern types it exists to cover. A tell-tale artifact: the output contains a valid Arrow schema (`binary` field) with 0 rows before the error. ### How to reproduce ```bash clickhouse local -q "SELECT '{\"a\":1}'::JSON AS j FORMAT Arrow" # Code: 48, getDataAt clickhouse local -q "SELECT 42::Dynamic AS d FORMAT Arrow" # Code: 48, getDataAt (Variant) ``` Reproduced on 26.5.1.882 and 26.6.1.1193 via FORMAT Arrow, HTTP, native client, and Arrow Flight SQL (src/Server/ArrowFlight/ passes output_unsupported_types_as_binary on every conversion, so any Flight SQL SELECT touching a table with a JSON column fails — one JSON column makes a table unreadable for BI clients like Power BI). ### Expected behavior _No response_ ### Error message and/or stacktrace _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_

signals.title: Correlated scalar subquery: max() over a non-empty group returns NULL for a subset of rows under a small max_block_size (nondeterministic wrong result)
signals.text: ### Summary A correlated scalar subquery whose aggregate is `max` (and, we expect, any aggregate) returns `NULL` for a subset of the outer rows of a **non-empty** correlation group, when the query runs with a `max_block_size` below the default. `max` over a non-empty set can never be `NULL`, so the result is silently wrong. It is also **nondeterministic**: the number of wrongly-`NULL` rows changes from run to run (observed `0`, `16384`, `54464`) at fixed settings, which points to a race in the correlated-subquery decorrelation join rather than a plan-level mistake. At the default `max_block_size` the same query is correct. This is distinct from the empty-group family (#111615 / #111832 — those return `NULL` instead of `0`/`[]` for a genuinely *empty* group): here the group is provably non-empty (it has 120000 rows and its true `max(k)` is `339999`), and the trigger is the physical `max_block_size`, not the group being empty. It is also distinct from #112576 (a `NULL` *correlation value*): the correlation column `s` is never `NULL` here. Correlated subqueries require the new analyzer (`enable_analyzer = 1`, the default) and `allow_experimental_correlated_subqueries = 1` (also the default on this build). ### ClickHouse version Reproduced on `master` (`26.8.1.1485` and `26.8.1.1448`, both from the CI build cache). ### How to reproduce ```sql CREATE TABLE t (g UInt32, k UInt64, s LowCardinality(String)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY (g, k); INSERT INTO t SELECT intHash32(number) % 30000, number, 'g' || toString(number % 200) FROM numbers(220000); INSERT INTO t SELECT number % 512, 220000 + number, 'hot' FROM numbers(120000); INSERT INTO t SELECT 3000000000 + number, 340000 + number, 'x' || toString(number) FROM numbers(60000); -- The 'hot' group is non-empty; its true max(k) is 339999, so no output row may carry a NULL max: SELECT max(k) FROM t WHERE s = 'hot'; -- 339999 -- The offending query: the same correlated max subquery in the SELECT and in the WHERE. -- The WHERE predicate `mk >= o.k` is always true (mk is the group's max), so every one of the -- 400000 rows must be returned, each with a non-NULL mk. SELECT o.s, (SELECT max(i.k) FROM t AS i WHERE i.s = o.s) AS mk FROM t AS o WHERE (SELECT max(i.k) FROM t AS i WHERE i.s = o.s) >= o.k SETTINGS max_threads = 1, max_block_size = 100; ``` **Expected:** 400000 rows, and no row has `mk = NULL` (every group is non-empty). **Actual:** the output still has 400000 rows, but 16384 of the `('hot', …)` rows carry `mk = \N` (NULL). Counting them: ``` $ clickhouse-client --query "$Q" --max_threads=1 --max_block_size=100 | grep -Pc '^hot\t\\N$' 16384 ``` Run it again (dropping the mark cache in between is not required) and the count changes — we observed `0`, `16384` and `54464` `NULL`-max `hot` rows across runs at the identical settings, with `max_threads = 8` making the nondeterminism more pronounced. At the default `max_block_size` (`65409`) the query is stable and correct (`0` NULL rows); the wrong result appears once `max_block_size` drops below roughly `32768`. ### Reproducibility Deterministically wrong in 19 of 20 consecutive runs on a freshly started, otherwise-idle server (one run happened to return the correct `0`, which is the nondeterminism itself). The output is complete every time (all 400000 rows), so this is not truncation. Wrapping the query in an outer `SELECT count() FROM (…)` re-plans it and hides the bug, and restricting the outer query to `WHERE o.s = 'hot'` also hides it — the divergence only surfaces in the bare multi-group query with the correlated subquery in both the `SELECT` and the `WHERE`. ### Related - Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111615 - Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112576 - Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111440 Found by an automatic optimizer-testing framework.
signals.author: zlareb1

signals.title: NightlySQLancer: LIMIT 1 BY returned the same key twice under ORDER BY (not reproduced)
signals.text: The 2026-08-16 NightlySQLancer run (`arm_asan_ubsan`, master @ 5c9f28ed5a2c585ad46bf74d6600cdcf3aa07a9e) failed with a `LIMIT BY` cap violation that I could not reproduce; filing this to track it in case it recurs. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=5c9f28ed5a2c585ad46bf74d6600cdcf3aa07a9e&name_0=NightlySQLancer&name_1=SQLancer%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%29&name_1=SQLancer ``` java.lang.AssertionError: LimitRanking LIMIT-BY cap violation: key 0 appears 2 times but 'LIMIT 1 BY `c0`' caps it at 1. Q: SELECT toString(`c0`) FROM `t0` ORDER BY `c0` ASC LIMIT 1 BY `c0` ``` The table is `CREATE TABLE t0 (c0 String) ENGINE = MergeTree() ORDER BY tuple()`, filled by 11 small `VALUES` inserts (18 rows, among them the empty string four times) and one `INSERT INTO t0 SELECT toString(number) FROM numbers(9982)` — 10000 rows total, and the value `'0'` exists in the table **exactly once** (the other values starting with `0` are `'0.0'`, `'0.85...'`, `'0S...'` — different strings). No mutations or deletes ever ran on the table, and no other statement in the session log touches it. So for the result of `SELECT toString(c0) FROM t0 ORDER BY c0 ASC LIMIT 1 BY c0` to contain the key `'0'` twice, the result stream must have contained the same physical row twice. The plan for this query is a full sort into a single stream followed by `LimitBySortedStreamTransform`, which removes adjacent duplicates, so the duplicate must have been non-adjacent (or appeared on the client side). What I tried, without a single reproduction: - Rebuilt the exact table content (from the SQLancer reproducer log) and ran the query 300 times on a release master build and 500 times on the **exact** `arm_asan_ubsan` binary of the failing run, sweeping `max_threads` 1..64, `optimize_read_in_order`, `query_plan_optimize_lazy_materialization`, `read_in_order_use_buffering`, with six concurrent workers doing INSERT/SELECT/OPTIMIZE/ALTER DELETE noise on another table. - The CI server error log of the run has no sanitizer reports and no logical errors ("exception" class); the SQLancer overrides pin only `alter_sync`/`mutations_sync`/`async_insert` and disable logs — no fault-injection settings are involved. - This is the first occurrence of this oracle failure in at least 30 days of nightly runs. Two hypotheses, in decreasing order of plausibility to me: 1. A harness-side artifact: the SQLancer provider uses the `com.clickhouse:client-v2` HTTP transport, which retries requests (newer `ClickHouse/sqlancer` commits added `"Query request failed (attempt:"` and other transport errors to the tolerated error sets). If a retry happens after part of the first response body was already consumed and the reader concatenates the partial and the retried response, a duplicated key appears in the client-side result without any server misbehavior. 2. A very rare race in the read/sort pipeline that duplicates a row (the sorted-stream `LIMIT BY` transform only removes adjacent duplicates, so a duplicated row that ends up non-adjacent after the sort would pass through). The sibling failure of the same run (the `FinalMerge` oracle mismatch on a `SummingMergeTree` table) turned out to be a genuine, deterministic server bug and is fixed separately. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115032

signals.title: Paimon: pypaimon-written MAP columns make the whole table unreadable (Unsupported Paimon type: MAP<STRING, BIGINT>)
signals.text: **Describe what's wrong** A Paimon table with a `MAP` column written by pypaimon 2.0 (the official Apache Paimon Python SDK, `pip install pypaimon`) is completely unreadable by ClickHouse: both `DESCRIBE` and `SELECT` over `paimonLocal` / `paimon` fail with `Code: 36. DB::Exception: Unsupported Paimon type: MAP<STRING, BIGINT>`. The cause is a spelling mismatch in the composite-type kind. For a composite field, Java Paimon serializes the inner `type` as the bare kind (`"MAP"` / `"MAP NOT NULL"`), and ClickHouse's parser requires exactly that: `src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Paimon/Types.h` strips ` NOT NULL` and then compares `real_type == "MAP"` (and `== "ARRAY"`) for equality. pypaimon 2.0 instead writes the full generic signature into that field, e.g. `"MAP<STRING NOT NULL, BIGINT>"`, so after the ` NOT NULL` strip ClickHouse is left with `MAP<STRING, BIGINT>`, the exact-match fails, and the whole table throws. The `key`/`value` element types are carried in their own JSON fields either way, so the generic arguments in the kind string are redundant — a kind-prefix match would read both spellings. `schema/schema-0` as written by pypaimon 2.0: ```json {"id": 1, "name": "m", "type": {"type": "MAP<STRING NOT NULL, BIGINT>", "key": "STRING NOT NULL", "value": "BIGINT", "nullable": true}} ``` The same table written by Java Paimon carries `"type": "MAP NOT NULL"` in that position and reads fine. `ARRAY` columns are unaffected because pypaimon spells their kind as bare `ARRAY`. **Does it reproduce on the most recent release?** Reproduces on master 26.8.1.1448, 20/20 runs. **How to reproduce** Write a MAP-bearing table with pypaimon 2.0 (`pip install pypaimon pyarrow`): ```python import pyarrow as pa from pypaimon import CatalogFactory, Schema cat = CatalogFactory.create({"warehouse": "/tmp/pmap_wh"}) cat.create_database("db", ignore_if_exists=True) schema = pa.schema([("k", pa.int64()), ("m", pa.map_(pa.string(), pa.int64()))]) cat.create_table("db.t", Schema.from_pyarrow_schema(schema), ignore_if_exists=True) t = cat.get_table("db.t") wb = t.new_batch_write_builder() bw, cw = wb.new_write(), wb.new_commit() bw.write_arrow(pa.table({"k": pa.array([1, 2], pa.int64()), "m": pa.array([[("a", 1)], [("b", 2)]], pa.map_(pa.string(), pa.int64()))}, schema=schema)) cw.commit(bw.prepare_commit()) ``` Then: ```bash clickhouse local -q "DESCRIBE paimonLocal('/tmp/pmap_wh/db.db/t')" # Code: 36. DB::Exception: Unsupported Paimon type: MAP<STRING, BIGINT>. (BAD_ARGUMENTS) clickhouse local -q "SELECT * FROM paimonLocal('/tmp/pmap_wh/db.db/t')" # same error — the table is entirely unreadable, including columns other than the MAP ``` pypaimon itself reads its own table back fine, so the files are internally consistent from the Python SDK's point of view. **Expected behavior** The table reads (`m` maps to `Map(String, Int64)` with the appropriate nullability), or at minimum the non-MAP columns stay readable. **Actual behavior** `Code: 36 Unsupported Paimon type: MAP<STRING, BIGINT>` on any access to the table, `DESCRIBE` included. **Mechanism / fix direction** In `Types.h`'s composite branch, `real_type` is compared for exact equality with `"ARRAY"` / `"MAP"`. Matching the kind as a prefix (`real_type == "MAP" || real_type.starts_with("MAP<")`, same for `ARRAY`) accepts both the Java and the pypaimon spelling; the element types should keep coming from the dedicated `key` / `value` / `element` fields as today. (Arguably pypaimon's spelling is also worth an upstream report to apache/paimon-python — but tables in that format exist in the wild either way.) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113337 --- Found by an automatic optimizer-testing framework (differential testing of optimizer settings, query plans, and equivalent rewrites).

signals.title: DeltaLake: the legacy (non-kernel) reader silently loses rows on a deletion-vector table instead of erroring
signals.text: **Describe what's wrong** With `allow_experimental_delta_kernel_rs = 0` (the legacy non-kernel DeltaLake reader, still a supported switch of a BETA-tier default), reading a Delta table that contains a deletion vector silently returns a tiny fraction of the table: 10 rows out of 310 written / 260 alive. No error, no warning — for the exact same table the kernel reader (`= 1`, the default) returns the correct 260 rows. This is worse than the reader merely not supporting deletion vectors: a DV-ignorant reader would return 310 (deleted rows resurrected). Instead, whole untouched files vanish. The table declares `minReaderVersion: 3` + `readerFeatures: ["deletionVectors"]`, which per the Delta protocol a reader without deletion-vector support must refuse to read — the legacy reader ignores the protocol action entirely and returns garbage instead of erroring. **Does it reproduce on the most recent release?** Reproduces on master 26.8.1.1448, 20/20 runs. **How to reproduce** Write a table with a deletion vector using Spark (`pip install pyspark==3.5.3 delta-spark==3.2.1`, needs a JRE) — the same table as in #114933: ```python from delta import configure_spark_with_delta_pip from pyspark.sql import SparkSession b = (SparkSession.builder.master("local[1]") .config("spark.sql.extensions", "io.delta.sql.DeltaSparkSessionExtension") .config("spark.sql.catalog.spark_catalog", "org.apache.spark.sql.delta.catalog.DeltaCatalog")) spark = configure_spark_with_delta_pip(b).getOrCreate() spark.sql("CREATE TABLE t (k BIGINT, v BIGINT) USING delta LOCATION '/tmp/dv_table' TBLPROPERTIES (delta.enableDeletionVectors = true)") spark.sql("INSERT INTO t SELECT id, id*10 FROM range(300)") spark.sql("DELETE FROM t WHERE k < 50") # persisted as a deletion vector, cardinality 50 spark.sql("INSERT INTO t SELECT id, id*10 FROM range(300, 310)") ``` The table holds 260 alive rows. Then: ```bash clickhouse local -q "SELECT count(), sum(k), min(k), max(k) FROM deltaLakeLocal('/tmp/dv_table') SETTINGS optimize_trivial_count_query = 0, allow_experimental_delta_kernel_rs = 1" # 260 46670 50 309 <- kernel reader, correct clickhouse local -q "SELECT count(), sum(k), min(k), max(k) FROM deltaLakeLocal('/tmp/dv_table') SETTINGS optimize_trivial_count_query = 0, allow_experimental_delta_kernel_rs = 0" # 10 3045 300 309 <- legacy reader: only the last append's file survives, 250 alive rows silently gone ``` **Expected behavior** Either the correct 260 rows, or — since the legacy reader does not implement deletion vectors — a hard error refusing the table: it declares `minReaderVersion: 3` with `readerFeatures: ["deletionVectors"]`, and the Delta protocol requires readers to reject tables whose reader features they do not support. **Actual behavior** 10 rows, silently. **Mechanism** `DeltaLakeMetadata::processMetadataFile` (`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/DeltaLakeMetadata.cpp`) folds the log into a `std::set<String>` of file paths: `add` inserts, `remove` erases. A deletion-vector `DELETE` commit re-adds the *same* data file path with a `deletionVector` field and also emits a `remove` for that path (Spark writes the `add` line before the `remove` line), so processing the commit in line order first re-inserts the path and then erases it — the 300-row file is dropped from the result entirely, leaving only the later append. Two layered problems: (1) the fold is order-sensitive within a commit and cancels a same-commit re-add, which is what loses the file; (2) even if the file survived, the reader has no deletion-vector handling and no `protocol`-action check, so it would resurrect the 50 DV-deleted rows (310) rather than error. A minimal fail-close fix is to parse the `protocol` action and refuse `minReaderVersion >= 3` / unsupported `readerFeatures`; that would turn every DV table into a clean error on the legacy path. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114933 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/100502 --- Found by an automatic optimizer-testing framework (differential testing of optimizer settings, query plans, and equivalent rewrites).

signals.title: DeltaLake CDF: the table-function-only guard is constructor-only — SELECT over an existing engine table serves the change stream without meta columns
signals.text: **Describe what's wrong** DeltaLake CDF is documented (by its own guard) as table-function-only: constructing a `DeltaLake*` storage while `delta_lake_snapshot_start_version` / `delta_lake_snapshot_end_version` are set throws `Code: 36 Delta lake CDF is allowed only for deltaLake table function`. But the guard lives in the `StorageObjectStorage` constructor, so it fires only when the storage object happens to be built with CDF settings in the query context (e.g. `CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE = DeltaLakeLocal(...)` inside a query that carries the settings). A plain `SELECT` with CDF settings over an *already-created* engine table bypasses it: the read path (`StorageObjectStorage::read`) happily branches into `ReadFromDeltaLakeTableChangesStep` for any data-lake configuration. The bypassed read is a third, incoherent behavior: it returns the change-stream *row multiset* — for a 1000-row table with 100 deleted rows, `count()` returns 1100, a number that corresponds to no state of the table at any version — but *without* the `_change_type` / `_commit_version` / `_commit_timestamp` meta columns (the engine's schema was fixed at CREATE), so the stream cannot even be filtered into its insert/delete parts. Referencing `_change_type` throws `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`. **Does it reproduce on the most recent release?** Reproduces on master 26.8.1.1448, 20/20 runs. **How to reproduce** Write a small CDF-enabled table with delta-rs (`pip install deltalake pyarrow`): ```python import pyarrow as pa from deltalake import DeltaTable, write_deltalake def rows(a, b): return pa.table({"k": pa.array(range(a, b), pa.int64()), "v": pa.array([7 * x for x in range(a, b)], pa.int64())}) write_deltalake("/tmp/cdf_table", rows(0, 500), mode="append", configuration={"delta.enableChangeDataFeed": "true"}) write_deltalake("/tmp/cdf_table", rows(500, 1000), mode="append") DeltaTable("/tmp/cdf_table").delete("k < 100") ``` Then, on a server: ```sql CREATE TABLE cdf_eng ENGINE = DeltaLakeLocal('/tmp/cdf_table'); -- the guard fires only if the CDF setting is in context at storage construction: CREATE TABLE cdf_eng2 ENGINE = DeltaLakeLocal('/tmp/cdf_table') SETTINGS delta_lake_snapshot_start_version = 0; -- Code: 36. DB::Exception: Delta lake CDF is allowed only for deltaLake table function. SELECT count() FROM cdf_eng; -- 900, correct SELECT count() FROM cdf_eng SETTINGS delta_lake_snapshot_start_version = 0; -- 1100 (!) — the change-stream row count, no error SELECT count(), countIf(_change_type = 'insert') FROM cdf_eng SETTINGS delta_lake_snapshot_start_version = 0; -- Code: 47 UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER `_change_type` — the meta columns don't exist on the engine's schema -- for contrast, the table function returns the actual usable stream: SELECT _change_type, count() FROM deltaLakeLocal('/tmp/cdf_table') GROUP BY _change_type ORDER BY 1 SETTINGS delta_lake_snapshot_start_version = 0; -- delete 100 -- insert 1000 ``` **Expected behavior** One of the two coherent contracts, consistently: either the engine-table SELECT with CDF settings throws the same `Code: 36` the CREATE-time guard produces (move/duplicate the check into the read path), or engine tables genuinely support CDF, including the meta columns. **Actual behavior** The guard is decorative for existing tables: the SELECT succeeds and returns change-stream row counts that match no table version, with the meta columns unreachable. **Mechanism** `src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorage.cpp`: the `is_delta_lake_cdf && !is_table_function` check runs in the constructor only; `StorageObjectStorage::read` branches into the table-changes step for any `isDataLakeConfiguration()` storage with `delta_lake_snapshot_start_version` set, with no table-function check at that point. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/100449 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104667 --- Found by an automatic optimizer-testing framework (differential testing of optimizer settings, query plans, and equivalent rewrites).

signals.title: PK-range join sharding: pruned side yields 1 port, non-sharded fallback throws
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **`SELECT ... JOIN ...` with `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges = 1` and `join_algorithm = 'full_sorting_merge'` fails with `Code: 49 ... Join is supported only for pipelines with one output port, got 3 and 1. (LOGICAL_ERROR)` whenever the primary key prunes one join side to zero parts. Pre-existing on master, not introduced by this PR - found while validating the PR's claim about the join-by-shards positional-port invariant.** - **Root cause:** The `use_sharding` fallback at [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/JoinStep.cpp:153`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/0fc2db3239a1b/src/Processors/QueryPlan/JoinStep.cpp#L153) does not do what its own comment promises ("fall back to the regular join pipeline which handles different stream counts"): the `YShaped` branch it falls back to requires exactly one port per side and neither pipeline is resized, unlike the `Paste` branch in `joinPipelinesYShaped` which calls `resize(1)` first. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `optimizeJoinByShards::apply` (Optimizations/optimizeJoinByShards.cpp:311) enables layer sharding on the join and attaches per-source layers to both reads. The pruned side never builds them: `ReadFromMergeTree::initializePipeline` returns a single `NullSource` port at ReadFromMergeTree.cpp:4758 when `result.parts_with_ranges` is empty, while the other side emits one port per layer. `JoinStep::updatePipeline` then sees mismatched stream counts, sets `use_sharding = false` (JoinStep.cpp:153) and calls `QueryPipelineBuilder::joinPipelinesYShaped`, which accepts only 1-vs-1 and throws at QueryPipelineBuilder.cpp:374. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/JoinStep.cpp:153`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/0fc2db3239a1b/src/Processors/QueryPlan/JoinStep.cpp#L153) — use_sharding falls back to the 1-port-only YShaped join without resizing - [`src/QueryPipeline/QueryPipelineBuilder.cpp:374`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/0fc2db3239a1b/src/QueryPipeline/QueryPipelineBuilder.cpp#L374) — throw site: 'Join is supported only for pipelines with one output port' - [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/ReadFromMergeTree.cpp:4758`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/0fc2db3239a1b/src/Processors/QueryPlan/ReadFromMergeTree.cpp#L4758) — pruned side emits one NullSource port instead of one port per sharded layer **Impact:** A valid query fails with a LOGICAL_ERROR (abort in debug/sanitizer builds). `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges` is off by default but is randomized on in `tests/clickhouse-test` at 30%, so any existing test that full-sorting-merge-joins two MergeTree tables where one side is pruned by the primary key can redden CI. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `0fc2db3239a1b`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/9da94266-8d1a-41af-8898-3b6ac1451724) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Test: JOIN sharded by primary-key ranges when one side is entirely pruned by the primary key. DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_04907_l; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_04907_r; CREATE TABLE t_04907_l (k UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k SETTINGS index_granularity = 128; CREATE TABLE t_04907_r (k UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k SETTINGS index_granularity = 128; INSERT INTO t_04907_l SELECT number FROM numbers(1000); INSERT INTO t_04907_r SELECT number FROM numbers(1000); -- The sharding applies only to reads in order, so pin `optimize_read_in_order` against the settings randomizer. SET query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges = 1, join_algorithm = 'full_sorting_merge', max_threads = 4, optimize_read_in_order = 1; SELECT count() FROM t_04907_l AS l JOIN (SELECT * FROM t_04907_r WHERE k > 100000) AS r ON l.k = r.k; SELECT count() FROM (SELECT * FROM t_04907_l WHERE k > 100000) AS l LEFT JOIN t_04907_r AS r ON l.k = r.k; DROP TABLE t_04907_l; DROP TABLE t_04907_r; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` 0 0 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` Code: 49. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:19010. DB::Exception: Join is supported only for pipelines with one output port, got 3 and 1. (LOGICAL_ERROR) (query: SELECT count() FROM t_04907_l AS l JOIN (SELECT * FROM t_04907_r WHERE k > 100000) AS r ON l.k = r.k;) Having 1 errors! 0 tests passed. ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> In `JoinStep::updatePipeline`'s `!use_sharding` YShaped branch, resize both pipelines to a single stream before calling `joinPipelinesYShaped` (mirroring the `Paste` handling at QueryPipelineBuilder.cpp:368-372), or keep the sharded path by making the pruned side emit one empty port per layer. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - The same divergence arises from the other early return that collapses a sharded side to one port - `ReadFromMergeTree::readByLayers` returns an empty pipe when `0 == info.sum_marks` (ReadFromMergeTree.cpp:1155), which `initializePipeline` also replaces with a single `NullSource`. Same root cause, same fix. Found during automated review of [PR #114177](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114177). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr114177_001` </details> cc @alexey-milovidov (from #114177)
