signals.title: Take referential dependencies into account in DROP DATABASE table order
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114917 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/97057 `InterpreterDropQuery::executeToDatabaseImpl` sorts the tables of a database being dropped in reverse topological order, so that a dependent is always dropped before the tables it depends on, and if the server crashes mid-drop, the remaining tables keep their dependencies intact and can be loaded on restart. Previously the ordering took only loading dependencies into account (#97057); now it takes the union of loading and referential dependencies (loading dependencies are mostly a subset of referential ones, but that is not enforced anywhere, so we merge both). This implements the TODO added in #114917, and the comment in `DatabaseCatalog::checkTableCanBeRemovedOrRenamedUnlocked` now simply documents the invariant. Like #97057, this comes without a functional test: within a single `DROP DATABASE`, dependents from the same database are deliberately ignored by the dependency check, so the drop order is not observable without crash injection in the middle of `DROP DATABASE`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `DROP DATABASE` now drops tables in reverse topological order of both loading and referential dependencies (previously only loading dependencies), so a crash in the middle of `DROP DATABASE` cannot leave a table whose dependencies were already dropped. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1488` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Fix an unkillable hang when dropping a low-sorting-name TimeSeries table
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114259 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a hang when dropping a `TimeSeries` table whose name sorts lexicographically below its inner tables' names, for example `` DROP TABLE `-ts` `` or dropping a materialized view declared with `ENGINE = TimeSeries`. The drop self-deadlocked on the DDL guard and could not be cancelled with `KILL QUERY`. ### Description `DROP TABLE` of a `TimeSeries` table never returned and could not be killed when the table's own qualified name sorted below its inner tables' names: ```sql SET allow_experimental_time_series_table = 1; CREATE TABLE `-ts` ENGINE = TimeSeries; DROP TABLE `-ts`; -- hung forever ``` A materialized view's inner name is `.inner_id.<uuid>`, which always sorts below `.inner_id.metrics.<uuid>`, so dropping an `MV ... ENGINE = TimeSeries` hung too. **Root cause.** `executeDropQuery` takes the DDL guard for the inner table, then synthesizes an `ASTDropQuery` for that same table without setting `no_ddl_lock`, so the nested interpreter takes the guard for the identical name again. `DDLGuard::table_lock` wraps a non-recursive `std::mutex`, so the thread deadlocks against itself. A mutex wait is not a cancellation point, so `KILL QUERY` could not land and the guard stayed held for the server's lifetime. `need_ddl_guard = true` comes from one call site, `StorageTimeSeries::dropInnerTableIfAny`, which requests the inner guard only when the parent name sorts first. That predicate is correct and is kept: guards must be taken in increasing name order. Only its comment was wrong, claiming the inner name is "almost always less", which holds for `MaterializedView` but not `TimeSeries`. **The change.** `executeDropQuery` now sets `no_ddl_lock = need_ddl_guard`, so the inner name is guarded exactly once, by the caller, across the nested execute. `InterpreterCreateQuery` sets the same field for the same reason. The fix is inert for the other ten call sites, which all take the `need_ddl_guard = false` default. The `ddl_guard` null check is pre-existing hardening. **Validation.** Both shapes time out before the fix and succeed after, while a high-sorting-name control passes on both builds. Eight concurrent drops serialize and complete and the name is reusable afterwards, so the guard is still taken and released. New test `04920` covers both shapes and asserts no inner table is left behind.

signals.title: Fix `rows_before_limit_at_least` under parallel replicas local plan (#113279)
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113279 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `rows_before_limit_at_least` returning 0 when querying with LIMIT under parallel replicas local plan (`parallel_replicas_local_plan = 1`). ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is not required for this bug fix --- ### Detailed Description #### Problem With parallel replicas enabled (`parallel_replicas_local_plan = 1`), queries with a `LIMIT` incorrectly returned `rows_before_limit_at_least = 0` even when `exact_rows_before_limit = 1`. #### Root Cause In `createLocalPlanForParallelReplicas` (`src/Processors/QueryPlan/ParallelReplicasLocalPlan.cpp`), `select_query_options.is_local_shard_plan` was previously only initialized to true when `processed_stage == QueryProcessingStage::WithMergeableStateAfterAggregationAndLimit`. For queries planned at `QueryProcessingStage::WithMergeableState`, `is_local_shard_plan` evaluated to false. Consequently, `addPreliminaryLimitStep` in `src/Planner/Planner.cpp` did not invoke `limit->markAsShardLimit()`, causing `initRowsBeforeLimit` in `src/QueryPipeline/QueryPipeline.cpp` to treat the preliminary limit as a top-level query accounting boundary and terminate processor traversal without attaching the rows-before-limit counter to the local input stream. #### Solution Set `select_query_options.is_local_shard_plan` to true for both `QueryProcessingStage::WithMergeableState` and `QueryProcessingStage::WithMergeableStateAfterAggregationAndLimit`. This marks the preliminary limit on the local replica branch as a shard limit, enabling `initRowsBeforeLimit` to traverse through it and attach the statistics counter to the local input stream matching remote replica behavior. #### Test Plan - Added `tests/queries/0_stateless/02590_parallel_replicas_local_plan_rows_before_limit.sh` and reference test asserting correct `rows_before_limit_at_least` row count under `parallel_replicas_local_plan = 1`.

signals.title: Apply a row policy to a read shipped as a serialized query plan
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112891 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `SELECT` row policy on a shard-local table being ignored when the read is shipped to the executing replica as a serialized query plan (`serialize_query_plan = 1`, with `process_query_plan_packet` enabled there). Reads through a `Distributed` table with `prefer_localhost_replica = 0`, and reads over parallel replicas, returned rows the policy excludes. Closes #112891. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112891 **What breaks.** With a policy `USING y < 5` on a 10-row MergeTree table, `SELECT count()` through a `Distributed` table returns 10 instead of 5 and `SELECT DISTINCT y` returns 0..9. Parallel replicas leak the same way once remote replicas get read tasks. **Root cause.** The initiator resolves the policy into `SelectQueryInfo::row_level_filter`, since a MergeTree table accepts filter push-down into the read. When the plan is built for shipping, the leaf becomes a placeholder `ReadFromTableStep`, which has no field for that filter, so it is never serialized; on the executing node `replaceReadingFromTable` rebuilds the read with a hand-built `SelectQueryInfo` that never sets it. Each side assumes the other applied the policy. **The change.** Such a read is now rebuilt through the reconstructed-query path `resolveStorages` already uses for remote and `Merge` storages. That path runs the ordinary planner, so the policy is resolved in the executing node's own access context, and the read-column widening, the `FINAL` deferral and the PREWHERE ordering come with it. No wire format change and no version bump. Reads without a policy keep the direct path. The initiator cannot make this decision: effective policies resolve per node. **Residual, pre-existing and not introduced here.** A policy existing only on the receiver is still missed where the initiator pushes no policy into the read: storages without PREWHERE support (`Memory`, `View`) and those whose PREWHERE-column contract is not `nullopt` (`Buffer`, `File`, data lakes). Those behave exactly as on master. Replanning them would double-apply the filter step the initiator already shipped, and telling the two apart needs the plan to carry whether that step was emitted. So the fix assumes the shards behind one `Distributed` table use engines with the same PREWHERE contract. **Validation.** Three stateless tests (`Distributed`, parallel replicas, column grants), all failing on master. <details> <summary>Arms run on both binaries</summary> Measured on a debug build of base `63b0a472f4b62ac2` and of this branch. | arm | base | fix | |---|---|---| | `count()` / `sum(x)` / `sum(y)` / subquery, `serialize_query_plan = 1` | 10 / 45 / 45 / 10 | 5 / 10 / 10 / 5 | | `SELECT DISTINCT y` | 0..9 | 0..4 | | parallel replicas `sum(x)` / `count()` / `max(y)` | 548895757384 / 1046417 / 1111952 | correct on all three | | explicit `PREWHERE` + policy | 8 | 3 | | policy on `LowCardinality` / `Nullable` / `Array` / `ALIAS` / `MATERIALIZED` column | 10 each | matches the non-serialized result | | always-false policy | 10 | 0 | | `FINAL`, both `apply_row_policy_after_final` values | disagrees with the non-serialized path | agrees | | policy on `Memory` (push-down refused, must keep the direct path) | 5 | 5, and a nondeterministic policy is applied exactly once | | `additional_table_filters` on the read table, nondeterministic | applied once | applied once | | `additional_table_filters` on a table only the policy's subquery reads | n/a, policy not applied at all | applied, agreeing with `serialize_query_plan = 0` | | policy on the `Distributed` table itself | `ILLEGAL_PREWHERE` | same code and outcome; the message drops its now-stale `serialize_query_plan` advice | | `max_rows_to_read = 1` | returns 10 silently | `TOO_MANY_ROWS`, matching the non-serialized path | | no policy, `serialize_query_plan` 1 and 0 | 10 / 10 | 10 / 10 | Existing row-policy and serialized-plan tests pass unchanged, including `03743_apply_row_policy_after_final_safety`, `04652_prewhere_final_move_skipped_when_deferred`, `03006_parallel_replicas_prewhere` and `03302_analyzer_distributed_filter_push_down`. The new `Distributed` test is 50/50 stable under randomized settings. </details>

signals.title: Codex tries to learn from its mistakes
signals.text: The unattended PR continuation workflow made two kinds of unsafe decisions. It incorrectly closed PR #114849 after confusing commit visibility with containment by the current `master`, and it force-pushed PR #111032 from a malformed single-parent commit that changed 673 files and deleted 26,457 lines. Require an explicit base-branch ancestry check and a separate current-state check so reverted changes are not considered integrated. Before committing or pushing, the workflow must inspect the staged and complete PR diffs, preserve the existing remote head as an ancestor, and stop on unexplained scope changes. A `pre-push` hook now enforces fast-forward-only updates and rejects branch deletion even if an agent attempts a force-push. An audit of recent automation activity found eight account-level force-pushes since 2026-08-13. PR #111032 was the only malformed large-diff outlier; the other seven replacement heads changed 2–8 files. The audit also found a smaller scope failure in PR #104495, where conflict resolution accidentally staged three unrelated untracked test files. The new explicit-path staging rule and staged-diff inspection cover that failure mode. The safety hook was tested in a throwaway repository: normal fast-forward updates were accepted, while non-fast-forward updates, branch deletion, and the exact PR #111032 rewrite were rejected. Shell syntax and ShellCheck validation also pass. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114849 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111032 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104495 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Not for changelog.

signals.title: Fix signed integer overflow reading Iceberg decimal bounds
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114929 Decoding a `Decimal` column bound from an Iceberg manifest ran in `int64_t` regardless of how wide the bound was, in `deserializeFieldFromBinaryRepr` (`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/ManifestFileIterator.cpp`). Three steps overflow: * the big-endian accumulation `unscaled_value = (unscaled_value << 8) | byte`, once the bound is more than eight bytes wide; * the sign extension `sign_extension <<= (str.size() * 8)`, which shifts by 64 or more for a bound of eight bytes or more; * the scaler loop `scaler *= 10`, which computes `10^scale` and leaves `int64_t` at scale 19. A `Decimal(38, 30)` column reaches all three: its bounds are 14 bytes wide. Bounds are parsed for every column of a manifest entry, so any query with a filter is enough and the filter does not have to touch the decimal column. A build with the undefined behaviour sanitizer aborts, as reported in the issue. Only `Decimal32` and `Decimal64` bounds are ever turned into a `Field` (everything else already returned `std::nullopt` a few lines below), and both fit into `Int64`. So the fix decodes exactly those and rejects anything wider before the arithmetic, which keeps the observable behaviour: a bound that used to be computed and then discarded is now not computed at all. Two smaller defects in the same expression are fixed along the way: * the sign extension is skipped when the value already fills all 64 bits. Previously it shifted an `int64_t` by 64, which is undefined; on the usual targets the shift count is taken modulo 64, so `-1` was left unchanged and OR-ing it in turned every eight-byte negative bound into `-1`. That is a wrong bound, not just undefined behaviour, and a wrong bound prunes files that do contain matching rows. * the widening `unscaled_value += scaler` and the narrowing to `Int32` are range checked. The bound comes from the manifest and is not validated against the declared precision, so a malformed manifest could otherwise wrap it into a bogus bound. ### Testing `tests/queries/0_stateless/04907_iceberg_decimal_bounds_overflow.sh` reads a `Decimal(38, 30)` Iceberg table with a filter. The table is the one attached to the issue, produced by Spark, repacked without the Spark checksum files and embedded as base64: ClickHouse cannot write a decimal column to Iceberg (`Unsupported type for iceberg Decimal(38, 30)`), so the test cannot build it itself. Because the overflowed bound was discarded anyway, the query results are the same before and after this change; the test fails before the fix only under the undefined behaviour sanitizer, and pins the results everywhere else. I verified the reproducer and the resulting query output against the official master build `26.8.1.1463`; I have not built this branch locally, so the compile and the sanitizer runs are left to CI. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes reading Iceberg tables whose manifests carry `Decimal` column bounds that do not fit into 64 bits, such as those of a `Decimal(38, 30)` column. Such a bound is now ignored instead of being decoded into a meaningless value, and a negative bound stored in eight bytes is no longer read as `-1`, which could skip files that do contain matching rows.

signals.title: Mask credentials of the Azure data lake table engines
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114939 `IcebergAzure`, `DeltaLakeAzure` and `PaimonAzure` appear in neither branch of the table engine dispatch in `FunctionSecretArgumentsFinder::findTableEngineSecretArguments` (`src/Parsers/FunctionSecretArgumentsFinder.cpp`): the S3 branch lists the S3 family lake engines (`DeltaLake`, `DeltaLakeS3`, `Hudi`, `Iceberg`, `IcebergS3`, `Paimon`, `PaimonS3`, `S3Queue`) and the Azure branch lists `AzureBlobStorage` and `AzureQueue`. With no branch matching, none of the three engines has any argument marked secret, so the storage account key stays verbatim in `SHOW CREATE TABLE`, in `system.tables.engine_full` and in the logged query text, at the default `format_display_secrets_in_show_and_select = 0` and without the `displaySecretsInShowAndSelect` privilege. Both spellings leak: the `AccountKey=` inside a connection string and the positional `account_key` of the five argument form. The three engines take the same leading arguments as `AzureBlobStorage`, and `findAzureBlobStorageTableEngineSecretArguments` already handles both spellings, so this routes them to it. The Azure *table functions* (`icebergAzure`, `deltaLakeAzure`, `paimonAzure` and their `*Cluster` variants) were already dispatched there, which is why a `CREATE VIEW ... AS SELECT * FROM icebergAzure(...)` masked while the engine did not. As the issue notes, this is not a regression: `git log -S "IcebergAzure"` over the secret finder's history is empty, so the engines were never masked. `findBackupNameSecretArguments`, the other dispatch in the same file, is left alone: it resolves a `BACKUP ... TO` destination, and the lake engines are not backup destinations. ### Testing `tests/queries/0_stateless/04908_azure_lake_engines_secret_mask.sh` covers all three engines and both argument spellings against an unreachable endpoint, so no Azure endpoint or emulator is needed: * `DeltaLakeAzure` defers reading the table when the columns are given, so its `CREATE` succeeds and `SHOW CREATE TABLE` and `system.tables.engine_full` are asserted directly. * `IcebergAzure` and `PaimonAzure` read their metadata while the table is created, so theirs fail against that endpoint. The masking happens when the query is formatted for the log, before the failure, so for those two the assertion is that the logged query text carries no key. Against the official master build `26.8.1.1463` the test prints the raw account key in all four `SHOW CREATE` and `engine_full` rows and reports 4 logged queries containing it; the committed reference is the masked output with 0. I have not built this branch locally, so the compile and the test run are left to CI. The Azure part of `tests/integration/test_mask_sensitive_info/test.py` is untouched: it runs against Azurite, and these three engines need a real table to exist there, which the unreachable-endpoint approach above avoids. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The `IcebergAzure`, `DeltaLakeAzure` and `PaimonAzure` table engines now hide the Azure storage account key in `SHOW CREATE TABLE` and in `system.tables.engine_full`, as the `AzureBlobStorage` engine already did. Previously any user allowed to run `SHOW CREATE TABLE` or read `system.tables` could see the key of such a table.

signals.title: Mask the Azure shared access signature carried in a url argument
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114946 A storage account url is a documented, working way to authenticate: when the url contains a `?`, `processURL` (`src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/ObjectStorages/AzureBlobStorage/AzureBlobStorageCommon.cpp`) takes everything after it as `sas_auth`, and `tests/integration/test_storage_azure_blob_storage/test.py::test_sas_token` exercises exactly that form. `maskAzureConnectionString` (`src/Parsers/FunctionSecretArgumentsFinder.cpp`) skips any argument starting with `http`, so the token stayed verbatim in `SHOW CREATE TABLE`, in `system.tables.engine_full` and in `system.query_log.query` at the default `format_display_secrets_in_show_and_select = 0`. The same credential spelled as a connection string (`...;SharedAccessSignature=...`) was hidden, and the positional `account_key` was hidden, so the url spelling was the one gap. A shared access signature is a bearer credential: whoever holds it gets the access it was issued for until it expires. This masks the `sig` parameter, the HMAC over the signed fields and the only part of the token that cannot be guessed. The remaining parameters (`sv`, `sp`, `se`, `sr`, ...) grant nothing without it and stay visible, which keeps the url diagnosable, the same way `maskPresignedURLParameters` keeps a presigned S3 url readable. The new `maskAzureSASSignature` sits next to it in `src/Common/maskURIPassword.h` and is written the same way. The url argument is replaced in place (`result.replaced_arguments`) rather than hidden whole, and the function keeps returning `false`, so a positional `account_key` in the same call is still masked by the caller. That is the mechanism the S3 url masking already uses, and it composes with the other masking. All the call sites of `maskAzureConnectionString` are covered by the one change: the `AzureBlobStorage` and `AzureQueue` engines, and the `azureBlobStorage` table function with its `*Cluster` and named collection forms. If masking the whole query string is preferred over masking only `sig`, that is a one line change here; I went with the narrower one because the other parameters are not secret and are useful in a log. ### Testing `tests/queries/0_stateless/04909_azure_sas_url_secret_mask.sql` covers the engine through `SHOW CREATE TABLE` and `system.tables.engine_full`, and the table function and its cluster variant through `EXPLAIN QUERY TREE run_passes = 0`, which leaves them unresolved so nothing is read. A url with no signature in it is asserted to be left alone. The `CREATE` needs no reachable endpoint: with a shared access signature the engine skips the container probe. Against the official master build `26.8.1.1463` every one of those surfaces prints the signature verbatim; the committed reference is the same output with `sig=[HIDDEN]`. I also compiled `maskAzureSASSignature` standalone and checked it over multiple occurrences, a fragment, an empty value, a missing `=`, and the near-miss names `signature`, `xsig` and `SIG`. I have not built this branch, so the compile and the test run are left to CI. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): When an Azure shared access signature is passed inside the url of the `AzureBlobStorage` engine or the `azureBlobStorage` table function, its `sig` value is now hidden in `SHOW CREATE TABLE`, `system.tables.engine_full` and `system.query_log`. Previously the whole token was stored and displayed in plain text, even though the equivalent connection string spelling was already hidden. The rest of the signature stays visible so the url is still readable in a log.

signals.title: Avoid merge conflicts in the append-only lists of events, metrics and failpoints
signals.text: Two pull requests that each add a `ProfileEvents`, `CurrentMetrics` or `FailPoint` entry almost always add it at the same place - the end of the list - and Git reports that as a conflict, even though keeping both entries is always the right resolution. GitHub then marks the pull request as conflicting and it has to be resolved by hand. Marking the file `merge=union` in `.gitattributes` makes Git keep both sides instead, which is exactly the wanted resolution. This is already done for `src/Core/SettingsChangesHistory.cpp`. A union merge resolves *every* overlapping region by keeping both sides, so it is only safe for a file that contains nothing but such a list. Each list is therefore moved into its own `.inc` file, and only those files are marked, so a union merge can never silently duplicate or interleave ordinary code: - `src/Common/ProfileEventsList.inc` - `src/Common/CurrentMetricsList.inc` - `src/Common/FailPointsList.inc` The other idea considered was padding the entries apart with blank or backslash lines. That does not help: Git reports a conflict whenever both sides insert different text at the same point, however much unchanged context surrounds it, and insertions a line or two apart already merge cleanly today. This is written down in a comment in each list so it does not get retried. The last entry of `APPLY_FOR_FAILPOINTS` had no trailing backslash, so adding an entry edited that line instead of inserting after it - under a union merge that would duplicate the line and truncate the macro. All three lists now end the same way, with every entry a self-contained line, so appending is always a pure insertion. `src/Common/ErrorCodes.cpp` is deliberately left alone, and `.gitattributes` says why: an error code is a value in the public protocol, and a union merge there would silently keep two entries with the same number. The change is a pure text move, verified as such: - the preprocessed expansion of each list is byte-identical before and after, warning-clean under `-Wall -Wextra -Werror` (the failpoints are checked with four distinct category macros, so a miscategorised entry would show up); - all three translation units compile with production flags with no new warnings, and their symbol tables are unchanged (1703 / 544 / 470 symbols); - `ci/jobs/scripts/check_style/check_cpp.sh` reports nothing; - two branches that each append an entry to all three lists now merge cleanly, keeping both entries, and the merged lists still preprocess with no duplicates. The same scenario on `master` today conflicts. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required)

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/87206 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103537 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112457 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `BAD_DATA_PART_NAME` ("Trying to get part name in new format for old format version") on a `ReplicatedMergeTree` created with the deprecated positional syntax under `allow_deprecated_syntax_for_merge_tree`. A mutation could be reported as done on a replica that had not applied it, and the table could stay readonly after a restart. ### Description Reported by @ alexey-milovidov on #112457 ([`Upgrade check (amd_release)` report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112457&sha=f888781eb610bfabdc8c8675d835b99482bec8a2&name_0=PR&name_1=Upgrade%20check%20%28amd_release%29)). No related open issue found. A table created with `ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree(date, key, granularity)` uses date-based (V0) part names. `MergeTreePartInfo::getPartNameAndCheckFormat` cannot produce one, because the min/max dates it needs are not part of a `MergeTreePartInfo`, so it throws. Two `ActiveDataPartSet` entry points take only an info and regenerate the name that way; each had exactly one caller, and both callers already held the name and threw it away. This change passes the name at both call sites, as in `536b611c96a757e`, which fixed the `ATTACH PARTITION` instance of this bug. V0 name formatting is untouched, and current-format tables are unaffected because the name-taking overload re-parses to the same info and runs the same insertion code. The linked report contains both failures: - `ReplicatedMergeTreeQueue::getPartNamesToMutate` builds `mutation.parts_to_do`. The throw left it empty, so a mutation reported `is_done` on a replica that never mutated its part, and `mutations_sync = 2` returned success while that replica still served pre-mutation values. Regressed by #87206, which changed `produced_parts` to hold infos instead of names. - `StorageReplicatedMergeTree::checkPartsImpl` builds the set of empty unexpected parts. The throw aborted `ReplicatedMergeTreeAttachThread`, leaving the table readonly. Regressed by my own #103537, which replaced a name-based call with an info-based one. The V0 gap in `MergeTreeData::restorePartFromBackup` that the throw-site comment describes is a different code path, absent from both stacks, and is not addressed. A new stateless test asserts `parts_to_do` on the frozen replica: it fails on master (`parts to do 0`) and passes here (`parts to do 2`), and 50/50 randomized runs pass. `checkPartsImpl`'s state needs parts fabricated on disk, so that half is covered by three V0 cases added to `gtest_active_data_part_set.cpp`, all of which fail with this change reverted. `00062_replicated_merge_tree_alter_zookeeper_long` and `00652_replicated_mutations_zookeeper` still pass.

signals.title: Do not drop the whole GROUP BY when unwrapping injective functions of constants
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104863 (same logical error, closed earlier without this cause identified) ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix wrong results for a `GROUP BY` whose only key is an injective function of constants, for example `SELECT 1 FROM t GROUP BY materialize(NULL)`. Such a key was removed by `optimize_injective_functions_in_group_by`, which left the query with no `GROUP BY` and no aggregation at all, so it returned one row per input row instead of one row per group. Over a `Merge` table that mixes a local and a remote child the same cause also raised the logical error `Chunk info was not set for chunk in GroupingAggregatedTransform`. ### Description `unwrapInjectiveFunctionsInKeys` unwraps an injective function to its arguments and skips constant arguments, so a key that is an injective function *of a constant* unwraps to nothing and is dropped. `OptimizeGroupByInjectiveFunctionsPass` assigned that result unconditionally: when such a key was the only one and the query had no aggregate function, `GROUP BY` became empty and the query stopped aggregating. Under a `Merge` table mixing a child that aggregates with one that does not, the un-aggregated child's raw chunks reach a merge transform that requires aggregate state; both wordings of the message occur, `GroupingAggregatedTransform` and `MergingAggregatedTransform`, depending on `distributed_aggregation_memory_efficient`, and one fix closes both. Found by the fuzzers, e.g. [AST fuzzer (amd_debug)](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=94148&sha=8eb1df1331f7fd5dcf93b4b0e975e56685b6f732&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29). The fix assigns the unwrapped list only when it is non-empty, which is what `OptimizeLimitByInjectiveFunctionsPass` already does for `LIMIT BY` and what the non-analyzer `TreeOptimizer::optimizeGroupBy` does via `appendUnusedGroupByColumn`. Of those three sibling paths only the analyzer's `GROUP BY` pass lacked the guard. The shared helper is unchanged, so `LIMIT BY` is unaffected. A per-key variant was deliberately not used: it would weaken the optimization when another key survives, and it is the branch added in 462445c2c201a5f and removed the next day in 355909eb3a415b7. `GROUP BY materialize(NULL), k` still groups by `k` alone. Affected queries now return a different row count, which is the point of the fix. Across 25 shapes the patched default is byte-identical to running with `optimize_injective_functions_in_group_by = 0`, where before it diverged on 7 of them; `enable_analyzer = 0` and a plain `GROUP BY NULL` key agree. The old behaviour stays reachable with that setting. The new test fails on master and passes here.

signals.title: Optimize aggregations of LowCardinality of 128 and 256 bit integers
signals.text: This is simply expanding what is done for narrower integers to wider ones. Comparing `column_low_cardinality_key_holder` to the previous commit: | Key type | Encoding | Before CPU time | After CPU time | Reduction | Speedup | |-----------|----------|----------------:|---------------:|----------:|--------:| | `UInt8` | Plain | 320,240 ns | 321,169 ns | -0.3% | 1.00x | | `UInt8` | LC | 1,366,296 ns | 1,369,728 ns | -0.3% | 1.00x | | `UInt16` | Plain | 320,863 ns | 322,198 ns | -0.4% | 1.00x | | `UInt16` | LC | 1,391,415 ns | 1,377,083 ns | 1.0% | 1.01x | | `UInt32` | Plain | 320,757 ns | 321,323 ns | -0.2% | 1.00x | | `UInt32` | LC | 1,388,380 ns | 1,385,711 ns | 0.2% | 1.00x | | `UInt64` | Plain | 326,842 ns | 325,383 ns | 0.4% | 1.00x | | `UInt64` | LC | 1,381,219 ns | 1,440,143 ns | -4.3% | 0.96x | | `UInt128` | Plain | 1,012,926 ns | 911,887 ns | 10.0% | 1.11x | | `UInt128` | LC | 8,019,216 ns | 1,452,770 ns | 81.9% | 5.52x | | `UInt256` | Plain | 8,149,345 ns | 8,132,693 ns | 0.2% | 1.00x | | `UInt256` | LC | 11,576,753 ns | 1,498,433 ns | 87.1% | 7.73x | For end-to-end benchmark in `group_by_integer_key_width.xml`: | Grouping key | Before median | After median | Reduction | Speedup | |-------------------------------|--------------:|-------------:|----------:|--------:| | `LowCardinality(UInt64)` | 2.0680 s | 2.1344 s | -3.2% | 0.97x | | `UInt64` | 0.6938 s | 0.6905 s | 0.5% | 1.00x | | `LowCardinality(UInt128)` | 2.8588 s | 2.5819 s | 9.7% | 1.11x | | `UInt128` | 1.0269 s | 1.0140 s | 1.3% | 1.01x | | `LowCardinality(UInt256)` | 3.3996 s | 2.9630 s | 12.8% | 1.15x | | `UInt256` | 1.7643 s | 1.6781 s | 4.9% | 1.05x | There's ~5% noise level if you look at the unaffected paths. There's now also a test to ensure that the right aggregation is used. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Optimize aggregations of LowCardinality of 128 and 256 bit integers.

signals.title: Report the real error when an in-place `IN`-set build destroys its source
signals.text: `FutureSetFromSubquery::buildOrderedSetInplace` speculatively builds the set of an `IN` subquery during index analysis. A subquery whose source plan cannot be cloned - a read from a remote cluster, for example - takes the destructive path there, which consumes the source plan. When that build then throws, the set can never be built again: `build` returns a null plan, every caller takes that for "nothing left to build", and the query keeps running with an unready set until `FunctionIn` reports the logical error `Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in'`. That is exactly what happens whenever a caller deliberately ignores an in-place build failure. Statistics-based part pruning is such a caller: it logs the failure and keeps reading the part whose condition it could not evaluate. So ```sql SELECT count() FROM t WHERE a IN (SELECT a FROM clusterAllReplicas('cluster_with_an_unavailable_replica', currentDatabase(), t)) ``` reported `Not-ready Set` instead of the connection error, which aborts the server in a build with `abort_on_logical_error`. The failure of a destructive in-place build is remembered now and rethrown from `build` instead of returning a null plan, so the query fails with the real reason - the same error it fails with when no in-place build is attempted at all. This is the cause of the recurring master `Stress test` failure `Logical error: Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'A (STID: 0250-3e49)`, seen on `arm_release` and `arm_msan` a few times a day since 2026-07-23: CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=2926be24e6102daae60b8f44c88969495a76ec3c&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_release%29 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107924 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107619 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix the logical error `Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in'` for a query with an `IN` subquery reading from a remote cluster: the query now fails with the actual error from the subquery, such as a connection failure.

signals.title: Fix logical error for IN with an identical non-constant tuple on both sides in the old analyzer
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer, `AST fuzzer (arm_asan_ubsan)`, STID 2508-3457: ```sql EXPLAIN PIPELINE graph = 0, graph = 0, compact = 1 SELECT 'null', (SELECT tuple(materialize(NULL), NULL) GLOBAL IN (materialize(NULL), NULL)) GROUP BY ALL SETTINGS transform_null_in = 1 ``` Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111552&sha=38215c1758332de1ea8a4b5a620ba8364586f6c6&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%29 It reaches the old interpreter through a scalar subquery, and reduces to `SELECT (materialize(1), 2) IN (materialize(1), 2) SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 0`. Release builds catch the exception but still reject the query with an empty identifier name: `Code: 47 ... Unknown identifier: ; there are columns: dummy, 1, materialize(1), 2, ...`. Root cause: a literal's `unique_column_name` is assigned lazily, only when `ActionsMatcher::visit(const ASTLiteral &)` runs, and `getNameAndTypeFromAST` requires it. The old interpreter's row-wise `IN` rewrite visits the left argument first, and here the right-hand `tuple` renders to the same column name as the left one, so `visit(right_argument, data)` takes the common-subexpression early return and never descends into the right-hand children. The loop that follows then asks for the name and type of each raw child, and a literal child is still unnamed. The fix visits each child before naming it. That call site was the only one of the eight `getNameAndTypeFromAST` callers in the file not already preceded by a `visit()` of the node it names. `visit` is idempotent, so the added call is a no-op when the child is already indexed. The abort is gone after the change, with the result now matching `enable_analyzer = 1` on 20 shapes (including `NULL` with `transform_null_in`, `nullIn`, `GLOBAL IN`, `LowCardinality`, array and tuple literal children, `indexHint`, and the query above). 13 shapes that already worked are unchanged, with byte-identical `EXPLAIN actions = 1` output. Removing the added line reinstates the abort. Introduced by #104993 and present only on master, so no backport is needed. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104993

signals.title: Label "submodule changed" only when a submodule actually changed
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) The `submodule changed` label is applied by matching the `contrib/` path prefix: ```python if "contrib/" in " ".join(changed_files): pr_labels_to_add.append(Labels.SUBMODULE_CHANGED) ``` Most of `contrib/` is not submodules. The `contrib/<lib>-cmake/` directories are ClickHouse's own build glue, `contrib/CMakeLists.txt` is ours, and some directories under `contrib/` are ordinary in-repo trees — `contrib/antlr4-grammars` and `contrib/antlr4-grammars-cmake` are not registered in `.gitmodules` at all. Editing any of them gets a PR labelled as changing a submodule although no gitlink moved. **Of the 77 open PRs currently carrying the label, 33 contain no submodule change at all.** I measured this by taking each PR's diff and looking for `Subproject commit` lines, which is what a gitlink change always renders as — that catches bumps, additions and removals without depending on any `.gitmodules` baseline. Representative cases: | PR | `contrib/` files touched | gitlink changed | | --- | --- | --- | | #63057 | `contrib/arrow-cmake/CMakeLists.txt` | no | | #88857 | `contrib/jwt-cpp-cmake/CMakeLists.txt` | no | | #78494 | `contrib/datasketches-cpp-cmake/CMakeLists.txt` | no | | #80177 | `contrib/CMakeLists.txt`, `contrib/aws-sdk-cpp-*/CMakeLists.txt` | no | | #107200 | `contrib/datasketches-cpp-cmake/include_patched/…` | no | | #113173, #112861, #114558 | `contrib/antlr4-grammars…/PromQLLexer.{g4,cpp,interp}` | no | This decides the label from the submodule lifecycle instead, using only the data the hook already has — the PR's changed-file list and the checkout's `.gitmodules`: - a **bump** leaves `.gitmodules` untouched, but the submodule path is in the changed-file list and is still registered, so the path intersection catches it; - **adding**, **removing** and **renaming** a submodule all edit `.gitmodules` itself, so that file appearing in the changed-file list is the signal. Both conditions are needed. A removal is invisible to the path intersection, because the removed path is no longer registered at the head — and a removal that forgets to clean up `.gitmodules` leaves the entry in place, where the intersection catches it. `ci/tests/test_pr_labels_submodule_changed.py` pins the whole lifecycle. Against those cases: | implementation | wrong | | --- | --- | | `contrib/` substring match | 3 of 11 — the `-cmake` glue and grammar false positives | | head `.gitmodules` paths only | 1 of 11 — the removal | | this PR | 0 of 11 | One thing this PR deliberately does not change: the label is only ever added, never removed, so a PR that once touched `contrib/` keeps it afterwards. That accounts for 9 of the 33 above, which touch no `contrib/` file at all today. Worth knowing when checking this fix against an existing PR — the stale label will not clear by itself. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01XvXEBdaJTCCnUdunCf8icr

signals.title: Reuse LowCardinality aggregation mappings across blocks
signals.text: Previously dictionary position to aggregate state mappings were only valid within a block. For parts where there's only a single dictionary, this is too restrictive and resulted in repeated work. This moves the mapping cache to the aggregation method, matching its lifetime to the aggregation hash table. We keep the successful mappings while the dict remains unchanged. Non-shared dictionaries remain block local. This gives a very nice speedup to the benchmark in the previous commit: | Width | LC before | LC after | Change | |-----------------|----------:|----------:|-------:| | `UInt8` | 0.1220 s | 0.1419 s | +16.3% | | `UInt16` | 0.1703 s | 0.1349 s | -20.8% | | `UInt32` | 0.1884 s | 0.1529 s | -18.8% | | `UInt64` | 0.1952 s | 0.1534 s | -21.4% | | `UInt128` | 0.5676 s | 0.5645 s | -0.5% | | `UInt256` | 0.9354 s | 0.9105 s | -2.7% | | `String` (6 B) | 0.2535 s | 0.1616 s | -36.3% | | `String` (26 B) | 0.2521 s | 0.1635 s | -35.1% | | `String` (56 B) | 0.2689 s | 0.1655 s | -38.4% | The improvements for UInt128 and UInt256 will be there after #114982 is merged. The benefit is largest when many blocks share the same dictionary, because dictionary-position mappings are reused across those blocks. _AI assisted, scratching an itch I've had for a while._ ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Improve aggregation performance by reusing LowCardinality aggregation mappings across blocks.

signals.title: Fix data race and silent data loss on the object-storage path list
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/90967 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed silent data loss when several `INSERT`s run concurrently into one non-partitioned `s3`, `azure` or `hdfs` table with `s3_create_new_file_on_insert = 1` or its per-storage equivalent, once the base object exists: the writers could derive the same new file name and overwrite each other's rows with no error. Also fixed the data race on the shared path list caused by the same sequence. ### Description Found by `La Casa Del Dolor (amd_tsan)`, STID `3437-4fb8`, on an unrelated PR: [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=94148&sha=8eb1df1331f7fd5dcf93b4b0e975e56685b6f732&name_0=PR&name_1=La%20Casa%20Del%20Dolor%20%28amd_tsan%29), [log](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/PRs/94148/8eb1df1331f7fd5dcf93b4b0e975e56685b6f732/la_casa_del_dolor_amd_tsan/stderr0.log) `StorageObjectStorage::write()` read the configuration's path list, derived the next file name from it and published the result, unsynchronized. The configuration is created once per table and shared by every query, so two INSERT pipelines ran that sequence on one vector, which ThreadSanitizer reported in `std::vector::operator=`. The race is only the visible half. The new name is `<base>.<N>`, N from the length of the list the caller was handed, so the list is the name allocator: two concurrent INSERTs derive the same name, find it free, and open it with `WriteMode::Rewrite`, so one writer's rows silently replace the other's. With eight writers, two of nine rows survived. Fix: the concurrency moves into the class owning the state. `getPaths`/`setPaths` become non-virtual base methods taking a shared mutex and delegating to protected `*Impl` virtuals, so all five subclasses and the twelve `DataLakeConfiguration` instantiations inherit it, and `getPaths()` returns by value, since a reference into mutex-protected state protects nothing. Allocate-derive-publish becomes `allocatePathForWrite()` under a second, writer-only mutex, keeping the existence probes off the list's lock so a slow remote request cannot stall `SELECT`s. Three cases are left, so they are not mistaken for fixed: with no base object yet, nothing is reserved and both writers use the base path; wildcard-partitioned writes derive their name in the sink, so writers into one partition can still collide; and two `INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3(...)` queries build a configuration each, so there is no shared list. All three need an in-flight reservation, not a lock, as creating a sink creates no object to probe for. The new tests fail on master and pass 50/50 with the fix.
signals.author: groeneai

signals.title: Fix PromQL offset inside range selectors
signals.text: Any PromQL query using `offset` inside a range selector, e.g. `rate(m[2m] offset 5m)`, failed with: ``` Code: 43. DB::Exception: Illegal type Decimal(18, 0) of argument of function toIntervalNanosecond: In scope prometheus_query_step_2. (ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT) ``` Instant-vector `offset` (e.g. `m offset 5m`) worked, because it takes the grid branch of `applyOffset` which only shifts the evaluation range. The `StoreMethod::RAW_DATA` branch, which rewrites `timestamp + INTERVAL x` in the generated SQL, had two defects: 1. The scale clamp used `std::max` instead of `std::min`, so the rounded-up scale was always 9 and the generated function was always `toIntervalNanosecond`, regardless of the timestamp scale. 2. The offset was emitted as a `Decimal64` literal, which the `toInterval*` functions do not accept (and which loses its scale, hence `Decimal(18, 0)` in the message) — so the path failed unconditionally for any `DateTime64` timestamp column, including the default `DateTime64(3)`. The fix emits the exact integer number of interval units (exact because the interval unit scale is rounded up from the timestamp scale). The new test covers `rate`/`increase`/`last_over_time` with `offset` in instant and range evaluation, asserts that `offset` is equivalent to shifting the evaluation time, and exercises the `toIntervalNanosecond` branch with `DateTime64(9)` timestamps and a sub-second offset. Found via a PromQL equivalence harness while benchmarking the TimeSeries engine. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix the error `Illegal type Decimal(18, 0) of argument of function toIntervalNanosecond` when a PromQL query uses `offset` inside a range selector, e.g. `rate(m[2m] offset 5m)`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1516` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Schedule text-index virtual columns first in the PREWHERE cost model
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110695 The `cost_with_selectivity` score from #110695 orders PREWHERE conditions by bytes-per-rejected-row, but conditions with `columns_size == 0` fall back to a score of `estimated_row_count` — a plain row count. The two units are not comparable. `__text_index_*` virtual columns are not physical columns, so they always score through the fallback (millions) and lose to any byte-based score of a physical predicate (hundreds). The expensive raw predicate then runs first, on all rows, reading the whole `text` column; the near-free index check runs last, where it filters nothing. Our internal full-text-search benchmark (59M rows of StackOverflow data, multi-KB `text` column with a `text` index) caught this the day after #110695 merged, on 14 query shapes: an equality residual (`hasToken(...) AND text = concat(...)`) went from 89 ms to 3.45 s on every execution (~39x), `match` residuals slowed 2–2.4x, `multiMatchAny`/`multiSearchAny` by 30–40%. The fix is deliberately narrow. Conditions that read only text-index virtual columns get cost 0: their posting lists are read for granule pruning anyway, so their marginal evaluation cost is a bitmap lookup per row, with no column I/O. Every other zero-size case (compact parts, table virtual columns like `_part`, columns not yet materialized after `ALTER`, subcolumns without size info) keeps the existing pessimistic selectivity fallback, because their evaluation cost is unknown and they must not be scheduled first. Standalone reproduction (wide part required — on compact parts all sizes are 0, every condition ties, and the bug hides): ```sql CREATE TABLE t (id UInt64, v UInt64, text String, INDEX idx_text text TYPE text(tokenizer = 'splitByNonAlpha')) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id SETTINGS min_bytes_for_wide_part = 0, min_rows_for_wide_part = 0; -- insert rows where the token filter is index-answerable and the residual is per-row -- then run with send_logs_level='test': SELECT count() FROM t WHERE hasToken(text, 'alpha') AND text = concat('x', toString(id)); ``` The `Condition ... moved to PREWHERE` log lines print in scheduling order. Before this fix: `equals(text, ...)` (columns_size 293748504, score ≈ 877) is scheduled before `__text_index_*` (columns_size 0, score = 165000). After: the virtual column comes first. Note `EXPLAIN` cannot show this — the printed argument order of the `AND` is the reverse of the evaluation order — hence the new test asserts on `read_bytes` instead: with the correct order the equality never reads `text`, because the token conditions reject every row first. After the fix, the internal benchmark returned to its pre-#110695 numbers (0 regressions), and one query improved 11.6x beyond its old baseline (a per-row `LIKE concat(...)` residual that had been misordered by an earlier heuristic as well). cc @avogar ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: Fix reading a tuple element through a positional Tuple structure hint
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114991 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114991 Reading a tuple element through a positional structure hint returned default values instead of the file's data. Over a Parquet file written as `t Tuple(x UInt64, y String)`: ```sql SELECT tupleElement(t, 1) FROM file('p.parquet', Parquet, 't Tuple(UInt64, String)'); -- returned 0, 0, 0 instead of 0, 1, 2 ``` `WHERE tupleElement(t, 1) = 1` matched no rows, and with `input_format_parquet_allow_missing_columns = 0` the query failed with `THERE_IS_NO_COLUMN`. Silent wrong results, on default settings. Root cause: an unnamed tuple names its elements `1`, `2`, ..., so `optimize_functions_to_subcolumns` rewrote `tupleElement(t, 1)` to the subcolumn `t.1`. The existing guards there consult the storage snapshot, which is built from the structure argument and does contain `t.1`. The Parquet reader then resolves a flattened element name by string against the file's real field names `t.x`, `t.y`, found no match, and substituted a missing column filled with defaults. The fix suppresses the rewrite when the element name is a bare ordinal and the source resolves subcolumn names against a file schema. Named hints keep their pushdown, and storages serving subcolumns from their own metadata (MergeTree and friends) are unaffected. This regressed in #113383 and is master-only: that merge is an ancestor of no release branch and is in no release tag, hence `Not for changelog`. That category also skips `Bugfix validation`, so the reddening check below is the evidence. Validated on a Debug build, with a regression arm added to `04706_tuple_subcolumn_pushdown_parquet`: - Reddening: removing only the new guard term makes the new arm fail while the pre-existing arms stay green. - Preservation: `t.x` pushdown survives for a named hint by name and by ordinal, and `t.1` still pushes down for MergeTree's unnamed tuple. - `04706`, `04707`, `04708`, `04873` pass; a `subcolumn`/`tuple_element`/`functions_to_subcolumns` sweep has no failure absent from an unmodified-master control; 50 randomized runs pass.

signals.title: Support `Merge` tables with plan-based parallel replicas
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/67770 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110972 Lets a `Merge` table be read with parallel replicas, implemented on top of the plan-based parallel replicas (`parallel_replicas_plan_based`). `ReadFromMerge` is opaque to the parallel-replicas plan transformation: it unites the pipelines of its per-table subplans instead of their plans, so the underlying `MergeTree` reads do not exist yet while the plan is transformed. An eligible `ReadFromMerge` is therefore expanded into a plan-level `UnionStep` over those child reads, right before the reads to distribute are collected. A `Merge` then has exactly the shape the transformation already distributes - a union of `MergeTree` reads - so the reads are coordinated across the replicas, and the steps above the `Merge` (aggregation, joins) are distributed as well, without any `Merge`-specific code in the coordinator, in the serialization or in the local plan. The expansion is off by default, gated by the new setting `parallel_replicas_allow_merge_tables`, and takes effect only together with `parallel_replicas_plan_based`. A `Merge` is read by a single replica when one of its children is not a plain `MergeTree` read, when the read is `FINAL`, or when no table matches its regexp. This is an alternative to https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110972, which implements the same feature on the legacy (query-tree-based) path. There, the query text is reshipped and every replica re-analyzes it, which needs a fail-close handshake (`parallel_replicas_designated_table`, `_freshness_checked_tables`, `_merge_child_tables`) to guard against the set of underlying tables differing across replicas or changing between planning and reading. The plan-based path ships a serialized plan fragment with the tables already resolved, so none of that is needed. Tests: three new stateless tests - the core feature and its negative cases (`04907`), the query shapes a `Merge` can be read with, including the `merge` table function, a filter on the `_table` virtual column and reading in order with a limit (`04908`), and `Merge` tables inside JOINs on either side of the join (`04909`). Each of them checks the results against non-parallel execution and asserts through the plan how the query was distributed. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A `Merge` table can now be read with parallel replicas: the reads from the underlying `MergeTree` tables are coordinated across the replicas, and the aggregations and joins above them are distributed too. Enabled by the new setting `parallel_replicas_allow_merge_tables`, which takes effect together with `parallel_replicas_plan_based`.

signals.title: Perf: Skip ASCII scan for byte-mode pad functions
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/commit/a4466496488 ### Description - **Problem:** regular `leftPad` and `rightPad` already run in byte mode, but can still scan the full `chars` buffer with `isAllASCII`. - **Why the scan exists:** UTF-8 variants use it to take the byte path when the input and pad string are ASCII; non-ASCII input needs UTF-8 character counting. - **Why regular functions paid for it:** the setup is shared across all variants, so they inherited the check even though `is_utf8` is `false`. - **Why it is redundant:** `is_utf8` is already `false` for these functions, so the scan result cannot select the UTF-8 path. - **Change:** short-circuit the existing condition on `is_utf8`. - **UTF-8 behavior:** unchanged. `leftPadUTF8` and `rightPadUTF8` still use the ASCII check. - **Padding loop:** unchanged. The same byte or UTF-8 implementation is selected after the check. - **Where it runs:** once in `executeForSource` before the padding loop, so the wasted work grows with the input block size. ### Benchmark - **Machine:** macOS arm64 - **Compiler:** `clang++ -O3` - **Implementation:** real ClickHouse `isAllASCII` implementation - **Input:** 64 MiB ASCII payload - **Scope:** mode-selection preamble plus a fixed output copy - **Method:** median of 11 samples, 3 repetitions, 3 process runs - **Byte mode:** `8.26 to 9.41 ms` before, `4.60 to 5.22 ms` after, **44.0% to 46.2% faster**. - **UTF-8 control:** `8.23 to 9.49 ms` before, `8.29 to 9.48 ms` after, **within +/- 1.8%**. - **Result:** regular padding avoids one full pass over the input bytes, while the UTF-8 path is unchanged. ### History - **`a4466496488`:** added the ASCII scan for the UTF-8 optimization. - **`1aed1af2f57`:** moved the mode flag into the runtime function implementation. - **`67b6461b591`:** restored separate byte and UTF-8 dispatch in the hot loop. ### Tests - **Existing coverage:** `01940_pad_string.sql`, `02986_leftpad_fixedstring.sql`, and `04070_pad_string_asan_overflow.sql` cover regular and UTF-8 padding, constants, `FixedString`, and edge cases. - **Test changes:** none. The output branches and UTF-8 path are unchanged. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Improve `leftPad` and `rightPad` performance by avoiding an unnecessary ASCII scan.

signals.title: Fix a lambda argument taking the type of a table column with the same name
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103584 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103627 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes `LOGICAL_ERROR: Unexpected return type from FunctionExpression` when a higher-order function in `PREWHERE` has a lambda parameter named after a table column of a different type and the body reads that column before the parameter. The parameter took the column's type. A parameter whose name is also a generated expression name in the body is not covered. ### Description A lambda parameter named after a table column takes the column's type when the body reads the column first: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (v UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); INSERT INTO t SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 20; SELECT v FROM t PREWHERE arrayExists(v -> (t.v != 0) AND (v = 7), [toNullable(toUInt64(7))]) ORDER BY v; -- Code: 49. Unexpected return type from FunctionExpression. Expected Nullable(UInt8). Got UInt8. ``` Renaming the parameter, or swapping the `AND` operands, returns `10, 20`. Reproduced on master 26.8.1.1454; debug builds abort. Found by the AST fuzzer, STID 2458-5396: [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114721&sha=39164d61335228645d86f6613ff2bb2bfff00280&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%2C%20old_compatibility%29). Root cause: `ActionsScopeNode::addInputColumnIfNecessary` is a name-keyed get-or-create, called by `visitColumn` with the unqualified name (`use_column_identifier_as_action_node_name` is false in `PREWHERE`, mutations and `Merge`). The first visitor to reach the lambda scope decides its type. With the column first, the argument's INPUT takes the column's type, so the body yields `UInt8` while the declared return type stays `Nullable(UInt8)`. #103627 fixes the capture name, but runs later. Fix: before visiting the body, declare the arguments the body reads as a column as INPUTs of the lambda scope, so the name-keyed lookup finds them. The old interpreter does this in `ScopeStack::pushLevel`, so `enable_analyzer = 0` is unaffected. One scope map is shared by all node kinds, so the declaration is narrow: a candidate is matched through the same `calculateActionNodeName` the visitor uses, and a name bound by another lambda, or computed by the body, is left alone. A parameter whose name is also a generated expression name in the body is not covered, and still fails as on master. Validation: `arrayExists`, `arrayMap`, a `tuple()` body, nested lambdas, `LowCardinality(String)` and the inverted case failed before and pass now; `EXPLAIN actions = 1` is unchanged elsewhere.

signals.title: Perf: Skip ASCII scan for byte-mode substringIndex
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/commit/d03ae0655abaef54117f6455063009aa7aed790b Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115003 ### Description - **Problem:** byte-mode `substringIndex` still scans the input with `isAllASCII` before taking the byte search path. - **Why the scan exists:** UTF-8 variants use it to take the byte path when the input and delimiter are ASCII; non-ASCII input needs UTF-8 character handling. - **Why byte mode does not need it:** `is_utf8` is already `false`, so the ASCII result cannot change the selected implementation. - **Change:** skip the input and delimiter scans when `is_utf8` is `false`. - **Paths covered:** `vectorVector`, `vectorConstant`, and `constantVector`. - **Behavior:** unchanged. The existing byte and UTF-8 search paths are still used. ### Benchmark - **Machine:** macOS arm64 - **Compiler:** `clang++ -O3` - **Implementation:** real ClickHouse `isAllASCII` implementation - **Input:** 1,048,576 ASCII rows with 64-byte strings, `.` delimiter, and count `1` - **Method:** median samples from three process runs - **`vectorVector`, byte mode:** `47.63 to 47.70 ms` before, `45.18 to 45.26 ms` after, **about 5.1% faster**. - **`vectorConstant`, byte mode:** `53.72 ms` before, `53.62 to 53.70 ms` after, **within 0.2%**. The constant-string scan is tiny. - **UTF-8 scan control:** `5.76 to 5.82 ms` before, `5.79 to 5.80 ms` after, **within +/- 0.6%**. ### History - **`d03ae0655ab`:** added the ASCII check so UTF-8 functions can use the byte path for ASCII input. - **#115003:** applies the same byte-mode short-circuit to `leftPad` and `rightPad`. ### Tests - **Test changes:** none. This only skips dead ASCII detection in byte mode; the result and search implementations are unchanged. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Improve byte-mode `substringIndex` performance by avoiding an unnecessary ASCII scan.

signals.title: Anchor the Build profile diff master baseline windows on the run's own event
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `Build profile diff` fails closed with `No master baseline with build profile data found - cannot compare` when CI is re-run days after it was triggered, even though the baseline rows are present. Failing run: [PR #113672 @ `494760825`](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113672&sha=494760825526a945d48dd1b90c9965dfd8721df9&name_0=PR&name_1=Build%20profile%20diff). `find_baseline` intersects two sets measured from different origins: the candidates are the frozen first-parent chain of the head's master parent (`master_track_commits_sha`, chain relative), while the row filter was `date >= today() - BASE_DAYS` (wall-clock relative). A re-run replays the frozen event payload, so the chain stays anchored on the old merge base while `today()` moves on, and once the gap exceeds `BASE_DAYS` the intersection is empty by construction. On the run above, `created_at` is `2026-08-06T13:03:49Z` against a `run_started_at` of `2026-08-16T01:28:41Z`: ten days, seven-day window. Eight more sites share the mismatch, so fixing only `find_baseline` relocates the error. Every master-side window now derives from `info.event_time`, frozen with the event, as a closed interval `[anchor - N, min(anchor + 4 days, today)]`. The first-parent walk takes the same anchor and stops a whole upload day further back, so the chain it returns is a superset of what those windows can match. Closed rather than half-open because `date` leads the primary key of the profile tables: the width is then fixed however old the event is, so the window slides rather than grows. The upper bound allows for profiles uploaded after their commit, measured at 4 hours p99 and 85 hours max over 673 master `arm_release` builds. Pull request side windows keep `today() - PR_DAYS`: those rows are uploaded by the run itself. An anchor at today emits the same windows as before, a local run keeps the wall-clock ones, and both fail-closes stand. Driving the job with that run's real values reproduces the error on the current module and resolves the baseline here.

signals.title: Do not alias pre-aggregation states of a zero-size aggregate in arrayReduceInRanges
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108781 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108781 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `arrayReduceInRanges` over an array whose elements are all NULL aborts a debug or sanitizer build with `Logical error: 'IAggregateFunction::merge called with the same source and destination state'`: ```sql SELECT arrayReduceInRanges('groupArray', [(1, 64)], arrayMap(x -> (x + NULL), range(64))); ``` Found by the AST fuzzer: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114747&sha=95a67283e1b33c000dba21cddefcd4418c4a2c94&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29 An all-NULL argument collapses the aggregate to `AggregateFunctionNothing`, whose `sizeOfData()` is 0. `Arena::alignedAlloc` advances the arena by `size`, so every zero-byte allocation returns the same address. The function allocates one pre-aggregation state per 64 rows plus one state per range from a single arena, so all of those states alias and both the pairwise level merge and the per-range merge become `merge(p, p)`. The fix allocates `max(sizeOfData(), 1)` bytes for the pre-aggregation states, so they are distinct and every merge still runs. The per-range state needs no padding: that merge only runs when the range spans a whole 64-row block, which is also the condition for a pre-aggregation state to exist, and its one-byte allocation has already advanced the arena. For an aggregate with a non-empty state the allocation is byte-identical to before. I deliberately did not suppress the merge for zero-size states. `sizeOfData() == 0` does not imply that merging is a no-op: `StatelessWindowFunction` is also zero-size and its `mergeImpl` throws. Since the aggregate is caller-supplied, a genuinely empty state cannot be told apart from one whose merge enforces a contract, so skipping the call could drop that enforcement. Two further places with the same allocation pattern are left alone. `ColumnAggregateFunction` can hold zero-size states (the test builds one via `nothingState`) but its `insertMergeFrom` merges across two different arenas. The `Aggregator` merge paths have one reported sighting of the sibling assertion (`mergeAndDestroyBatch`, on #111459) that 15 probes did not reproduce. Release behaviour is unchanged - the assertion compiles out and `Nothing::mergeImpl` is empty.

signals.title: Perf: Reserve nested element count in generic arrayReverse
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/commit/73e3a7b662161d6005e7727d8a711b930386b871 ### Description - **Problem:** the generic path reserves `res_data` using `src_array_offsets.size()`, which is the number of outer arrays. - **Actual output:** the loop inserts one value for every nested source element. - **Change:** reserve `src_data.size()`, the exact number of nested elements that will be inserted. - **Scope:** generic fallback only. The typed numeric and string paths already size their output from the nested source data. - **Behavior:** unchanged. `arrayReverse` still inserts the same values in the same order; only capacity planning changes. ### Benchmark - **Machine:** macOS arm64 - **Compiler:** `clang++ -O3` - **Setup:** focused generic-loop allocation benchmark with 65,536 rows, 16-byte values, and a fresh output column per run - **Method:** median of 7 samples with 2 repetitions, repeated across 3 process runs - **Average elements per array:** `1` -> **about 0%**, `2` -> **12.6% to 13.8%**, `4` -> **30.5% to 34.8%**, `8` -> **50.3% to 50.9%** faster - **Larger arrays:** `16` -> **44.6% to 46.8%**, `32` -> **48.0% to 51.7%**, `64` -> **45.9% to 48.3%** faster - **Result:** the exact reservation avoids repeated capacity growth when arrays contain multiple generic elements. This is a focused allocation benchmark for the generic loop, not an end-to-end query throughput number. ### History - **`73e3a7b6621`:** introduced the generic `arrayReverse` implementation and the original reservation in 2018. - **Current typed paths:** already use the nested source size for exact output sizing. - **`arrayTranspose`:** uses the same `src_data.size()` reservation pattern. ### Tests - **Existing coverage:** the original `00758_array_reverse` test covers the output behavior. - **Test changes:** none. This changes capacity planning only. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Improve generic `arrayReverse` performance by reserving space for all nested elements.

signals.title: Raise p99 gate for netem fault scenarios in Keeper stress tests
signals.text: <!--- A technical comment, you are free to remove or leave it as it is when PR is created The following categories are used in the next scripts, update them accordingly utils/changelog/changelog.py tests/ci/cancel_and_rerun_workflow_lambda/app.py --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): `NightlyKeeperFaults` has failed on every scheduled run since 2026-05-20, always on the same gate: `p99_le` on `prod-mix-fault` and `large-payload-fault` (both `default` and `rocks` backends), with p99 of 10.3–12.6s against the default 10s threshold. The cause is https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104351 (progress-based timeout in the ZooKeeper client, merged a few hours after the last passing nightly on 2026-05-18). Requests stalled by netem fault injection are no longer fast-failed by the operation timeout — they stay alive and complete in the latency tail. The `keeper_stress_tests` warehouse shows a clean step at exactly that nightly on `prod-mix-fault[default]`: read p99 8.3–8.9s → 11.0–12.6s, errors ~130–300 per run → exactly 0, on every one of the 37 nightlies since. Paired no-fault scenarios are flat across the boundary and all server-side hard-failure counters (`KeeperCommitsFailed`, snapshot failures, soft-memory rejections) are zero, so this is a measurement-semantics change (arguably an improvement — zero failed requests during faults), not a Keeper regression. These are the only two scenarios still gating p99 with the 10s default (the `latency-*` fault scenarios gate on error rate only). This PR sets an explicit `max_ms: 15000` on both, giving ~20% headroom over the worst observed nightly (12.58s) while still tripping on a real ≥2x regression. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=0eb658995715c01dd3bc1d6fdd13d61598b8096e&name_0=NightlyKeeperFaults&name_1=Keeper%20Stress%20%28Faults%29 Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104351 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1510` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->
