signal.title: Support PromQL @ start() and @ end() modifiers
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - **Improvement** ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): **PromQL: support `@ start()` and `@ end()` timestamp modifiers.** ### Summary PromQL allows `start()` and `end()` as special values for the `@` modifier. They mean the fixed start and end of a range query. For an instant query, both resolve to the evaluation time. Without this support, valid PromQL such as `http_requests_total @ start()` and `rate(http_requests_total[5m] @ end())` cannot be used against ClickHouse. Fixed-`@` subqueries keep their complete inner time grid and remain step-invariant across the outer range query. Standalone `start()` and `end()` functions are not included. ### Why this matters This is standard PromQL surface used by major Prometheus-compatible systems: - VictoriaMetrics has executable range-query tests for both `time() @ start()` and `time() @ end()`. - Grafana Mimir, Thanos, and Cortex replace these modifiers with fixed timestamps before splitting range queries, including subqueries. - Elasticsearch includes `@ start()`, `@ end()`, and subquery forms in its valid PromQL grammar fixtures. These are public implementation and compatibility references, not a claim about private customer query volume. Supporting the syntax keeps dashboards and recording/alerting queries portable across Prometheus-compatible backends. References: - **[Prometheus Querying basics:** `@` modifier](https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/querying/basics/) - [VictoriaMetrics executable tests](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/blob/master/app/vmselect/promql/exec_test.go#L1207-L1227) - [Grafana Mimir query splitting](https://github.com/grafana/mimir/blob/main/pkg/frontend/querymiddleware/split_and_cache.go#L2838-L2948) - [Thanos query splitting](https://github.com/thanos-io/thanos/blob/main/internal/cortex/querier/queryrange/split_by_interval.go#L593-L690) - [Cortex query splitting](https://github.com/cortexproject/cortex/blob/master/pkg/querier/tripperware/queryrange/split_by_interval.go#L1061-L1157) - [Elasticsearch valid PromQL grammar fixtures](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/plugin/esql/qa/testFixtures/src/main/resources/promql/grammar/queries-valid.promql#L1112-L1122) ### Changes - **Add:** `start()` and `end()` to the PromQL timestamp grammar. - **Preserve:** the symbolic modifier in the Prometheus query tree. - **Resolve:** the symbols against the outer query boundaries during evaluation. - **Keep:** offset and range-selector handling consistent with numeric `@` timestamps. - **Preserve:** the complete inner grid for fixed-`@` subqueries. ### Tests - **Coverage:** parser coverage for both symbols, modifier order, literals, and subqueries. - **Coverage:** instant and range query coverage, including a range selector under `@ end()`. - **Coverage:** `last_over_time()` coverage for symbolic and numeric `@` on subqueries. - **Comparison:** the new range-query cases with Prometheus through the existing integration helpers. - **Generated artifacts:** the ANTLR parser artifacts. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1499` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

An empty `complete=` lists registered command names. - CLI command responses include `cwd` after execution, so `cd` validation and directory tracking stay on the server. - Completion results are shown in columnar format, with a confirmation prompt for large result sets. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added server-backed tab completion for commands and znode paths in the Keeper web dashboard CLI, and return `cwd` from HTTP CLI commands so `cd` path validation stays consistent with `clickhouse-keeper-client`. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)

signal.title: Optimize delayInsertOrThrowIfNeeded overhead
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Optimized the insert backpressure path in `MergeTree` by reducing parts lock contention and short-circuiting the parts count check. ### Optimize 1. `getMaxPartsCountAndSizeForPartitionWithState` now snapshots the parts under the lock and does the aggregation after releasing it, shortening the shared-lock critical section so exclusive-lock writers wait less. 2. The per-partition scan is skipped when the O(1) total active part count is below the delay/throw thresholds, since it cannot change the outcome. This is the common case in healthy tables, so most inserts avoid the scan entirely.

signal.title: Add coverage tests for six untested function branches
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103918 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103922 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103940 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107447 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103885 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103931 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Test-only, 12 files, 42 insertions. @ zlareb1 asked me to re-file six closed `clickgapai` coverage PRs (linked above); this is the functions/types group. I did not take the tests on trust. For each one I mutated the exact line it claims to cover, rebuilt, and required that test to fail while the other five stayed green. That found three defects in the originals: - **103931 was flaky by construction.** Its overflow arguments were unqualified `DateTime` literals, read in the session timezone, which CI randomizes. In a positive-offset zone the value falls below the overflow boundary and the guard never fires: unpinned it FAILs under `Africa/Khartoum` and `Asia/Kolkata` and passes only under UTC. Every argument now pins a timezone, and it passes in all six zones swept. - **103931 covered only one of two guard copies.** The `wstart > wend` check exists in both the `windowID` and `hop` paths and neither was tested. Mutating one copy reddens only its own row, so both are now pinned, each row the other's scoping control. - **103922's `Nullable(String)` block could not detect the regression.** Its nested default `''` never equals an array element, so it stays green under the mutation while `Nullable(UInt64)` (default `0`, present in the array) reddens. Dropped. Two oracles were also too weak to bind a per-row read, and were strengthened after review: `04146` now pins the ordered address-to-digest mapping rather than the digest count, and `04329` uses two distinguishable rows rather than one. Per the recent "trim the tests" reviews, each file keeps one row per distinct dispatch or template instantiation rather than every spelling that reddens. The implementation commentary lives in the commit messages, not the `.sql`. <details> <summary>Validation</summary> Debug build, `clickhouse-test` with randomization on (the CI default). Every mutation changes the branch's output rather than deleting it, so a fall-through to an equivalent slower path cannot be mistaken for a vacuous test. Each arm was reverted and rebuilt before the next. | test | mutated line | result | |---|---|---| | `04201_dot_product_const_nonconst_size_mismatch` | `arrayDotProduct.cpp:397` size check neutered | FAIL alone; other 5 OK | | `04201_array_index_of_count_equal_nullable_value` | `arrayIndex.h:1246` null_map skip removed | FAIL alone; other 5 OK | | `04201_json_extract_keys_and_values_low_cardinality_input` | `FunctionsJSON.cpp:577` LC stripping skipped | FAIL alone; other 5 OK | | `04329_like_fixedstring_constant_match_everything` | `MatchImpl.h:322` per-row fill replaced by a first-row-only write | FAIL alone; other 5 OK | | `04146_ipv6_hashing_distinct_values` | `FunctionsStringHashFixedString.cpp:316` `&data[i]` -> `&data[input_rows_count-1-i]` | FAIL alone; other 5 OK | | `04201_windowID_hop_time_overflow` | `FunctionsTimeWindow.cpp:580` guard neutered | FAIL, `windowID` row only | | `04201_windowID_hop_time_overflow` | `FunctionsTimeWindow.cpp:430` guard neutered | FAIL, `hop` row only | The 4th and 5th mutations are the point of the strengthening: under each, the weaker oracle those tests originally carried stays green on the same binary. - 50 randomized runs of each of the six: 300/300 OK, and 200/200 again on the four changed by the strengthening. - Each test run 8 times concurrently with itself: 16/16 OK on the two rewritten ones, so no `no-parallel` tag. - `04201_windowID_hop_time_overflow` swept across 6 timezones, one test per run: 6/6 OK. - `04146`'s digests are build-independent: an independent Python `sha256(inet_pton(AF_INET6, addr))` reproduces them byte-for-byte, and the same method reproduces master's own committed digest in `02184_hash_functions_and_ip_types.reference`. </details>

[`getArrowType` maps the unsupported type to binary](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/CHColumnToArrowColumn.cpp#L1735-L1739) - schema conversion succeeds. 2. [`fillArrowArray`'s default case routes data into the fallback](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/CHColumnToArrowColumn.cpp#L1451-L1454). 3. [`fillArrowArrayWithRawColumnData` fetches each row via `IColumn::getDataAt`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/CHColumnToArrowColumn.cpp#L200) — 4. which [`ColumnObject` does not implement](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Columns/ColumnObject.cpp#L429-L431) (nor does [`ColumnVariant`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Columns/ColumnVariant.cpp#L454-L456), which `Dynamic` delegates to). So the fallback crashes on precisely the modern types it exists to cover. A tell-tale artifact: the output contains a valid Arrow schema (`binary` field) with 0 rows before the error. ### How to reproduce ```bash clickhouse local -q "SELECT '{\"a\":1}'::JSON AS j FORMAT Arrow" # Code: 48, getDataAt clickhouse local -q "SELECT 42::Dynamic AS d FORMAT Arrow" # Code: 48, getDataAt (Variant) ``` Reproduced on 26.5.1.882 and 26.6.1.1193 via FORMAT Arrow, HTTP, native client, and Arrow Flight SQL (src/Server/ArrowFlight/ passes output_unsupported_types_as_binary on every conversion, so any Flight SQL SELECT touching a table with a JSON column fails — one JSON column makes a table unreadable for BI clients like Power BI). ### Expected behavior _No response_ ### Error message and/or stacktrace _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_

signal.title: Fix data race and silent data loss on the object-storage path list
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/90967 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed silent data loss when several `INSERT`s run concurrently into one non-partitioned `s3`, `azure` or `hdfs` table with `s3_create_new_file_on_insert = 1` or its per-storage equivalent, once the base object exists: the writers could derive the same new file name and overwrite each other's rows with no error. Also fixed the data race on the shared path list caused by the same sequence. ### Description Found by `La Casa Del Dolor (amd_tsan)`, STID `3437-4fb8`, on an unrelated PR: [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=94148&sha=8eb1df1331f7fd5dcf93b4b0e975e56685b6f732&name_0=PR&name_1=La%20Casa%20Del%20Dolor%20%28amd_tsan%29), [log](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/PRs/94148/8eb1df1331f7fd5dcf93b4b0e975e56685b6f732/la_casa_del_dolor_amd_tsan/stderr0.log) `StorageObjectStorage::write()` read the configuration's path list, derived the next file name from it and published the result, unsynchronized. The configuration is created once per table and shared by every query, so two INSERT pipelines ran that sequence on one vector, which ThreadSanitizer reported in `std::vector::operator=`. The race is only the visible half. The new name is `<base>.<N>`, N from the length of the list the caller was handed, so the list is the name allocator: two concurrent INSERTs derive the same name, find it free, and open it with `WriteMode::Rewrite`, so one writer's rows silently replace the other's. With eight writers, two of nine rows survived. Fix: the concurrency moves into the class owning the state. `getPaths`/`setPaths` become non-virtual base methods taking a shared mutex and delegating to protected `*Impl` virtuals, so all five subclasses and the twelve `DataLakeConfiguration` instantiations inherit it, and `getPaths()` returns by value, since a reference into mutex-protected state protects nothing. Allocate-derive-publish becomes `allocatePathForWrite()` under a second, writer-only mutex, keeping the existence probes off the list's lock so a slow remote request cannot stall `SELECT`s. Three cases are left, so they are not mistaken for fixed: with no base object yet, nothing is reserved and both writers use the base path; wildcard-partitioned writes derive their name in the sink, so writers into one partition can still collide; and two `INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3(...)` queries build a configuration each, so there is no shared list. All three need an in-flight reservation, not a lock, as creating a sink creates no object to probe for. The new tests fail on master and pass 50/50 with the fix.

signal.title: Fix force_index_by_date/force_primary_key INDEX_NOT_USED reading through a view with parallel replicas (serialize_query_plan = 0 stopgap)
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/108266 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a false-positive `INDEX_NOT_USED` error thrown when a query with `force_index_by_date` or `force_primary_key` reads through a view (or subquery) with parallel replicas enabled, even though the predicate covers the partition/primary key. The fix covers the default query transport (`serialize_query_plan = 0`); with `serialize_query_plan = 1` a follower can still throw — fixing that lane is deferred to plan-based parallel replicas. ### Description Closes: #108266 Reading through a view under parallel replicas threw `INDEX_NOT_USED` for `force_index_by_date` / `force_primary_key` even when the predicate covered the key: ```sql CREATE TABLE nginx (timestamp DateTime) ENGINE = MergeTree PARTITION BY toYYYYMMDD(timestamp) ORDER BY timestamp; CREATE VIEW v_nginx AS SELECT * FROM nginx; SELECT count() FROM v_nginx WHERE timestamp >= '2026-06-05 12:00:00' SETTINGS enable_parallel_replicas = 1, max_parallel_replicas = 3, cluster_for_parallel_replicas = 'default', parallel_replicas_for_non_replicated_merge_tree = 1, force_index_by_date = 1; -- Code: 277. INDEX_NOT_USED ``` Reading the base table directly, or the view without parallel replicas, worked. **Root cause.** `force_index_by_date` / `force_primary_key` are enforced on the MergeTree reading step (`MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor::filterPartsByPartition`, `ReadFromMergeTree::selectRangesToRead`), which must see the query's filter. When a table is read through a view under parallel replicas, the view is planned as its own inner query, so the outer `WHERE` stays in a `FilterStep` above the view boundary and never reaches the inner reading step. The key condition is then always unknown there, so both guards throw even though the outer filter is valid (the result was always correct, only the index-usage check was at the wrong layer). An explicit subquery does not hit this because the analyzer inlines it into a single plan; a view stays a separate reading step. **Fix.** The existing `parallel_replicas_filter_pushdown` mechanism already pushes the filter through the view boundary into the reading step. This change enables it automatically in `buildContext` when parallel replicas is used on the initiator and either guard is set, unless the user set the setting explicitly. The index is then genuinely used, the guards are enforced correctly (a covered predicate passes, and a genuinely unused index still throws), and parallel replicas stays enabled (no fallback, no no-op). **Scope and known limitation (`serialize_query_plan = 1`).** A follower receives the pushed filter only through the shipped query AST (`ReadFromParallelRemoteReplicasStep::initializePipeline` injects it via `addFilters`). With `serialize_query_plan = 1` (the "distributed plan" transport) the initiator ships a query plan that was serialized before the filter is pushed, and the follower runs that plan and ignores the rewritten AST — so a follower's reading step still does not see the predicate and the guards can still throw a false-positive `INDEX_NOT_USED` in that mode. Per review, this fix must not override `serialize_query_plan`, and force-carrying the predicate into the serialized plan would be new transport machinery out of scope for a stopgap. So this PR is explicitly a **`serialize_query_plan = 0` stopgap**: it fixes the default AST transport; the `serialize_query_plan = 1` lane is deferred to plan-based parallel replicas, where index pushdown into a view works automatically. The regression test pins `serialize_query_plan = 0` and documents the limitation in its header. The regression test covers positives (base table as a control; view, view-over-view, and aliased view, with each guard and both; view without parallel replicas as a control) and negatives (a predicate that does not use the key must still throw `INDEX_NOT_USED` through views, including nested views). Verified on a 3-replica loopback cluster: with `serialize_query_plan = 0` all positives pass and negatives throw; with `serialize_query_plan = 1` a follower still throws the documented false positive.

signal.title: Support group_by_use_nulls in WITH TOTALS
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/39574 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `GROUP BY ... WITH TOTALS` now respects the `group_by_use_nulls` setting when the analyzer is enabled (`enable_analyzer = 1`, the default): the GROUP BY keys in the TOTALS summary row are reported as `NULL` instead of their default values, consistent with `GROUPING SETS`, `ROLLUP` and `CUBE`. Keys whose types cannot be wrapped in `Nullable` (for example `Array` or `Map`) keep their default value. With the old query analyzer (`enable_analyzer = 0`) the keys keep their default value as before. ### Description Rebase and port of #39574 (original author @ novikd) on top of current master. With `group_by_use_nulls = 1`, GROUP BY keys are already reported as `Nullable` for `GROUPING SETS`, `ROLLUP` and `CUBE`, but plain `GROUP BY ... WITH TOTALS` was left out: the keys stayed non-nullable and the TOTALS summary row showed `0` (the default value) instead of `NULL`. The original PR fixed this in the old interpreter by converting the keys inside `AggregatingStep`. The analyzer is now the default, so this ports the fix to the analyzer planner: - `PlannerExpressionAnalysis`: include `WITH TOTALS` in the `group_by_use_nulls` condition so the result type of the keys is analyzed as `Nullable`. - `Planner`: insert a `toNullable` conversion for the GROUP BY keys right before the `TotalsHaving` step. The TOTALS row is filled from default values, so a `Nullable` key column yields `NULL` there. This also covers `CUBE`/`ROLLUP WITH TOTALS`, whose own nullable conversion happens after `TotalsHaving` and would otherwise leave the TOTALS row non-NULL. Keys that cannot be made `Nullable` are skipped. Example (before this change the last row was `0`): ```sql SELECT number FROM numbers(10) GROUP BY number WITH TOTALS ORDER BY number SETTINGS group_by_use_nulls = 1; -- 0 .. 9 -- -- \N ``` The behavior is analyzer-only, so the affected tests set `enable_analyzer = 1`, and the documentation/changelog qualify the behavior as applying only with the analyzer. Updated tests: `02343_group_by_use_nulls`, `02535_analyzer_group_by_use_nulls`, `03912_tuple_comparison_group_by_use_nulls`, and the new `02373_group_by_use_nulls_with_totals` (from the original PR).

signal.title: Fix use-of-uninitialized-value in WITH FILL suffix over a merge
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107074 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a use-of-uninitialized-value in `ORDER BY ... WITH FILL ... STALENESS` when the fill suffix generates no rows (for example when the staleness window leaves nothing to fill) and the result is read through a merge of sorted streams (such as a two-shard `Distributed` table). ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer under MSan on top of #107074. `FillingTransform`, when all input chunks are processed, may run the suffix path. If the fill constraints are satisfied but no fill rows are produced (e.g. `WITH FILL ... STALENESS` with an exhausted staleness window), `generateSuffixIfNeeded` returns `true` while the result columns are freshly `cloneEmpty()`'d and carry no data. Previously the transform still emitted a 0-row chunk built from those empty columns. A downstream `MergingSortedTransform` (as used when reading from a two-shard `Distributed` table) then built a sort cursor over that empty chunk and compared row 0, reading past the end of the empty column. Fix: do not emit the suffix chunk when it has no rows. Minimal reproducer (needs a two-shard merge on the initiator): ```sql CREATE TABLE m (key Int) ENGINE = Memory; INSERT INTO m VALUES (100); CREATE TABLE d2 AS m ENGINE = Distributed(test_cluster_two_shards_localhost, currentDatabase(), m); SELECT _shard_num FROM d2 ORDER BY _shard_num ASC WITH FILL TO 46 STALENESS 1; ``` CI finding: `AST fuzzer (amd_msan)`, report https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107074&sha=3ec54c88d4eb535a5d644fc1ab91af31d717f9a5&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_msan%29 MSan use-of-uninitialized-value in `ColumnVector<UInt32>::doCompareAt` (`MergingSortedAlgorithm::consume`), origin `FillingTransform::initColumns` (`cloneEmpty`) via the suffix path. Verified on a local `amd_msan` build: reproduces before the fix (server aborts), clean after; the new regression test returns `1\n2`.

signal.title: Promote exponentialTimeDecayed window-functions to aggregate-functions
signal.text: ## Motivation `exponentialTimeDecayedSum`, `exponentialTimeDecayedAvg`, and `exponentialTimeDecayedCount` already exist and are documented as aggregate functions, but their current implementation is a special window-function implementation in `WindowTransform`. They do not provide mergeable aggregate states that can be persisted and combined with aggregate combinators such as `-State` and `-Merge`. This prevents incremental time-decayed aggregation in engines such as `AggregatingMergeTree`: data has to be evaluated through the window path instead of being aggregated independently in multiple batches and merged later. This PR adds regular, mergeable aggregate implementations for those three names while preserving the existing window implementation and its behavior. ## What changes For the regular aggregate form, each state keeps the weighted sum and sum of weights at the greatest timestamp observed by that state, plus that timestamp. When a row or another state has an older anchor, it is moved to the newer anchor with: `exp((older_time - newer_time) / decay_length)` The existing semantics are unchanged: `decay_length` is the interval after which a contribution has weight `1/e`. It is not a half-life. The state representation makes independently built states mergeable with the same calculation. Input rows do not need to be timestamp ordered, and different row orders and batch distributions produce the same mathematical result subject to normal `Float64` rounding. The aggregate forms accept numeric timestamps, `DateTime`, and `DateTime64`. ### Finalized decaying values The sum and count aggregate forms return the experimental parameterized type: `ExponentialTimeDecayingFloat64(decay_length)` The decay length is part of the type. The stored representation contains the value, anchor time, and a redundant decay-length marker. The marker is checked against the type parameter when the value is evaluated or combined, preventing incompatible decay lengths from being silently mixed through layout-compatible custom-tuple paths. Values can be constructed/aggregated with: `exponentialTimeDecayingFloat64(decay_length)(value, time)` A finalized decaying value can be aggregated again without repeating the decay length: `exponentialTimeDecayedSum(decaying_value)` When the input is `ExponentialTimeDecayingFloat64(decay_length)`, the decay length is inferred from its type and the result has the same parameterized type. This gives the closure property required by `SimpleAggregateFunction`, so it can be stored directly in `AggregatingMergeTree`: ```sql CREATE TABLE decaying ( key UInt64, value SimpleAggregateFunction( exponentialTimeDecayedSum, ExponentialTimeDecayingFloat64(60)) ) ENGINE = AggregatingMergeTree ORDER BY key; ``` The scalar helpers are: - `exponentialTimeDecayingValueAt(value, target_time)` — evaluate the same exponential curve before, at, or after its anchor, including at `now()` / `now64()`; - `exponentialTimeDecayingDecayLength(value)` — read the decay length encoded in the type; - `exponentialTimeDecayingAdd(a, b)` — combine two values at their greatest anchor. The `+` operator uses the same addition logic for two decaying values. Different decay lengths are rejected. `exponentialTimeDecayedAvg` continues to return `Float64`. All new regular-aggregate and decaying-value behavior is experimental and disabled by default behind `allow_experimental_time_decay_aggregate_functions`. ## Effect on the existing window functions The existing window-function implementation remains in place. Window calls continue to use the previous frame-based implementation, retain their `Float64` result, and do not require `allow_experimental_time_decay_aggregate_functions`. This PR also corrects the function documentation to consistently call the parameter `decay_length` and describe the existing `1/e` decay semantics. ## Correctness and tests Stateless tests cover: - regular aggregation and `-State` / `-Merge`; - direct aggregation of finalized `ExponentialTimeDecayingFloat64(decay_length)` values; - direct `SimpleAggregateFunction(exponentialTimeDecayedSum, ExponentialTimeDecayingFloat64(decay_length))` storage and merging in `AggregatingMergeTree`; - different input orders and batch distributions, including reproducibly generated randomized inputs; - numeric, `DateTime`, and `DateTime64` time arguments; - the experimental setting in enabled and disabled forms; - forward and backward value evaluation, addition, decay-length lookup, and rejection of inconsistent/mixed decay lengths; - signed values, empty input, nullable paths, and large-time decay/underflow cases. The implementation uses `Float64` accumulation. As with other floating-point reductions, large signed values that nearly cancel can expose order/grouping-dependent rounding. Stronger reproducibility for that case is intentionally left for a separate improvement if feedback shows it is important in practice. ## Benchmark status There are no end-to-end ClickHouse benchmark results yet. The benchmark already posted in the PR discussion is a standalone C++ microbenchmark of the decay formulas. It showed the expected benefit from avoiding redundant `exp` evaluations in the merge/value paths, but it excludes ClickHouse aggregation, column access, serialization, scheduling, and `AggregatingMergeTree` overhead and therefore is not evidence of end-to-end query throughput. An end-to-end benchmark, preferably a ClickHouse performance test covering state creation and state merging, is still pending. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add experimental mergeable `exponentialTimeDecayedSum`, `exponentialTimeDecayedAvg`, and `exponentialTimeDecayedCount` aggregate forms, including a parameterized decaying-value type that can be stored directly with `SimpleAggregateFunction` in `AggregatingMergeTree`, while preserving the existing window-function behavior.

signal.title: Add ALTER TABLE ... RECOMPRESS COLUMN
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109432 Introduce a new `ALTER TABLE ... RECOMPRESS COLUMN col` statement that re-compresses the existing data of a column with the column's current compression codec. Changing a column's codec with `MODIFY COLUMN col CODEC(...)` is metadata-only: the new codec applies to newly written data, while data already stored in existing parts keeps its old codec until the parts happen to be merged. `RECOMPRESS COLUMN` rewrites the data of `col` in existing parts so that it is compressed with the codec currently set in the table metadata. Because a compression codec does not change the serialized representation of a column, for `Wide` parts the recompression is done **without deserializing the values**: each compressed block of every substream `.bin` is decompressed and re-compressed one-to-one with the new codec. This keeps the decompressed content and granule boundaries byte-identical, so the marks file only needs its compressed offsets remapped (the decompressed offsets, per-granule row counts, the primary index and skip indexes are preserved and hardlinked). The decompressed content is unchanged, so the `uncompressed_size`/`uncompressed_hash` checksums are carried over from the source part and only the on-disk `file_size`/`file_hash` are recomputed. `Compact` parts (and dynamic-subcolumn types) cannot recompress a single column in isolation, so they fall back to a normal whole-part re-serialization that writes every column with its current codec. Implemented as a mutation. A new `ALTER RECOMPRESS COLUMN` grant is added. The issue also asks to check `RECOMPRESS` TTL mutations, which currently go through a full deserialize/re-serialize merge; that is left for a follow-up. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added `ALTER TABLE ... RECOMPRESS COLUMN col`, which re-compresses a column's existing data with its current codec. For wide parts the data is recompressed without deserializing the column values.

signal.title: Iceberg: propagate table UUID from REST catalog to avoid metadata cac…
signal.text: REST catalog inline responses already contain the table UUID and metadata location. Propagate the UUID through DataLakeSpecificProperties -> StorageObjectStorageConfiguration.catalog_uuid_hint -> initializePersistentTableComponents so the metadata cache is checked before fetching metadata.json from network storage. ### Performance mechanism **Before:** On first table initialization, `getMetadataJSONObject` is called without a known UUID. The cache probe is skipped (`table_uuid == nullopt`), so metadata.json is always fetched from remote storage as a cold read. Even if the same table is initialized again later, the cache was never populated on the first pass. **After:** The REST catalog provides the table UUID upfront via `catalog_uuid_hint`. `getMetadataJSONObject` probes the cache with `uuid:path` key before doing any remote I/O. If the metadata was previously cached (e.g., by a prior query that retroactively populated it), the cold read is eliminated entirely. If not, the cold read still happens but the result is cached with the correct UUID for future lookups. **Impact:** Deterministic reduction in remote `metadata.json` fetches for REST catalog tables. Each avoided fetch saves one round-trip to S3/GCS/ABFS plus deserialization overhead. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Improve Iceberg catalog metadata caching by using table UUID from catalog responses to warm the metadata cache, avoiding a redundant remote metadata.json read on table initialization. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes Improve Iceberg catalog metadata caching. <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Medium risk because it changes Iceberg metadata cache key composition and the metadata-loading path to use a new UUID hint, which could affect cache hit rates or correctness if UUIDs/paths are inconsistent. > > **Overview** > **Improves Iceberg REST catalog metadata caching** by propagating the table UUID from REST inline responses through `DataLakeSpecificProperties` into `StorageObjectStorageConfiguration` as `catalog_uuid_hint`, so the first metadata fetch can probe the metadata cache before doing extra remote IO. > > Updates metadata loading to accept an optional known UUID, capture raw metadata JSON for reuse, and retroactively populate the cache once the real UUID is discovered. Also fixes potential cache-key collisions by changing `IcebergMetadataFilesCache::getKey` to use a `uuid:path` delimiter, and adds gtest coverage for key uniqueness and cache hit/miss behavior. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 2e7400b8dc007641c702d41b3fd6cafdc10eb823. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: S3Queue `after_processing='delete'` silently leaves objects in the bucket
signal.text: 🕵️ ## Describe what's wrong With `after_processing = 'delete'`, S3Queue consumes every row exactly once but does not always delete the source objects. The leftovers are never re-read either, so they are orphaned: the queue treats them as `Processed` while the object is still in the bucket. Nothing reports this. There is no error, no exception and no log line — the delete simply does not happen for some objects, and 3 of 4 objects in the very same run *are* deleted. The consequence is that a bucket the user has explicitly asked to be drained grows without bound, and no queue-side state reveals it. **This is not a duplicate of #114421** — see the section at the bottom. ## Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Reproduced on **26.8.1.1384** (release build) against MinIO. ## How to reproduce Write four CSV objects of five rows each under one prefix, then: ```sql CREATE TABLE dsink (id UInt64, v String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; CREATE TABLE dq (id UInt64, v String) ENGINE = S3Queue('http://127.0.0.1:19001/fuzz/<prefix>/*.csv', 'minio', 'minio123', 'CSV') SETTINGS keeper_path = '/clickhouse/s3q/<prefix>', after_processing = 'delete', mode = 'ordered', processing_threads_num = 8, buckets = 1, list_objects_batch_size = 2, max_processed_files_before_commit = 1, polling_min_timeout_ms = 50, polling_max_timeout_ms = 200; CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW dmv TO dsink AS SELECT id, v FROM dq; ``` Wait until `count()` in `dsink` reaches 20, then list the bucket prefix. One or more objects are still there, and stay there. ## Expected behaviour Every object whose rows have been committed is deleted from the bucket. ## Actual behaviour ``` rows=20/20 objects_left: f_1.csv <- 20s after start rows=20/20 objects_left: f_1.csv <- 50s after start, table still running ``` ## It is a race, not a specific setting combination An automated 30-minute campaign (339 S3Queue runs, 3438 oracle checks) hit this 8 times across 4 distinct configurations: | objects left | mode | threads | parallel_inserts | buckets | batch | commit_files | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | ordered | 8 | 0 | 1 | 2 | 1 | | 1 | ordered | 8 | 1 | 7 | 2 | 100 | | 3 | ordered | 8 | 1 | 0 | 2 | 3 | | 2 | ordered | 2 | 1 | 2 | 1000 | 0 | Only `mode='ordered'` and `after_processing='delete'` are constant. `processing_threads_num`, `buckets`, `list_objects_batch_size`, `parallel_inserts` and the commit thresholds all vary across hits, so no single one of them is necessary. Per-configuration rate, 12 trials each, judged after the rows land plus a 6 s grace and a 12 s re-check (so a merely slow delete cannot count as a leak): | configuration | runs leaving objects | |---|---| | `ordered`, threads=1 (else default) | 0/12 | | `ordered`, threads=8 (else default) | 0/12 | | `unordered`, threads=8 (else default) | 0/12 | | `ordered`, threads=2, `parallel_inserts=1` | 1/12 | | **full combination from the repro above** | **8/12** | Reading the two tables together: - `mode='ordered'` looks genuinely required — `unordered` is 0/12 here and all 8 campaign hits were ordered. - Concurrency alone is not enough: neither `threads=8` nor `threads=1` on an otherwise default ordered queue ever failed. - The full combination is the reliable trigger at **8/12**, so that is the one to use when reproducing. - But it is not the only trigger. `threads=2 + parallel_inserts=1` reaches it at 1/12, and the campaign independently hit it at `threads=2, batch=1000, commit_files=0, buckets=2, parallel_inserts=1` — a configuration the full-combination repro shares almost nothing with. So this is a race in the ordered-mode post-commit delete path that several different concurrency shapes can lose; the settings in the repro make it likely, not possible. ## What is and is not affected - **No data loss and no duplicates.** All 20 rows arrive exactly once in every run, including the failing ones. The bug is confined to the post-commit delete. - **The object is orphaned, not pending.** It is not re-read while the table keeps running (the row count stays flat for a further 30 s), so Keeper has the file as processed while the object is still in the bucket. ## Why this is not #114421 **#114421** ("S3Queue: swallowed `after_processing='delete'` failure silently re-ingests files as duplicates") reaches a similar end state by a different route: there the delete *errors* — `AccessDenied` from a least-privilege credential, or a transient failure past `after_processing_retries` — and the exception is swallowed in `ObjectStorageQueuePostProcessor.cpp`, which logs `LOG_WARNING "Failed to tag all N objects"`. That warning never appears here. Grepping the server log across the repro runs gives zero PostProcessor lines, zero `AccessDenied` and zero "Failed to tag", at `warning` level where they would have shown. The credentials are full, and most objects in the same run are deleted successfully. So the swallow path is not being hit: nothing fails, and nothing is logged. A fix for #114421 (don't mark `Processed` unless the action completed) would likely mask this one without addressing the underlying race. Adjacent but distinct: **#114595** (stale per-server `Processed` cache) and **#112341** (files marked `Processed` while rows are discarded). S3Queue's `Processed` bookkeeping has an active cluster of reports, but neither of those involves the post-commit delete. ## Notes `system.s3_queue_metadata` confirms the queue considers the run clean: `failed_nodes_count` is 0 for the affected `keeper_path`, so the leftover object is not sitting in a retry or failure state — it is simply never deleted. The object is also never re-read while the table keeps running. A trace-level run was also taken to count `Removing N objects` calls, but the 30-minute campaign was creating its own `after_processing='delete'` tables at the same time, so those lines cannot be attributed to this repro. Not used as evidence. The absence of the `Failed to tag` warning is unaffected: contamination can only add lines, not remove them.

signal.title: Explain data/expected structure mismatches in INSERT parse errors
signal.text: Improves the error message shown when parsing the data of an `INSERT` fails. Previously, inserting data whose structure does not match the destination produced a confusing low-level parse error (for example `Cannot parse input: expected '\t' before ...`) with no hint about the real cause. In the linked issue, the destination's inferred schema had integer columns while the inserted `TSV` data had string columns, and the reported error pointed at a tab that was actually present. Now, on a parse failure, ClickHouse infers the structure of the data being inserted (only when the format has a data schema reader, and solely for diagnostics) and, if it does not correspond to the expected structure, appends an explanation listing both the inferred and the expected structure. For example: ``` Code: 27. DB::Exception: Cannot parse input: expected '\t' before: 'page_view... ... The structure of the data being inserted does not match the structure expected by the query, which is likely the cause of the parsing error. Inferred structure of the input data (in format `TSV`): c1 Nullable(Int64) c2 Nullable(String) c3 Nullable(String) Expected structure: c1 Int64 c2 Int64 c3 Int64 ``` The check is wired through a lazy provider on `IInputFormat` that runs only on a genuine parse error, so there is no cost on the happy path. The comparison ignores the artificial `Nullable` wrapper that schema inference adds by default, so inserting valid data into non-nullable columns is not falsely flagged. It covers the synchronous local/server path, client-side parsing, and the asynchronous insert queue (the default path now that `async_insert` is enabled by default). Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110622 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): When parsing of the data being inserted by an `INSERT` fails, the error message now explains a likely structure mismatch by comparing the structure inferred from the data with the structure expected by the query.

signal.title: Set Keeper component in ZooKeeperLock destructor
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110590 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `LOGICAL_ERROR` ("Current component is empty") that could abort the server in debug/sanitizer builds when a zero-copy replicated merge or mutation task holding a zero-copy exclusive lock was torn down by the background executor. ### Description A replicated zero-copy merge/mutation task owns the zero-copy exclusive lock via its `std::optional<ZeroCopyLock>` member. When such a task is torn down on a `MergeTreeBackgroundExecutor` thread while the lock is still held, `~ZooKeeperLock` issues ZooKeeper requests (`exists`/`remove`) to release the ephemeral node. That teardown runs outside any Keeper component scope, so with `enforce_keeper_component_tracking` enabled `ZooKeeper::pushRequest` throws `Current component is empty, please set it for your scope using Coordination::setCurrentComponent` (a server abort in debug/sanitizer builds). Reported on #110590 (amd_debug flaky check). The Keeper component is set at the highest level that owns the section doing those ZooKeeper requests: the `MutateFromLogEntryTask` and `MergeFromLogEntryTask` destructors. Each sets the component and then releases `zero_copy_lock` explicitly inside that scope, because the member would otherwise be destroyed after the destructor body, outside the guard. Both task types own a `std::optional<ZeroCopyLock>`, so both are covered. Observed stack (baseline, before the fix): ``` Coordination::ZooKeeper::pushRequest (ZooKeeperImpl.cpp, "Current component is empty") zkutil::ZooKeeper::exists zkutil::ZooKeeperLock::unlock zkutil::ZooKeeperLock::~ZooKeeperLock DB::MutateFromLogEntryTask::~MutateFromLogEntryTask (~optional<ZeroCopyLock>) DB::TaskRuntimeData::resetTask DB::MergeTreeBackgroundExecutor<DynamicRuntimeQueue>::routine ``` Added a stateless regression test (`04546_zero_copy_lock_dtor_keeper_component`) that pauses a mutation task on a new failpoint `rmt_mutate_task_pause_after_zero_copy_lock` fired right after `tryCreateZeroCopyExclusiveLock()` succeeds, then drops the table so the task is destroyed while it provably holds the lock. Verified locally (embedded Keeper, s3_cache zero-copy, `enforce_keeper_component_tracking=1`): fails with SIGABRT ("Current component is empty") without the fix, passes with it.

signal.title: Fix logical error for IN with an identical non-constant tuple on both sides in the old analyzer
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer, `AST fuzzer (arm_asan_ubsan)`, STID 2508-3457: ```sql EXPLAIN PIPELINE graph = 0, graph = 0, compact = 1 SELECT 'null', (SELECT tuple(materialize(NULL), NULL) GLOBAL IN (materialize(NULL), NULL)) GROUP BY ALL SETTINGS transform_null_in = 1 ``` Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111552&sha=38215c1758332de1ea8a4b5a620ba8364586f6c6&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%29 It reaches the old interpreter through a scalar subquery, and reduces to `SELECT (materialize(1), 2) IN (materialize(1), 2) SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 0`. Release builds catch the exception but still reject the query with an empty identifier name: `Code: 47 ... Unknown identifier: ; there are columns: dummy, 1, materialize(1), 2, ...`. Root cause: a literal's `unique_column_name` is assigned lazily, only when `ActionsMatcher::visit(const ASTLiteral &)` runs, and `getNameAndTypeFromAST` requires it. The old interpreter's row-wise `IN` rewrite visits the left argument first, and here the right-hand `tuple` renders to the same column name as the left one, so `visit(right_argument, data)` takes the common-subexpression early return and never descends into the right-hand children. The loop that follows then asks for the name and type of each raw child, and a literal child is still unnamed. The fix visits each child before naming it. That call site was the only one of the eight `getNameAndTypeFromAST` callers in the file not already preceded by a `visit()` of the node it names. `visit` is idempotent, so the added call is a no-op when the child is already indexed. The abort is gone after the change, with the result now matching `enable_analyzer = 1` on 20 shapes (including `NULL` with `transform_null_in`, `nullIn`, `GLOBAL IN`, `LowCardinality`, array and tuple literal children, `indexHint`, and the query above). 13 shapes that already worked are unchanged, with byte-identical `EXPLAIN actions = 1` output. Removing the added line reinstates the abort. Introduced by #104993 and present only on master, so no backport is needed. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104993

signal.title: `RENAME DATABASE` query doesn't work for materialized views
signal.text: **Company or project name** Prefer not to specify **Describe what's wrong** `RENAME DATABASE` query doesn't seem to be working correctly with materialized view statements. After renaming a database with `RENAME DATABASE old_name TO new_name` query, the materialized views would still reference tables with the `old_name` as could be seen with `SHOW CREATE new_name.materialized_view` statement in the repro. That leads to a bunch of issues with database permissions and `SELECT` queries. And while `INSERT` queries into the main table seem to be working, they are not triggering any relative materialized views. Repro: https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/797f730d-d037-4b64-8d17-ce47911fccdd **Does it reproduce on the most recent release?** Yes **Enable crash reporting** Doesn't crash **How to reproduce** I first got this on `24.8.1.10452` in ClickHouse Cloud, but I'm also able to reproduce it on current latest. ``` CREATE DATABASE test; CREATE TABLE test.sample ( id UUID DEFAULT generateUUIDv4(), data TEXT DEFAULT '' ) ENGINE = MergeTree PRIMARY KEY (id) ORDER BY (id); -- Create materialized view without explicitly specifying target table CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW test.inline_mat_view ( uuid UUID, data TEXT ) ENGINE MergeTree ORDER BY (uuid) AS SELECT id as uuid, data FROM test.sample; -- Create table for materialized view explicitly CREATE TABLE test.explicit_table ( uuid UUID, data TEXT ) ENGINE MergeTree ORDER BY (uuid); -- Create materialized view pointing to explicitly created table CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW test.explicit_mat_view TO test.explicit_table AS SELECT id as uuid, data FROM test.sample; -- Output original CREATE statements for both materialized views SHOW CREATE test.inline_mat_view; SHOW CREATE test.explicit_mat_view; RENAME DATABASE test TO dev; -- Inserting data into main table doesn't trigger any error, but materialized views are not updated INSERT INTO dev.sample (data) VALUES ('test1'), ('test2'), ('test3'), ('test4'), ('test5'); -- CREATE statements for materialized views after renaming the database still points to the old database name SHOW CREATE dev.inline_mat_view; SHOW CREATE dev.explicit_mat_view; -- Exception due to missing 'test' database SELECT * FROM dev.inline_mat_view; SELECT * FROM dev.explicit_mat_view; ``` **Expected behavior** When renaming the database I would expect materialized view to be updated accordingly and to point to the correct table in the renamed database.

signal.title: Arrow Flight SQL: CloseSession action not implemented - errors instead of closing
signal.text: ### Company or project name _No response_ ### Describe the unexpected behaviour The Flight session-management spec defines three actions: [`SetSessionOptions`, `GetSessionOptions`, `CloseSession`](https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/f64e90ac8305c2cab5abd849f02abac305d7a955/format/Flight.proto#L600-L660). ClickHouse implements the first two ([Set](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Server/ArrowFlight/ArrowFlightServer.cpp#L1342), [Get](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Server/ArrowFlight/ArrowFlightServer.cpp#L1425)) but `CloseSession` falls into the [DoAction catch-all](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Server/ArrowFlight/ArrowFlightServer.cpp#L1614-L1615): ```<Error> ArrowFlightServer: DoAction failed: NotImplemented: CloseSession is not supported``` So spec-compliant clients cannot tear down sessions cleanly, and every attempt logs an Error-level entry. (A close path exists, but only via the nonstandard [`x-clickhouse-session-close` header](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Server/ArrowFlight/AuthMiddleware.cpp#L252-L254).) ### Related: bearer-token TTL Each basic-auth call mints a bearer token returned in the[`authorization` response header](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Server/ArrowFlight/AuthMiddleware.cpp#L25-L29), expiring on a [60-second sliding TTL (`default_session_timeout`)](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Server/ArrowFlight/AuthMiddleware.cpp#L152). On a failed RPC the response header (and rotated token) may never reach the client, and BI tools routinely idle >60 s between user interactions - the result is spurious `Session expired or not authenticated` failures that surface in Power BI as **"We couldn't authenticate with the credentials provided"** with valid credentials. ### How to reproduce ```python # pip install pyarrow import pyarrow.flight as flight client = flight.FlightClient("grpc://localhost:9006") tok = client.authenticate_basic_token(b"default", b"clickhouse") opts = flight.FlightCallOptions(headers=[tok]) list(client.do_action(flight.Action("CloseSession", b""), opts)) # -> ArrowNotImplementedError: CloseSession is not supported ``` Reproduced on 26.5.1.882 and 26.6.1.1193 (official Docker images). ### Expected behavior CloseSession returns CloseSessionResult{CLOSED} and releases the session, or at minimum succeeds as a no-op, so clients can recycle pooled connections without error noise. ### Error message and/or stacktrace _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_

signal.title: Do not derive a DISTINCT limit hint when the LIMIT must read till end
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111326 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix wrong results for `SELECT DISTINCT` with a `LIMIT` that has to read its whole input: `LIMIT n WITH TIES` dropped tying rows, `exact_rows_before_limit = 1` reported a truncated `rows_before_limit_at_least`, and `GROUP BY ... WITH TOTALS` computed the totals row from a prefix of the stream. ### Description Related: #111326, which fixed the sibling cases (negative / fractional / bare-offset LIMIT) in these same guards. Here the hint is wrong for an ordinary positive LIMIT too. Three wrong answers on default settings: ```sql -- all 200000 rows tie on k, so all must come back; returns 65409 SELECT count() FROM (SELECT DISTINCT number, 0 AS k FROM numbers(200000) ORDER BY k LIMIT 1 WITH TIES); -- MergeTree t, 200000 rows: totals row is 3125, must be 200000 SELECT DISTINCT c FROM (SELECT n AS k, count() AS c FROM t GROUP BY k WITH TOTALS) LIMIT 1 FORMAT JSONCompact; -- same table: rows_before_limit_at_least is 65536, must be 200000 SELECT DISTINCT n FROM t ORDER BY n LIMIT 3 FORMAT JSONCompact SETTINGS exact_rows_before_limit = 1; ``` `limit_hint` makes the distinct transform call `stopReading()` after `limit + offset` distinct rows, closing its input. All three consumers need rows beyond that: `WITH TIES` needs the unbounded suffix tying with the last row, `exact_rows_before_limit` counts rows passing the Limit/Offset transforms, and `WITH TOTALS` without `ORDER BY` (or below a subquery in `FROM`) aggregates the whole stream. No finite hint is safe for any of them. `WITH TIES` has its own flag on the `LimitStep`, so the guards in both analyzers reject it directly. The other two are exactly the cases in which the `LimitStep` is built with `always_read_till_end`, so the guards reuse that predicate, extracted into one function per analyzer and called both where the `LimitStep` is built and where the hint is decided, so the two cannot drift apart. `limitPushDown.cpp` needs the same check, since it re-introduces the hint through `DistinctStep::updateLimitHint`; it mirrors the `UnionStep` guard just above. This costs nothing: such a LIMIT reads everything anyway, and `rows_read` is identical either way. Otherwise purely restrictive, and no setting or format change. New test `04845_distinct_limit_hint_with_ties` fails on master, passes 100/100 randomized here, and reverting each hunk reddens the matching cases. It also pins the exception: `WITH TOTALS` plus `ORDER BY` on the same query does not read till end, so the hint still applies. One reference line moves: `04539_lazy_final_read_in_order_limit_disabled` asserted lazy FINAL stays disabled for `DISTINCT ... LIMIT n SETTINGS exact_rows_before_limit = 1`, which held only because the hint stopped reading early. That query now reads everything, so lazy FINAL applies, as it already does for the plain `LIMIT` case in the same test. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1496` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Set the current Keeper component in TextIndexCountSource::generate
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113295 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Related: #113295 `SELECT count() FROM t WHERE hasAllTokens(str, [...])` is rewritten by the trivial-count-from-text-index optimization into a `ReadFromTextIndexCount` step (added in #111494). Its source runs on a pipeline execution thread: `TextIndexCountSource::generate` -> `computeCountForPart` -> `makeTextIndexInputStream` -> `IMergeTreeDataPart::getStreamNameOrHash(..., IDataPartStorage &)`, whose body probes the part storage with `existsFile`. On a disk that keeps part metadata in Keeper that probe is a real Keeper request, and `Coordination::ZooKeeper::pushRequest` throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` when no component is set for the scope. `generate()` is the outermost scope this step owns on that thread, and it set none: the step builds its own `Pipe`, so unlike the ordinary read path it never inherits the guard from `MergeTreeSource::tryGenerate`. This adds the one-line RAII guard at the top of `generate()`. The guard is a nesting-safe thread-local stack and every Keeper-reaching call above is a descendant of that scope, so no deeper placement is needed. Same shape as #113295 for `MergeTreeCodecBlockCountsSource::generate` and the sibling `MergeTreeTextIndexSource::generate`. Of the four callers of `makeTextIndexInputStream`, the other three already have an ancestor guard (`MergeTreeSource::tryGenerate` for both `MergeTreeReaderTextIndex` sites, the mutate/merge task guards for `MergeTextIndexesTask`); this step was the only gap. Category is `CI Fix or Improvement`, as in #113295 and #113386: the metadata-in-Keeper storage type is registered only under `#if CLICKHOUSE_CLOUD`, and `LOGICAL_ERROR` aborts only in debug and sanitizer builds, so this cannot happen in an official stable build. For the same reason no test is added: no public build reaches Keeper through `existsFile`. Validated with the existing `02346_text_index*` suite (plus 50/50 randomized runs of `02346_text_index_optimize_trivial_count`), an `EXPLAIN` assertion that the modified scope is the one the query executes, and a run with `enforce_keeper_component_tracking = 1`. Left alone: the plan-time `getDeserializedFormat` path can also reach `existsFile` for packed skip-index parts and is likewise unguarded, but it predates this step by three weeks and is not this failure's carrier.

signal.title: Histogram metric `keeper_read_wait_for_write_time_milliseconds` is never recorded with the new request dispatcher
signal.text: ### Describe what's wrong The Prometheus histogram `keeper_read_wait_for_write_time_milliseconds` ("Time read request waits for the write request it depends on to complete") is still registered and exported, but it is never observed when `use_new_dispatcher` is enabled (the default). The new dispatcher still parks read requests behind in-flight same-session writes (`LateReads` in `KeeperRequestDispatcher`), so the wait the metric is supposed to measure still happens — it is just no longer instrumented. Consumers of the metric see a histogram that is present but permanently empty, which reads as "reads never wait for writes" instead of "not measured". The Keeper stress-test nightlies confirm it: on `prod-mix-no-fault` the histogram recorded ~875k observations per run (average wait ~65 ms) up to the 2026-05-21 nightly, and exactly 0 from the 2026-05-23 nightly onward — the first nightly containing the new dispatcher. All sibling Keeper span histograms (`keeper_read_process_*`, `keeper_write_commit_*`, `keeper_receive_request_*`, ...) kept reporting across the same boundary. ### How to reproduce * Which ClickHouse server version to use: any build after 2026-05-22 (master) Run a 3-node `clickhouse-keeper` ensemble with the Prometheus endpoint enabled, drive a mixed read/write workload that issues reads while writes from the same session are in flight (e.g. `keeper-bench` with a prod-mix workload), and watch `keeper_read_wait_for_write_time_milliseconds_count`: it stays at 0. With `<use_new_dispatcher>0</use_new_dispatcher>` in `coordination_settings` it advances as before. Public data from the Keeper stress warehouse showing the flatline (per-nightly max of the exported `_count`): ```sql SELECT toDate(ts) AS d, max(value) AS cnt FROM keeper_stress_tests.keeper_metrics_ts WHERE scenario = 'prod-mix-no-fault[default]' AND branch = 'master' AND name = 'ClickHouseHistogramMetrics_keeper_read_wait_for_write_time_milliseconds_count' AND ts >= '2026-05-19' GROUP BY d ORDER BY d -- 2026-05-19: 874616, 2026-05-21: 886896, 2026-05-23 and later: 0 ``` (run on https://play.clickhouse.com/ with user `play`) Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/101757
signal.author: zlareb1

signal.title: Cheaper per-sample add path in timeSeries*ToGrid aggregate functions
signal.text: The `timeSeries*ToGrid` aggregate functions pay a fixed cost for every incoming sample in `AggregateFunctionTimeseriesBase`: computing the grid bucket index and looking the bucket up in a hash map. This PR makes both cheaper: - **Int64 fast path for the bucket-index computation.** `bucketIndexForTimestamp` used Int128 division and modulo per sample to stay overflow-safe for adversarial grid parameters. Now, when all grid parameters are bounded by 2^61 (checked once in the constructor; covers every practical case), the per-sample computation runs in plain Int64 arithmetic, dividing by the fixed `step` through a precomputed `libdivide` reciprocal — the `__udivmodti4` calls disappear from query profiles. The Int128 path is kept as-is for out-of-range parameters and single-point grids (`start == end`). - **Cached last-bucket pointer in the batch add loops.** Samples arrive sorted by timestamp within a series, so consecutive samples usually land in the same bucket; the loops now reuse the last bucket pointer and skip the hash-map lookup for same-bucket runs. Inserting into the map can invalidate the cached pointer, but an insert happens only on a bucket change, which re-acquires the pointer. Measured on tsbench, a PromQL benchmark over the ClickHouse `TimeSeries` engine (30 days of scrape data at 15 s step; scale 1 = 1.06 billion samples / 6112 series, Ryzen 9950X, query result cache disabled, best of 3): on a 30-day PromQL `rate` query scanning 69M samples, the per-sample Int128 division (`__udivmodti4`) was ~2% of CPU and the bucket-index computation ~3% — both disappear from the profile with the Int64 fast path; the whole rate-aggregation add path went from ~12% to ~8% of the query. A new performance test `tests/performance/timeseries_to_grid_scalar_add.xml` targets exactly this path: dense scalar samples (40M rows, 200 series, one sample per 15 s) aggregated with `step` = `window` = 300 s, so every in-range sample contributes to exactly one bucket and ~20 consecutive samples land in the same bucket. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Speed up the `timeSeries*ToGrid` aggregate functions: per-sample bucket math now avoids Int128 division, and consecutive samples in the same bucket skip the hash-map lookup. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1498` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Check access rights in EXPLAIN QUERY TREE and EXPLAIN SYNTAX
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/78938 `EXPLAIN QUERY TREE` and `EXPLAIN SYNTAX` (in the analyzer) resolve the query and dump table metadata such as column names and types, but unlike `EXPLAIN PLAN` they do not build a query plan. The `SELECT` access check that the planner performs in `prepareBuildQueryPlanForTableExpression` was therefore skipped, so a user with no privileges could read the column names and data types (including `Enum` element lists) of tables they are not allowed to access, while `SELECT`, `EXPLAIN PLAN` and `EXPLAIN PIPELINE` are correctly rejected. This adds a `SELECT` access check for every table referenced anywhere in the query tree (including tables inside subqueries in expressions such as `WHERE x IN (SELECT ... FROM t)`). The check mirrors the planner: it validates access to the columns that are actually read, with the trivial-count fallback (access is granted if at least one column is accessible) for queries that read no specific column, e.g. `SELECT count() FROM t`. As a result, a user with a column-level grant sees the same behavior as for a plain `SELECT` (`EXPLAIN QUERY TREE SELECT granted_col FROM t` is allowed, `... other_col ...` is denied). `buildQueryTree` only builds the tree; table identifiers are bound to storages and columns are resolved by the query analysis pass. The check runs on the resolved tree: on `query_tree` directly when the passes already resolved it, or on a throwaway resolved copy otherwise (e.g. `EXPLAIN QUERY TREE run_passes = 0`, which intentionally dumps the unresolved tree, so the tree that gets dumped is unchanged). ### Changelog category (leave one): - Critical Bug Fix (crash, data loss, RBAC) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `EXPLAIN QUERY TREE` and `EXPLAIN SYNTAX` not checking access rights on the referenced tables, which allowed a user without privileges to read table column names and data types. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: Arrow Flight SQL: CommandGetXdbcTypeInfo is not implemented
signal.text: ### Company or project name _No response_ ### Describe the unexpected behaviour ## Describe the issue [`CommandGetXdbcTypeInfo`](https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/f64e90ac8305c2cab5abd849f02abac305d7a955/format/FlightSql.proto#L1075-L1138) - the standard Flight SQL command that returns the server's data-type catalog - is not handled by the Arrow Flight SQL server. The [command dispatch](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Server/ArrowFlight/commandSelector.cpp#L626-L718) covers GetSqlInfo / GetCatalogs / GetDbSchemas / GetTables / GetTableTypes / GetPrimaryKeys and the statement commands, but has no branch for `CommandGetXdbcTypeInfo`, so it falls into the [`NotImplemented` catch-all](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/31f8c5d8418ef7e0e75c43a9956590e5f065e6f8/src/Server/ArrowFlight/commandSelector.cpp#L713-L718): ```Command is not implemented: [type.googleapis.com/arrow.flight.protocol.sql.CommandGetXdbcTypeInfo]``` ## Impact Generic clients rely on this catalog to interpret column types: - **Power BI**'s built-in ADBC Flight SQL path fails to load **every** table - even a single `String` column - with `Expression.Error: Unable to understand the type for column` (Verified: the identical connector works once type metadata is supplied client-side.) - The Flight SQL **JDBC** driver's `DatabaseMetaData.getTypeInfo()` has the same dependency. Related: the `CommandGetTables` `include_schema` path serializes schemas without any `ARROW:FLIGHT:SQL:*` field metadata (e.g. `TYPE_NAME`), so per-column type names are unavailable there as well. ### How to reproduce ```python # pip install pyarrow import pyarrow.flight as flight client = flight.FlightClient("grpc://localhost:9006") tok = client.authenticate_basic_token(b"default", b"clickhouse") url = b"type.googleapis.com/arrow.flight.protocol.sql.CommandGetXdbcTypeInfo" any_msg = bytes([0x0A, len(url)]) + url # google.protobuf.Any{type_url}, empty message desc = flight.FlightDescriptor.for_command(any_msg) client.get_flight_info(desc, flight.FlightCallOptions(headers=[tok])) # -> ArrowNotImplementedError: Command is not implemented: ...CommandGetXdbcTypeInfo ``` Reproduced on 26.5.1.882 and 26.6.1.1193 (official Docker images). ### Expected behavior _No response_ ### Error message and/or stacktrace _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_

signal.title: Add tests for the HTTP status code of an unknown role and for a conflicting quota key
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104075 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104092 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Two stateless tests for `src/Server/HTTP` branches that nothing currently asserts. `04870_http_role_unknown_status_code.sh` covers `exceptionCodeToHTTPStatus.cpp:109`, where `UNKNOWN_ROLE` belongs to the `HTTP_NOT_FOUND` group, so a non-existent `role=` query parameter must answer 404. `03096_http_interface_role_query_param.sh` greps the response body only and asserts no HTTP status at all (`grep -c http_code` is 0; only 5 tests in `0_stateless` assert `%{http_code}`), so dropping that mapping would silently fall through to 500 and break client retry logic while leaving CI green. The test also requests the same URL without the parameter and expects 200, so a non-200 above can only come from the role lookup. `04871_http_quota_key_conflict.sh` covers `authenticateUserByHTTP.cpp:291-299`, which rejects a quota key supplied both as the `X-ClickHouse-Quota` header and as the `quota_key` query parameter. `01399_http_request_headers.sh` passes each source alone but never both, so the conflict is never reached. One case suffices: the check sits after the auth-scheme if/else closes at `:289`, so every scheme converges on the same `throw`. Both were mutation-tested rather than merely run. Deleting the `UNKNOWN_ROLE` term turns the expected 404 into 500, and deleting the conflict `throw` removes the `Code: 36` line; each test fails in that state and passes on unmodified master, including 100 runs with randomized settings. Both assert only build-independent surfaces (an HTTP status code, one error code), use test-unique names, require no role or user setup, and need no `no-parallel` tag. Requested by @ zlareb1 in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103950#issuecomment-5243989578, which asked me to re-open a batch of closed coverage PRs. I triaged all 18 and am re-filing these 2; the reason for each of the other 16 is posted on its own PR.

signal.title: Keep the projection's intermediates out of the WITH FILL header
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114404 Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107700 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS_DOESNT_MATCH` for a distributed query combining an `ALIAS` column whose body is an expression with `ORDER BY ... WITH FILL ... INTERPOLATE`. ### Description `analyzeSort` passed every column *available* to the `Before INTERPOLATE` step through as an output. A step's available columns are all the nodes of the previous step's `ActionsDAG` — the intermediates of a computed expression included, since a later step is allowed to *reference* any of them. Turning "referenceable" into "must be in the stream" pinned those intermediates into the header of the `Filling` step. That made the header depend on something that should not matter. Two query trees that differ only by whether an `ALIAS` column was inlined into its defining expression produced different headers, because `v * 2` contributes its `2` and the un-inlined `a_v` does not: ``` un-inlined inlined __table1.k __table1.k __table1.a_v multiply(__table1.v, 2_UInt8) __table1.v __table1.v 2_UInt8 <- extra materialize(__table1.k) materialize(__table1.k) a_v a_v ``` A distributed query is planned from the un-inlined tree on the initiator and executed from the inlined one on the shard, so the two headers meet. `buildShardCollapseFanOut` only handles a *smaller* shard header, and the positional `makeConvertingActions` then throws `NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS_DOESNT_MATCH`. The fix holds back the projection's own intermediates and passes everything else through as before, including the sort columns materialized just above, which is what `Filling` fills by. They all remain *inputs* either way, so the step still asks the previous one to produce them. One exception has to be carved out: a column that an `INTERPOLATE` expression names. Those expressions become actions later, in `Planner`, against a dag built from this step's *header*, so whatever they reference must survive as a column even when the query does not select it — `INTERPOLATE (inter AS inter2 + inter)` where `inter2` is not in the `SELECT` list. Those names are collected by visiting the expressions into a throwaway dag. ### Scope Everything here is inside `if (query_node.hasInterpolate())`, so only queries with `INTERPOLATE` change. The shape was already broken over a `Distributed` table before #107700, since that path has always inlined `ALIAS` columns; #107700 extended the inlining to the parallel-replicas paths and so exposed it there too. Both are fixed. It also stops the reconciliation failure from masking a query error: `INTERPOLATE (k AS k)` on an `ORDER BY` column reports `INVALID_WITH_FILL_EXPRESSION` again instead of `NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS_DOESNT_MATCH`. ### Validation Built and run against a three-replica localhost cluster and a two-shard `Distributed` table, compared with the CI binaries of the commit before #107700 (`75b17ad`) and of its merge (`dd01d270e`): | | before #107700 | after #107700 | this | |---|---|---|---| | repro, parallel replicas shipping a plan | pass | `NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS_DOESNT_MATCH` | pass | | repro, parallel replicas shipping SQL | pass | `NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS_DOESNT_MATCH` | pass | | repro over a 2-shard `Distributed` table | `NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS_DOESNT_MATCH` | `NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS_DOESNT_MATCH` | pass | | `INTERPOLATE (k AS k)` under parallel replicas | `INVALID_WITH_FILL_EXPRESSION` | `NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS_DOESNT_MATCH` | `INVALID_WITH_FILL_EXPRESSION` | The new test `04891_with_fill_interpolate_alias_column_header` reports four exceptions on the commit before #107700 and seven on the merge commit, and passes here. Every self-contained stateless test mentioning `WITH FILL` or `INTERPOLATE`, plus the `ALIAS`-shipping tests from #107700, passes: 94 of 94.
