signal.title: Segmentation guard gated on `balance > 0` drops the old unconditional size cap
signal.text: ### Describe what's wrong **Feeding non-JSON bytes containing no opening bracket to `JSONEachRow` with `input_format_parallel_parsing=1` buffers the entire input into a single segmentation `Memory<>` before failing. The old code threw as soon as the segment exceeded `10 * min_chunk_bytes_for_parallel_parsing`.** - **Root cause:** [`src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp:53`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp#L53) — the `balance > 0` conjunct. The check it replaced (`min_bytes != 0 && current_object_size > 10 * min_bytes`) was unconditional, so it also bounded bytes accumulated outside any object. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `ParallelParsingInputFormat` segmentator -> `JSONUtils::fileSegmentationEngineJSONEachRow` -> `fileSegmentationEngineJSONEachRowImpl` ([`src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp:53`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp#L53)). The size check is now inside `if (max_row_size && balance > 0)`. While no opening bracket has been seen `balance` stays 0, `find_first_symbols` scans to the buffer end, `continue` re-enters `loadAtPosition`, and the segment grows with no bound until EOF. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp:53`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp#L53) — size check gated on balance > 0 - [`src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp:111`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp#L111) — object_start_bytes updated only when balance reaches 0 **Impact:** The DoS protection that `01701_parallel_parsing_infinite_segmentation.sh` was written to guard is weakened: malformed input that never opens a bracket (truncated files, an HTML error page piped into `JSONEachRow`, JSONEachRow data sent to `JSONCompactEachRow` where the searched bracket is `[`) is buffered in full instead of being rejected at `10 * min_chunk_bytes_for_parallel_parsing` (100 MiB with defaults). Transient memory per malformed request grows from a bounded 100 MiB to the full input size. Because `input_format_json_max_object_size` is also not consulted anywhere on the non-parallel `JSONEachRow` data path, the segmentation engine is the only enforcement point for this format. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `da67f74224255`). ### How to reproduce _See root cause description and affected locations above._ ### Expected behavior ``` Code: 117. DB::Exception: Size of JSON object at position ... is extremely large. Expected not greater than 1048576 bytes, but current is ... bytes per object. Increase the value of setting 'input_format_json_max_object_size' or check your data manually, most likely JSON is malformed. (INCORRECT_DATA) ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` Code: 117. DB::Exception: Unexpected eof: (at row 0) : (in file/uri (fd = 0)): While executing JSONEachRowRowInputFormat: While executing File. (INCORRECT_DATA) ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Drop the `balance > 0` conjunct and keep `object_start_bytes` as the anchor: `if (max_row_size)` still measures bytes since the last completed object, which is the intended semantics and additionally bounds inter-object garbage. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - `input_format_json_max_object_size` is never read on the non-parallel `JSONEachRow`/`JSONCompactEachRow` data-parsing path with a known schema (verified: with `--input_format_json_max_object_size=1000 --structure='a String'`, a 50007-byte object is accepted at `input_format_parallel_parsing=0` and rejected at `=1`), which contradicts the setting description in `src/Core/FormatFactorySettings.h` ("The same limit is applied in both parallel and non-parallel parsing paths"). Found during automated review of [PR #107669](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107669). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr107669_002` </details> cc @Avogar @Manerone (from #107669)
signal.author: clickgapai

signal.title: INSERT rejected with NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK when an ALIAS column declares STATISTICS
signal.text: ### Describe what's wrong **A table created with an ALIAS column carrying explicit `STATISTICS(...)` accepts INSERTs on 26.4-26.7 but rejects every INSERT after this PR: `Code: 10. DB::Exception: Not found column b in block. There are only columns: a. (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK)`. The table becomes effectively read-only after upgrade; SELECT, merges and `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS` keep working.** - **Root cause:** The insert path uses `ColumnsStatistics::build` (hard `getByName`) while the merge path uses `ColumnsStatistics::buildIfExists`, which skips columns absent from the block ([`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:690-700`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L690-L700)). Statistics on non-physical columns are otherwise treated as unsupported — `addImplicitStatistics` skips Alias/Ephemeral columns (Statistics.cpp:927-929) and `ALTER ... ADD STATISTICS` rejects them via `columns.hasPhysical` (StatisticsDescription.cpp:181) — but the inline `CREATE TABLE ... col T ALIAS expr STATISTICS(...)` form has no such check (ColumnsDescription.cpp:260-261). Flipping `materialize_statistics_on_insert` to `true` turns that latent inconsistency into a hard INSERT failure. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `MergeTreeSink::writeNewTempPart` ([`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeSink.cpp:409`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeSink.cpp#L409)) -> `MergeTreeDataWriter::writeTempPartImpl` ([`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp:848`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp#L848)) -> `ColumnsStatistics` ctor collects every column whose statistics description is non-empty, including ALIAS columns ([`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:644-647`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L644-L647)) -> `ColumnsStatistics::build` looks the column up with `block.getByName` ([`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:684`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L684)), and an ALIAS column is never in the written block. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp:849`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp#L849) — insert path calls ColumnsStatistics::build on the written block - [`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:684`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L684) — build() uses block.getByName, which throws for a column not in the block - [`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:646`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L646) — ColumnsStatistics ctor does not skip Alias/Ephemeral columns - [`src/Storages/StatisticsDescription.cpp:181`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/StatisticsDescription.cpp#L181) — ALTER path rejects statistics on non-physical columns; the inline CREATE path does not **Impact:** Any table whose DDL puts `STATISTICS(...)` on an ALIAS column stops accepting INSERTs after upgrading to 26.8 (or after `SET materialize_statistics_on_insert = 1`). The error is an internal-sounding `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK` at write time with no hint that statistics caused it, and there is no DDL-time warning. `ALTER TABLE ... DROP STATISTICS <alias_col>` is not a workaround either, since that path also refuses non-physical columns. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `2746afad95f`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/63424d1d-98a2-4f38-92d8-552f32129820) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Test that INSERT works when an ALIAS column declares statistics. DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_alias_statistics; SET allow_statistics = 1; SET materialize_statistics_on_insert = 1; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_alias_statistics; CREATE TABLE t_alias_statistics (a UInt64, b UInt64 ALIAS a + 1 STATISTICS(basic)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY a; INSERT INTO t_alias_statistics VALUES (1), (2), (3); SELECT a, b FROM t_alias_statistics ORDER BY a; DROP TABLE t_alias_statistics; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` 1 2 2 3 3 4 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` Received exception from server (version 26.8.1): Code: 10. DB::Exception: Received from 127.0.0.1:19020. DB::Exception: Not found column b in block. There are only columns: a. (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK) (query: INSERT INTO t_alias_statistics VALUES (1), (2), (3);) ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Use `statistics.buildIfExists(block)` on the insert path (matching `MergeTask`'s `BuildStatisticsTransform`), or skip Alias/Ephemeral columns in the `ColumnsStatistics` constructor the way `addImplicitStatistics` does. Rejecting the DDL instead is the wrong lever: the same code path parses metadata on ATTACH/startup, so existing tables would fail to load. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - The same `build` vs `buildIfExists` asymmetry would also fire for any other future column kind that is present in the metadata but absent from the written block. Found during automated review of [PR #109454](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109454). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr109454_001` </details> cc @alexey-milovidov @rschu1ze @egor-click (from #109454)

signal.title: Pushdown applies view-level `FINAL`/`SAMPLE` to shards: row set changes, `ILLEGAL_FINAL`
signal.text: ### Describe what's wrong **With the default `optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 1`, `FINAL` and `SAMPLE` written on a view reference are propagated to the shard-local table instead of being ignored. Two user-visible consequences: (a) `SELECT id, val FROM <view over ReplacingMergeTree Distributed> FINAL` returns a different row set than before (3 rows -> 2 rows, verified); (b) `SELECT count() FROM <view over plain MergeTree Distributed> FINAL`, which returned a count in every released version, now throws `ILLEGAL_FINAL` (code 181). Same for `SAMPLE`: `SELECT count() FROM view SAMPLE 1/2` went from 1000 to 492.** - **Root cause:** [`src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp:2238`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp#L2238) — `dist_table.setTableExpressionModifiers(TableExpressionModifiers{merged_final, merged_sample_size, merged_sample_offset});` is applied unconditionally whenever the outer reference carries modifiers, with no check that the underlying table supports them and no gate on the resulting semantic change. There are two defensible readings of intent and they need different fixes, so this is filed rather than assumed: (i) propagating `FINAL`/`SAMPLE` is the intended behaviour (04092 Test 1 asserts it for `ReplacingMergeTree`) — then the PR is a Backward Incompatible Change, not a Performance Improvement, and the `ILLEGAL_FINAL` case still needs handling because it turns a working query into an error; (ii) the pushdown was meant to be result-neutral — then the modifier merge should be dropped, or the pushdown suppressed whenever the outer reference carries `FINAL`/`SAMPLE`. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `buildQueryPlanForTableExpression` ([`src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp:2227-2239`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp#L2227-L2239)) reads the outer `TableNode`'s `TableExpressionModifiers` (the `FINAL`/`SAMPLE` the caller wrote on the view reference), ORs `FINAL` with the view body's own modifiers, and calls `dist_table.setTableExpressionModifiers(...)` on the inlined `Distributed` table node. That node is then substituted with the shard-local table, so the shard receives `... FROM (SELECT id FROM local_table FINAL) ...`. On the `StorageView::readImpl` path the outer modifiers were never forwarded into the view body, so `FINAL`/`SAMPLE` on a view reference were silently dropped. For a plain `MergeTree` the shard-side analyzer rejects the modifier in `QueryAnalyzer::validateTableExpressionModifiers` and throws `ILLEGAL_FINAL`. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp:2238`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp#L2238) — unconditional `setTableExpressionModifiers` merging outer `FINAL`/`SAMPLE` into the inlined `Distributed` table node - [`src/Storages/StorageView.cpp:522`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Storages/StorageView.cpp#L522) — `tryGetUnderlyingDistributed` gates the pushdown on parameterized/`DEFINER` views only; it does not consider whether the underlying engine supports the modifiers the caller wrote **Impact:** Queries that ran successfully in every released version start failing with `ILLEGAL_FINAL` after upgrade, with no opt-in, whenever a view over a `Distributed` table backed by an engine without `FINAL` support is read with `FINAL`. Queries over `ReplacingMergeTree`/`CollapsingMergeTree`-backed views silently change their row set. The behaviour is also inconsistent in a way users cannot predict: whether `FINAL` takes effect now depends on whether the view happens to satisfy the AST-level triviality test (a view with an `ORDER BY` in its body, or over a local table, still ignores `FINAL`). </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `6c53bb45d8b`). ### How to reproduce ```sql -- Test that FINAL on a view over a Distributed table behaves the same regardless of -- optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed: the plain MergeTree case must not start failing, -- and the ReplacingMergeTree case must not change its row set. SET enable_analyzer = 1; SET enable_parallel_replicas = 0; SET prefer_localhost_replica = 0; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_04892_plain; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_04892_plain_dist; DROP VIEW IF EXISTS t_04892_plain_view; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_04892_repl; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_04892_repl_dist; DROP VIEW IF EXISTS t_04892_repl_view; CREATE TABLE t_04892_plain (id UInt32) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; INSERT INTO t_04892_plain SELECT number FROM numbers(4); CREATE TABLE t_04892_plain_dist AS t_04892_plain ENGINE = Distributed(test_shard_localhost, currentDatabase(), t_04892_plain); CREATE VIEW t_04892_plain_view AS SELECT id FROM t_04892_plain_dist; CREATE TABLE t_04892_repl (id UInt32, val UInt32, ver UInt32) ENGINE = ReplacingMergeTree(ver) ORDER BY id; SYSTEM STOP MERGES t_04892_repl; INSERT INTO t_04892_repl VALUES (1, 10, 1); INSERT INTO t_04892_repl VALUES (1, 20, 2); INSERT INTO t_04892_repl VALUES (2, 30, 1); CREATE TABLE t_04892_repl_dist AS t_04892_repl ENGINE = Distributed(test_shard_localhost, currentDatabase(), t_04892_repl); CREATE VIEW t_04892_repl_view AS SELECT id, val FROM t_04892_repl_dist; SELECT 'repl_off', id, val FROM t_04892_repl_view FINAL ORDER BY id, val SETTINGS optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 0; SELECT 'repl_on', id, val FROM t_04892_repl_view FINAL ORDER BY id, val SETTINGS optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 1; SELECT 'plain_off', count() FROM t_04892_plain_view FINAL SETTINGS optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 0; SELECT 'plain_on', count() FROM t_04892_plain_view FINAL SETTINGS optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 1; DROP VIEW t_04892_repl_view; DROP TABLE t_04892_repl_dist; DROP TABLE t_04892_repl; DROP VIEW t_04892_plain_view; DROP TABLE t_04892_plain_dist; DROP TABLE t_04892_plain; ``` ### Expected behavior ``` repl_off 1 10 repl_off 1 20 repl_off 2 30 repl_on 1 10 repl_on 1 20 repl_on 2 30 plain_off 4 plain_on 4 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` repl_off 1 10 repl_off 1 20 repl_off 2 30 repl_on 1 20 repl_on 2 30 plain_off 4 <run aborts here> Code: 181. DB::Exception: Storage MergeTree doesn't support FINAL. (ILLEGAL_FINAL) (in query: SELECT 'plain_on' AS `'plain_on'`, count() AS `count()` FROM (SELECT `__table2`.`id` AS `id` FROM `test_h4x5c2x3u5n2`.`t_04892_plain` AS `__table2` FINAL) AS `__table1`) ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Pick one of the two intents and make it explicit. If propagation is intended: keep the merge but relabel the changelog category as Backward Incompatible Change with an explicit note, and suppress the pushdown (falling back to `readImpl`) when the outer reference carries `FINAL` and the underlying table does not support it, so a previously-working query does not start erroring. If result-neutrality is intended: drop the merge at :2227-2239 and instead suppress the pushdown whenever `table_expression_query_info.table_expression`'s `TableExpressionModifiers` are set. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> Found during automated review of [PR #101791](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/101791). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr101791_002` </details> cc @simonmichal @alexey-milovidov (from #101791)
signal.author: clickgapai

signal.title: View pushdown force-disables `extremes`, dropping the block on single-shard clusters
signal.text: ### Describe what's wrong **With the default `optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 1`, `SELECT ... FROM <trivial view over a single-shard Distributed table> SETTINGS extremes = 1` returns no extremes block at all. The same query against the underlying `Distributed` table, and the same query with the setting turned off, both return it.** - **Root cause:** [`src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp:2331`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp#L2331) — `read_context->setSetting("extremes", Field(false));`. The comment above it (:2324-2327) justifies the override by asserting "The outer query still runs under query_context, so the limits remain enforced on the result the client receives." That is true for `max_result_rows`/`max_result_bytes`, which are enforced by the pipeline on the final result, but false for `extremes`, which needs either a plan step on the initiator or `add_extremes` on the remote source — and the pushdown removes both. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `buildQueryPlanForTableExpression` ([`src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp:2329-2331`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp#L2329-L2331)) builds `read_context` for the pushed-down read and sets `extremes` to false on it. That context becomes `effective_context` and is passed to `effective_storage->read(...)`, i.e. `StorageDistributed::read`, and from there to `ReadFromRemote` ([`src/Processors/QueryPlan/ReadFromRemote.cpp:564`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Processors/QueryPlan/ReadFromRemote.cpp#L564), `add_extremes = context->getSettingsRef()[Setting::extremes]`). So the shard is never asked for extremes. Separately, because the pushdown swaps `effective_storage` to the `Distributed` table, `getQueryProcessingStage` returns `Complete` on a single-shard cluster and the initiator's plan collapses to a bare `ReadFromRemote` — so `Planner.cpp:2677 addExtremesStepIfNeeded` never contributes an initiator-side `ExtremesStep` either. Both producers of the extremes block are eliminated. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp:2331`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp#L2331) — `read_context->setSetting("extremes", Field(false))` on the context used for the pushed-down `StorageDistributed::read` - [`src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp:1221`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp#L1221) — sibling optimization `pushOrderByIntoView` bails out when `extremes` is set instead of overriding it — the treatment this path should have used **Impact:** Any client asking for `extremes` (the `extremes` setting, `--extremes`, or the `extremes` key of `JSON*` formats) silently stops receiving min/max rows when reading a qualifying view over a single-shard `Distributed` table. There is no error and no warning — the block is simply absent, so consumers that key off it see no data rather than a failure. Single-shard `Distributed` tables are the common starting topology (and the shape used by `test_shard_localhost` in most of this PR's own tests). Multi-shard clusters are unaffected because the initiator retains an `ExtremesStep`. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `6c53bb45d8b`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/255ed7d0-67d5-43df-8d66-8a5b1bd3a564) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Test that `extremes` is still reported for a query reading a view over a single-shard Distributed table. SET enable_analyzer = 1; SET enable_parallel_replicas = 0; SET prefer_localhost_replica = 0; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_04891_local; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_04891_dist; DROP VIEW IF EXISTS t_04891_view; CREATE TABLE t_04891_local (id UInt32) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; INSERT INTO t_04891_local SELECT number FROM numbers(4); CREATE TABLE t_04891_dist AS t_04891_local ENGINE = Distributed(test_shard_localhost, currentDatabase(), t_04891_local); CREATE VIEW t_04891_view AS SELECT id FROM t_04891_dist; SELECT 'control_distributed_table'; SELECT id FROM t_04891_dist ORDER BY id SETTINGS extremes = 1; SELECT 'view_pushdown_off'; SELECT id FROM t_04891_view ORDER BY id SETTINGS extremes = 1, optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 0; SELECT 'view_pushdown_on'; SELECT id FROM t_04891_view ORDER BY id SETTINGS extremes = 1, optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 1; DROP VIEW t_04891_view; DROP TABLE t_04891_dist; DROP TABLE t_04891_local; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` control_distributed_table 0 1 2 3 0 3 view_pushdown_off 0 1 2 3 0 3 view_pushdown_on 0 1 2 3 0 3 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` control_distributed_table 0 1 2 3 0 3 view_pushdown_off 0 1 2 3 0 3 view_pushdown_on 0 1 2 3 ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Do not override `extremes` on `read_context`. Either drop that line entirely (`max_result_rows`/`max_result_bytes` are the only two that need the override, and unlike `extremes` they are enforced at the pipeline boundary), or, matching the precedent set by `pushOrderByIntoView` at :1221, add `settings[Setting::extremes]` to the list of conditions that suppress the pushdown. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - Worth checking whether any other initiator-side step gated on the storage stopping short of `Complete` disappears under the same stage flip — the `where_filters` / row-level-filter step just below the `till_stage` computation is the obvious candidate to audit. Found during automated review of [PR #101791](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/101791). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr101791_001` </details> cc @simonmichal @alexey-milovidov (from #101791)

signal.title: Nullable LHS defeats the no-supertype cast guard: nullIn(NULL, 'x') returns 1
signal.text: ### Describe what's wrong **With compare-nulls semantics (`nullIn`/`notNullIn`, or `transform_null_in = 1`) and a `Nullable` left-hand side, a non-constant set element that cannot be represented in the left-hand side type silently becomes a `NULL` set member. `SELECT nullIn(CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(UInt8)'), materialize('x'))` returns 1 (and `notNullIn` returns 0) on both analyzers; the correct answer is 0 (resp. 1) because `'x'` is not `NULL`.** - **Root cause:** `cast_elements_to` is initialised to `left_type`, and the guard immediately below only ever *adds* `Nullable` (`makeNullableOrLowCardinalityNullableSafe`). When `left_type` is already `Nullable`, the guard cannot remove it, so the cast target stays `Nullable` even under compare-nulls semantics and a failed `CAST` produces a matching `NULL` instead of throwing. The PR's own `04839` pins `SELECT nullIn(1, materialize('x'))` as `CANNOT_PARSE_TEXT` for the non-`Nullable` LHS — merely wrapping the same left-hand side in `toNullable` turns that error into a silent answer. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `ActionsMatcher::visit` ([`src/Interpreters/ActionsVisitor.cpp:1094`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Interpreters/ActionsVisitor.cpp#L1094)) / `QueryAnalyzer::resolveFunction` ([`src/Analyzer/Resolve/resolveFunction.cpp:1782`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Analyzer/Resolve/resolveFunction.cpp#L1782)) → no common supertype for `{Nullable(UInt8), String}` → cast-to-LHS-type fallback at resolveFunction.cpp:1808 / ActionsVisitor.cpp:1259 → `CAST('x' AS Nullable(UInt8))` yields `NULL` → `isNotDistinctFrom(NULL, NULL)` / `has([NULL], NULL)` matches. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Analyzer/Resolve/resolveFunction.cpp:1808`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Analyzer/Resolve/resolveFunction.cpp#L1808) — Case 3 scalar RHS: cast_elements_to = left_type, then Nullable-only guard - [`src/Interpreters/ActionsVisitor.cpp:1259`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Interpreters/ActionsVisitor.cpp#L1259) — old-analyzer row-wise rewrite: same cast-to-LHS-type fallback **Impact:** Silently wrong boolean results for `nullIn`/`notNullIn` and for `IN`/`NOT IN` under `transform_null_in = 1` whenever the left-hand side is `Nullable` and the non-constant right-hand side contains a value with no common supertype (e.g. a `String` against a numeric/`Date`/`UUID`/`IPv4` column). Every `NULL` row matches the set, so `WHERE nullable_col IN (some_string_expr)` selects all `NULL` rows and `NOT IN` drops them. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `6c53bb45d8b`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/82b544fb-550e-4257-9a5d-322c41921cf1) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Test: with compare-nulls IN semantics, a non-constant set element that cannot be represented in -- the left-hand side type must not become a NULL member of the set when the left-hand side is Nullable. SELECT nullIn(CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(UInt8)'), materialize('x')) SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 1; SELECT notNullIn(CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(UInt8)'), materialize('x')) SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 1; SELECT CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(UInt8)') IN (materialize('x')) SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 1, transform_null_in = 1; SELECT nullIn(CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(UInt8)'), materialize('x')) SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 0; SELECT notNullIn(CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(UInt8)'), materialize('x')) SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 0; SELECT CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(UInt8)') IN (materialize('x')) SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 0, transform_null_in = 1; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` 0 1 0 0 1 0 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` 1 0 1 1 0 1 ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Make the cast target non-`Nullable` under compare-nulls semantics regardless of the left-hand side's nullability — e.g. `cast_elements_to = compare_nulls && !isNullableOrLowCardinalityNullable(right_type) ? removeNullable(left_type) : ...` — so an unrepresentable element throws `CANNOT_PARSE_TEXT` exactly as it already does for a non-`Nullable` left-hand side (`04839`). Alternatively keep the `Nullable` cast but AND the comparison with a cast-succeeded predicate so the phantom `NULL` cannot match. Trade-off: the first option makes `nullIn(toNullable(1), materialize('x'))` throw where it currently returns 0, which is the behavior `04839` already pins for the non-`Nullable` left-hand side. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - The multi-element form (`x IN (materialize('a'), materialize('b'))`) goes through `convertTupleToArray`/`makeInArrayArgumentsList` and shows the same phantom `NULL` under the analyzer; that path's `common_type = in_first_argument->getResultType()` fallback predates this PR, so fixing only the scalar path leaves the tuple path inconsistent. Found during automated review of [PR #104993](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104993). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr104993_001` </details> cc @niyue @alexbakharew @alexey-milovidov (from #104993)

signal.title: arrayIntersect overflow guard tests isInteger on a Nullable type, so it never fires
signal.text: ### Describe what's wrong **`arrayIntersect` on `Nullable` integer arrays of different widths silently matches values that do not survive the narrowing cast to the common element type. `arrayIntersect([toNullable(1)], [toNullable(257)])` returns `[1]`; the non-Nullable form `arrayIntersect([1], [257])` correctly returns `[]`. Pre-existing — not introduced by this PR.** - **Root cause:** arrayIntersect.cpp:398 sets `nested_init_type` to the array's nested type WITHOUT removing `Nullable`, and line 401 then calls `isInteger(nested_init_type)`. `WhichDataType(Nullable(UInt32))` is `TypeIndex::Nullable`, so `isInteger` (and `isDate`/`isDateTime`/`isDateTime64`) return false and the whole overflow-mask block is skipped for every `Nullable` argument. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `executeImpl` (arrayIntersect.cpp:463) computes the common subtype with `getMostSubtype`, which NARROWS (`Nullable(UInt16)` + `Nullable(UInt8)` -> `Nullable(UInt8)`), then `castColumns` casts the wider argument down. `prepareArrays` is meant to catch the values that changed under that cast by building `arg.overflow_mask` (arrayIntersect.cpp:395-415), and the element loop skips masked elements (arrayIntersect.cpp:711). For a `Nullable` array the guard at line 401 never lets that happen, so the truncated value is inserted and matched as if it were the original. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Functions/array/arrayIntersect.cpp:401`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2485f1496f7dff/src/Functions/array/arrayIntersect.cpp#L401) — overflow-mask guard: isInteger on a still-Nullable nested type - [`src/Functions/array/arrayIntersect.cpp:398`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2485f1496f7dff/src/Functions/array/arrayIntersect.cpp#L398) — nested_init_type keeps its Nullable wrapper **Impact:** Wrong results from `arrayIntersect` whenever the arguments are `Nullable` arrays of different integer widths (or Date/DateTime widths) and a value in the wider argument aliases a value in the narrower one modulo the narrower type. Reachable from ordinary SQL over two `Array(Nullable(...))` table columns; `Nullable` array columns are common, and the non-Nullable behaviour that users would infer from `00930_arrayIntersect.sql` is the opposite. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `2485f1496f7dff`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/6be77c3a-66e5-40e6-9596-b3c75b04e31c) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Test: a value that does not survive the cast to the common element type is not in the intersection, -- also when the arrays are Nullable. DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_04869; SELECT arrayIntersect([1], [257]); SELECT arrayIntersect([toNullable(1)], [toNullable(257)]); SELECT arrayIntersect([-100], [156]); SELECT arrayIntersect([toNullable(-100)], [toNullable(156)]); DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_04869; CREATE TABLE t_04869 (a Array(Nullable(UInt32)), b Array(Nullable(UInt8))) ENGINE = Memory; INSERT INTO t_04869 VALUES ([1024, 1031], [0, 7]), ([256, 300], [0, 44]); SELECT arraySort(arrayIntersect(a, b)) FROM t_04869 ORDER BY a; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_04869; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` [] [] [] [] [] [] ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` [] [1] [] [156] [0,44] [0,7] ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Strip `Nullable` before the type test, e.g. compute `auto init_nested = removeNullable(nested_init_type);` and gate on that. `callFunctionNotEquals` is already handed the null-stripped nested columns (arrayIntersect.cpp:389-392), so the types passed with them at lines 408-409 must be null-stripped too, and the existing `removeNullable(overflow_mask)` at line 412 then becomes redundant rather than load-bearing. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - `arrayUnion` and `arraySymmetricDifference` use `getLeastSupertype` and therefore never narrow — verified `arrayUnion([toNullable(1)], [toNullable(257)])` = `[1,257]`. No sibling call site to fix. Found during automated review of [PR #113021](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113021). Severity P1 · Finding `h_pr113021_001` </details> cc @alexey-milovidov (author of #113021) ### Additional context _Generated by ClickGap / Claude._

signal.title: `BigQueryClient::requestJSON` builds HTTP headers from user-controlled arguments without `HTTPHeaderFilter`, so `billing_project`/`access_token` can inject headers and smuggle a second request
signal.text:
_Found via ClickGap automated review. Please close or comment if this is incorrect or needs adjustment._ ### Describe what's wrong A line break inside the `billing_project` or `access_token` argument of `bigquery(...)` / `ENGINE = BigQuery(...)` is copied verbatim into the outgoing HTTP request, adding attacker-chosen headers and - with a blank line - a complete second HTTP request that the endpoint executes with the same credentials. The identical value is rejected by the `url` table function with `HTTP header "X" has invalid character` (BAD_ARGUMENTS). **Root cause:** src/Storages/BigQuery/BigQueryClient.cpp:218 and :220 add user-controlled header values without routing them through `HTTPHeaderFilter::checkAndNormalizeHeaders`, which src/Common/HTTPHeaderFilter.cpp:24 uses to reject any name or value containing '
' and to enforce the admin `<http_forbid_headers>` list. **Why we believe this is a bug:** `BigQueryConfiguration::fromArguments` (BigQueryConfiguration.cpp:135) accepts `billing_project` and `access_token` as arbitrary strings - `checkIdentifierPart` is applied only to `project`, `dataset` and `table` - then `BigQueryClient::requestJSON` (BigQueryClient.cpp:215-238) puts them into `HTTPHeaderEntries` and passes them to `BuilderRWBufferFromHTTP(...).withHeaders(headers)`. `context->getHTTPHeaderFilter().checkAndNormalizeHeaders(...)` is never called on this path, while `Poco::Net::HTTPRequest::set` performs no validation of its own. **Affected locations:** - `src/Storages/BigQuery/BigQueryClient.cpp:218` — Authorization header built from the unvalidated `access_token` - `src/Storages/BigQuery/BigQueryClient.cpp:220` — X-Goog-User-Project header built from the unvalidated `billing_project` - `src/Storages/BigQuery/BigQueryConfiguration.cpp:42` — only project/dataset/table go through `checkIdentifierPart`; billing_project and access_token are unchecked **Impact:** Two concrete consequences. (a) The admin `<http_forbid_headers>` filter, honoured by `StorageURL`, `StorageURLCluster` and the S3/Web object-storage configurations, has no effect on BigQuery requests. (b) Credentials stored in a named collection are meant to be usable without being readable; a user who may only call `bigquery(my_collection, billing_project = '...')` can append `

<any request>` and have ClickHouse issue arbitrary authenticated BigQuery API calls (for example `DELETE .../datasets/x/tables/y`) with the collection's service-account token, against the same host the `remote_host_filter` allowed. ## Assumptions The bot recorded these claims it could not verify directly from source. A maintainer ✅ confirms; ❌ flags a wrong premise (the bot should rework or close the finding). - [ ] **A real BigQuery front end (or any HTTP/1.1 server) processes the smuggled pipelined request** - *Why unverifiable:* the reproduction uses a local raw-socket listener, not googleapis.com - *Falsifiable test:* capture the bytes ClickHouse writes (the test does exactly this) and replay them against an HTTP/1.1 server with keep-alive enabled; the second request line is a syntactically complete request on the same connection ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `aa1a69b2a3c04d`). ### How to reproduce ```sql SET a raw listener and run: SELECT * FROM bigquery('p','d','t', base_url = 'http://127.0.0.1:<port>', access_token = 'tok', billing_project = 'proj
X-Injected: yes'); then inspect the bytes received on <port> - they contain a separate `X-Injected: yes` header line. Contrast with SELECT * FROM url('http://127.0.0.1:<port>/', JSONEachRow, 'a Int64', headers('X' = 'ok
X-Injected: yes')), which fails with BAD_ARGUMENTS before any request is sent. ``` ### Expected behavior ``` CAPTURE_WORKS url: NOT_INJECTED bigquery billing_project: NOT_INJECTED bigquery access_token: NOT_INJECTED ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` CAPTURE_WORKS url: NOT_INJECTED bigquery billing_project: INJECTED bigquery access_token: INJECTED ``` ### Additional context **Open risks:** - The same `HTTPHeaderEntries` path is used for `getTable`, `listTableData` and `insertAll`, so all three request kinds are affected; they share the single call site and need no separate fix. **Suggested fix:** In `BigQueryClient::requestJSON`, pass the assembled `HTTPHeaderEntries` through `context->getHTTPHeaderFilter().checkAndNormalizeHeaders(headers)` before `withHeaders(headers)` - the same call `StorageURL.cpp:1095` makes - or validate `billing_project` and `access_token` in `BigQueryConfiguration::validate` alongside the existing `checkIdentifierPart` checks. **Analysis details:** Confidence HIGH | Severity P1 | Testability: `STATELESS_SQL` Found during automated review of [PR #110166](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110166). --- _ClickGapAI · Confidence: HIGH · Severity: P1 · Finding: `h_pr110166_001`_

signal.title: Fix wrong subcolumn value over a `Merge` table with a mistyped child
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110844 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a wrong result when reading a subcolumn such as `arr.size0` through a `Merge` table whose child table declares that column with a type that does not expose the subcolumn. The subcolumn was filled with a default value while the parent column in the same row was converted correctly, so `sum(arr.size0)` silently undercounted. It is now derived from the converted parent column, so a parent value that cannot be converted raises an error instead of silently reading as a default. ### Description A `Merge` table resolves each requested column name against the child independently, so a subcolumn name is just another name. If the child declares the parent column with a type that does not expose that subcolumn, the name resolves nowhere in the child and takes the subcolumn's type default, while the parent is converted to the `Merge` table's declared type. One row then carries a converted parent and a subcolumn value contradicting it: ``` SELECT _table, arr, arr.size0, length(arr) FROM zm ORDER BY _table, arr; zb [4,5,6] 0 3 -- subcolumn must be 3 zg [1,2] 2 2 ``` There is no exception, and it reproduces at default settings. It is analyzer-specific: with `enable_analyzer = 0` the subcolumn resolves against the child's own type and the query raises `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`, which the test pins. The fix derives the subcolumn from the parent the wrapper converts, as a resolved `getSubcolumn(CAST(<parent>, '<declared type>'), '<subcolumn>')` evaluated before the structural conversion. A child that genuinely lacks the column keeps its default, which is what makes a `Merge` over different column sets work; so does a parent outside the child's physical read list. `MATERIALIZED` and `DEFAULT` parents derive like ordinary ones. One deliberate change: an unconvertible parent value now raises an error where the subcolumn read as a default. Reading that parent alone already raised it. Validated with a new stateless test covering both settings, every parent column kind, nested arrays, the `.null` sibling subcolumn, repeated identically-structured children, a child `ALIAS` column, a child engine without subcolumn support, and a row policy hiding an unconvertible parent. A 419-test A/B sweep with only the fix reverted shows zero regressions. `Buffer` and `View` carry this defect through other mechanisms and ship separately. Reading a subcolumn of an `ALIAS` parent through a `Merge` is also wrong today; that predates this change, needs a different fix, and is tracked separately.

signal.title: Paimon incremental read: the unfenced processing_lock lets a second consumer silently duplicate acknowledged rows after a session expiry
signal.text: ## Describe what's wrong The Paimon incremental-read stream state (`allow_experimental_paimon_storage_engine`) coordinates competing consumers that share one `paimon_keeper_path` with an ephemeral `processing_lock` znode. That lock has **no fencing**, so if the lock is lost while a consumer is mid-read (the usual cause being a Keeper session expiry that auto-removes the holder's ephemeral node), a second consumer acquires the freed lock and re-reads the same committed snapshot range. Both consumers then deliver the same committed data — an at-least-once **duplicate of already-acknowledged rows, with no error logged anywhere**. The `processing_lock` exists precisely to make the read/commit critical section mutually exclusive, so this defeats its only purpose. The unfenced-ness is visible in three places in `src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Paimon/PaimonStreamState.cpp` (line numbers on `master`): 1. Acquire writes the owner's `replica_name` into the lock node but it is **never read back** anywhere — the value is dead (`acquireProcessingLock`, lines 70–90): ```cpp keeper->create(processing_lock_path, replica_name, zkutil::CreateMode::Ephemeral); ``` 2. Release is an **unconditional** `tryRemove(path, -1)` whose return code is discarded, so it deletes whatever node is at the path — including an ephemeral created by a *different* session (`removeProcessingLock`, lines 269–274): ```cpp keeper->tryRemove(processing_lock_path, -1); ``` 3. The watermark advance is a **blind** `makeSetRequest(..., -1)` in its own standalone `tryMulti` with no check op on the lock and no monotonicity guard, so it succeeds regardless of whether the caller still holds the lock or whether another consumer moved the watermark underneath it (`setCommittedSnapshot`, lines 214–238): ```cpp ops.emplace_back(zkutil::makeSetRequest(committed_path, toString(snapshot_id), -1)); ``` For contrast, the sibling `is_active` node in the *same file* is fenced correctly — it reads the node back with its `Stat` and removes it version-checked (`tryGet(is_active_path, existing_identifier, &stat)` then `tryRemove(is_active_path, stat.version)`, lines ~159 and ~165) — so applying the same discipline to `processing_lock` is clearly feasible. Note this is distinct from the documented "at-most-once" window (a *loss* on crash between watermark advance and delivery): the issue here is a **duplicate with no crash**, produced by a routine session expiry, which an at-most-once contract does not permit. ## Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes, reproduces on current `master`. The Paimon storage engine is experimental (`allow_experimental_paimon_storage_engine`, default off). ## How to reproduce Two ClickHouse instances (two Keeper sessions), each with a Paimon incremental-read table over the **same** warehouse and the **same** `paimon_keeper_path`: ```sql -- on both servers CREATE TABLE c (id Int64, v String) ENGINE = PaimonLocal('/warehouse/db.db/t1') SETTINGS paimon_incremental_read = 1, paimon_keeper_path = '/paimon/stream', paimon_replica_name = 'ra'; -- 'rb' on the second server ``` 1. Commit snapshot 1 to the warehouse; consumer A drains it, so `committed_snapshot` = 1. 2. Commit snapshots 2 and 3 (ids above the watermark). 3. Consumer A starts an incremental read: it acquires `processing_lock`, reads `committed_snapshot` (still 1), and plans the read of snapshots 2–3. 4. Consumer A's Keeper session expires (network blip / GC pause / Keeper failover exceeding `session_timeout_ms`). A's ephemeral `processing_lock` is auto-removed, but A's in-flight read continues (its server process is alive; the ZooKeeper client reconnects on a fresh session). 5. Consumer B polls: it acquires the now-free `processing_lock`, reads `committed_snapshot` (still 1, because A has not advanced it yet), and delivers snapshots 2–3. 6. Consumer A finishes: its blind `setCommittedSnapshot(3)` succeeds (version `-1`), and A also delivers snapshots 2–3. Both consumers have now delivered snapshots 2–3 — the same committed rows twice, with no error. The window in step 3–4 is deterministically reproducible by pausing A's `setCommittedSnapshot` multi to Keeper and deleting the `processing_lock` znode during the pause (which is exactly what a session expiry does to the ephemeral), then letting B poll and finally releasing A. ## Expected behavior Each committed snapshot is delivered to at most one consumer. A consumer that lost its `processing_lock` (session expiry, or the node otherwise gone) must not silently commit over another consumer's progress: the watermark advance and the lock release should be fenced by lock ownership (e.g. a version/session check, as `is_active` already does) so that a stale holder fails loudly instead of duplicating acknowledged data. ## Error message and/or stacktrace None — this is the problem. No exception is thrown and nothing is logged; the duplication is silent. ## Additional context The three call sites above are all in `src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Paimon/PaimonStreamState.cpp`.

signal.title: Add LOOKUP INDEX support for MergeTree
signal.text: This change adds table-wide `LOOKUP INDEX` support for `MergeTree` tables and implements the `Set` and `Join` tables as indices task from #87836. Unlike secondary data-skipping indices, these indices build reusable in-memory lookup structures for repeated key-value style queries against the right-hand side table. It introduces: - `LOOKUP INDEX ... TYPE table_set` for `IN table` lookups and trivial key-only subqueries - `LOOKUP INDEX ... TYPE table_join` for direct-compatible equality joins with `join_algorithm = 'direct'` - parser, metadata, `ALTER`, and `ReplicatedMergeTree` support - planner integration, runtime cache invalidation for both data and metadata changes, stateless tests, performance benchmarks, and minimal user documentation Current limitations: - lookup keys must be plain columns - `table_join` requires non-nullable key columns - `table_join` is only used for direct-compatible equality joins - `table_join` is not always faster than `hash`; the included benchmarks show win, near-parity, and lose cases depending on the relative sizes of the left and right tables ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add `LOOKUP INDEX` support for `MergeTree` tables with `table_set` and `table_join` table-wide lookup indexes. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **High Risk** > High risk because it adds a new experimental index type that touches SQL parsing/formatting, ALTER/replication metadata, MergeTree read paths and caching, and join/set planner optimizations (including direct join behavior), which can affect query correctness and performance. > > **Overview** > Adds experimental `LOOKUP INDEX` support to `MergeTree`-family tables (gated by `allow_experimental_lookup_index`) with two new index types: `table_set` to accelerate `IN table`/trivial key-only subqueries and `table_join` to accelerate direct-compatible equality joins. > > Extends SQL/metadata plumbing end-to-end: new AST fields and parser/formatter support for `LOOKUP INDEX` (including `ALTER TABLE ... ADD/DROP LOOKUP INDEX`), metadata storage and replication via `ReplicatedMergeTreeTableMetadata`, and validation to prevent misuse (e.g., no `GRANULARITY`, no expressions/args, and non-nullable keys for `table_join`). > > Implements runtime lookup caches in `MergeTreeData` (with invalidation on metadata/part changes) and integrates planner fast paths for sets (`CollectSets`) and joins (`PlannerJoins`/`DirectKeyValueJoin`) while preserving correctness by disabling the optimization when row policies or unsupported modifiers/parallel replicas are in play. Adds documentation plus new stateless/performance tests for both lookup modes. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 6d94b002fc3c8794f1e83f81f540b2b85ebd9198. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: Optimize aggregations of LowCardinality of 128 and 256 bit integers
signal.text: This is simply expanding what is done for narrower integers to wider ones. Comparing `column_low_cardinality_key_holder` to the previous commit: | Key type | Encoding | Before CPU time | After CPU time | Reduction | Speedup | |-----------|----------|----------------:|---------------:|----------:|--------:| | `UInt8` | Plain | 320,240 ns | 321,169 ns | -0.3% | 1.00x | | `UInt8` | LC | 1,366,296 ns | 1,369,728 ns | -0.3% | 1.00x | | `UInt16` | Plain | 320,863 ns | 322,198 ns | -0.4% | 1.00x | | `UInt16` | LC | 1,391,415 ns | 1,377,083 ns | 1.0% | 1.01x | | `UInt32` | Plain | 320,757 ns | 321,323 ns | -0.2% | 1.00x | | `UInt32` | LC | 1,388,380 ns | 1,385,711 ns | 0.2% | 1.00x | | `UInt64` | Plain | 326,842 ns | 325,383 ns | 0.4% | 1.00x | | `UInt64` | LC | 1,381,219 ns | 1,440,143 ns | -4.3% | 0.96x | | `UInt128` | Plain | 1,012,926 ns | 911,887 ns | 10.0% | 1.11x | | `UInt128` | LC | 8,019,216 ns | 1,452,770 ns | 81.9% | 5.52x | | `UInt256` | Plain | 8,149,345 ns | 8,132,693 ns | 0.2% | 1.00x | | `UInt256` | LC | 11,576,753 ns | 1,498,433 ns | 87.1% | 7.73x | For end-to-end benchmark in `group_by_integer_key_width.xml`: | Grouping key | Before median | After median | Reduction | Speedup | |-------------------------------|--------------:|-------------:|----------:|--------:| | `LowCardinality(UInt64)` | 2.0680 s | 2.1344 s | -3.2% | 0.97x | | `UInt64` | 0.6938 s | 0.6905 s | 0.5% | 1.00x | | `LowCardinality(UInt128)` | 2.8588 s | 2.5819 s | 9.7% | 1.11x | | `UInt128` | 1.0269 s | 1.0140 s | 1.3% | 1.01x | | `LowCardinality(UInt256)` | 3.3996 s | 2.9630 s | 12.8% | 1.15x | | `UInt256` | 1.7643 s | 1.6781 s | 4.9% | 1.05x | There's ~5% noise level if you look at the unaffected paths. There's now also a test to ensure that the right aggregation is used. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Optimize aggregations of LowCardinality of 128 and 256 bit integers.

signal.title: Report the real error when an in-place `IN`-set build destroys its source
signal.text: `FutureSetFromSubquery::buildOrderedSetInplace` speculatively builds the set of an `IN` subquery during index analysis. A subquery whose source plan cannot be cloned - a read from a remote cluster, for example - takes the destructive path there, which consumes the source plan. When that build then throws, the set can never be built again: `build` returns a null plan, every caller takes that for "nothing left to build", and the query keeps running with an unready set until `FunctionIn` reports the logical error `Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in'`. That is exactly what happens whenever a caller deliberately ignores an in-place build failure. Statistics-based part pruning is such a caller: it logs the failure and keeps reading the part whose condition it could not evaluate. So ```sql SELECT count() FROM t WHERE a IN (SELECT a FROM clusterAllReplicas('cluster_with_an_unavailable_replica', currentDatabase(), t)) ``` reported `Not-ready Set` instead of the connection error, which aborts the server in a build with `abort_on_logical_error`. The failure of a destructive in-place build is remembered now and rethrown from `build` instead of returning a null plan, so the query fails with the real reason - the same error it fails with when no in-place build is attempted at all. This is the cause of the recurring master `Stress test` failure `Logical error: Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'A (STID: 0250-3e49)`, seen on `arm_release` and `arm_msan` a few times a day since 2026-07-23: CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=2926be24e6102daae60b8f44c88969495a76ec3c&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_release%29 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107924 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107619 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix the logical error `Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in'` for a query with an `IN` subquery reading from a remote cluster: the query now fails with the actual error from the subquery, such as a connection failure.
signal.author: alexey-milovidov

signal.title: Do not drop the whole GROUP BY when unwrapping injective functions of constants
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104863 (same logical error, closed earlier without this cause identified) ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix wrong results for a `GROUP BY` whose only key is an injective function of constants, for example `SELECT 1 FROM t GROUP BY materialize(NULL)`. Such a key was removed by `optimize_injective_functions_in_group_by`, which left the query with no `GROUP BY` and no aggregation at all, so it returned one row per input row instead of one row per group. Over a `Merge` table that mixes a local and a remote child the same cause also raised the logical error `Chunk info was not set for chunk in GroupingAggregatedTransform`. ### Description `unwrapInjectiveFunctionsInKeys` unwraps an injective function to its arguments and skips constant arguments, so a key that is an injective function *of a constant* unwraps to nothing and is dropped. `OptimizeGroupByInjectiveFunctionsPass` assigned that result unconditionally: when such a key was the only one and the query had no aggregate function, `GROUP BY` became empty and the query stopped aggregating. Under a `Merge` table mixing a child that aggregates with one that does not, the un-aggregated child's raw chunks reach a merge transform that requires aggregate state; both wordings of the message occur, `GroupingAggregatedTransform` and `MergingAggregatedTransform`, depending on `distributed_aggregation_memory_efficient`, and one fix closes both. Found by the fuzzers, e.g. [AST fuzzer (amd_debug)](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=94148&sha=8eb1df1331f7fd5dcf93b4b0e975e56685b6f732&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29). The fix assigns the unwrapped list only when it is non-empty, which is what `OptimizeLimitByInjectiveFunctionsPass` already does for `LIMIT BY` and what the non-analyzer `TreeOptimizer::optimizeGroupBy` does via `appendUnusedGroupByColumn`. Of those three sibling paths only the analyzer's `GROUP BY` pass lacked the guard. The shared helper is unchanged, so `LIMIT BY` is unaffected. A per-key variant was deliberately not used: it would weaken the optimization when another key survives, and it is the branch added in 462445c2c201a5f and removed the next day in 355909eb3a415b7. `GROUP BY materialize(NULL), k` still groups by `k` alone. Affected queries now return a different row count, which is the point of the fix. Across 25 shapes the patched default is byte-identical to running with `optimize_injective_functions_in_group_by = 0`, where before it diverged on 7 of them; `enable_analyzer = 0` and a plain `GROUP BY NULL` key agree. The old behaviour stays reachable with that setting. The new test fails on master and passes here.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Add IPv4/IPv6 auto-inference for JSON shared data insertion
signal.text: Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110761 ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added `input_format_try_infer_ipv4` and `input_format_try_infer_ipv6` settings (both disabled by default) that allow ClickHouse to automatically infer `IPv4`/`IPv6` types from string fields during schema inference for text formats, following the same pattern as `input_format_try_infer_dates`. --- ## What does this PR do? Adds two new opt-in format settings that allow ClickHouse to automatically infer `IPv4`/`IPv6` types from string values during schema inference for text formats, following the same pattern as the existing `input_format_try_infer_dates` / `input_format_try_infer_datetimes` settings. ## New settings | Setting | Default | Description | |---|---|---| | `input_format_try_infer_ipv4` | `false` | Infer `IPv4` from strings matching IPv4 address format | | `input_format_try_infer_ipv6` | `false` | Infer `IPv6` from strings matching IPv6 address format | ## How it works In `insertIntoSharedData` (`JSONExtractTree.cpp`), after the existing Date/DateTime inference chain, two new blocks attempt to parse the string as IPv4/IPv6 using the already-existing `IPv4Node::tryParse` / `IPv6Node::tryParse` methods. On a match, the value is encoded with its native binary type (`BinaryTypeIndex::IPv4`/`IPv6`) instead of falling back to `String`. ## Storage benefit | Value | As String | As IPv4 | |---|---|---| | `"192.168.100.200"` | 15 bytes | 4 bytes | | `"10.0.0.1"` | 8 bytes | 4 bytes |
signal.author: valerypetrov

signal.title: Race condition on `StorageObjectStorageConfiguration::(get/set)Paths`
signal.text: ClickHouse S3 related functions, when not using hive partitioning, supports writing multiple files to the same file path by appending a numbered counter at the end when using `s3_create_new_file_on_insert=1`. ``` create table s3_table (id UInt32) engine=s3(s3_conn, filename='root/file.parquet'); insert into s3_table values 1 SETTINGS s3_create_new_file_on_insert=1; insert into s3_table values 2 SETTINGS s3_create_new_file_on_insert=1; select _file, id from s3_table; "root/file.parquet", 1 "root/file.parquet.1", 2 ``` The way this has been implemented is through an in-memory vector keeping the paths produced by this function/ table so that the next insert knows the next filename and upon reading it is possible to enumerate all files. When the server re-starts, this information is lost and ClickHouse relies on a slow retry-mechanism to get the latest inserted file path. When looking at https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/87592, I realized the `StorageObjectStorageConfiguration::getPaths/setPaths` methods are not thread safe. AFAIK, `StorageObjectStorage::write` can be executed in parallel and does not impose any locking mechanism - which might result in the `paths` object being modified simultaneously. The obivous answer is to add protection around `(get/set)Paths`, but honestly wouldn't it be better if we just deprecated it since [hive partitioning is becoming the default](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/86746)? The downside tho is that we would no longer support multiple writes to a fixed location without a partition strategy. Actually, it could also break the wildcard partition strategy in case the user is also relying on `s3_create_new_file_on_insert`
signal.author: arthurpassos

signal.title: Row policy over a file-backed table breaks `DEFAULT` columns missing from the data file (`UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`; silently wrong results on 26.7)
signal.text: 🕵 Found while working on https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114262 (lazy materialization for local Parquet files); the behavior is identical with that PR's optimization on or off, and reproduces on current master without it. **Describe what's wrong** When a table over a data file (`File(Parquet)`, and by code inspection the same applies to the object-storage path) has a `DEFAULT` column that is missing from the file, and a row policy references either that column or interacts with reading it, the query fails with `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` — the source prunes the `DEFAULT` expression's input columns before `AddingDefaultsTransform` can compute the column. On the official 26.7 build, the first case below returned **silently wrong results** (0 rows instead of 900): the policy was evaluated against type defaults instead of real row values. Current master turned that into a fail-safe exception, which is safer, but the queries are legitimate and should work. **How to reproduce** ```bash clickhouse local ``` ```sql INSERT INTO FUNCTION file('rp.parquet', Parquet) SELECT number AS k, number % 10 AS a, concat('val_', toString(number)) AS s FROM numbers(1000) SETTINGS engine_file_truncate_on_insert = 1; -- Case 1: the row policy references a DEFAULT column missing from the file. CREATE TABLE t_rp_j (k UInt64, a UInt64, s String, j JSON DEFAULT toJSONString(map('user', map('name', concat('u', toString(a)))))) ENGINE = File(Parquet, 'rp.parquet'); CREATE ROW POLICY pol_j ON t_rp_j USING j.user.name != 'u0' TO ALL; SELECT k, s FROM t_rp_j ORDER BY k LIMIT 3; -- Code: 47. DB::Exception: Unknown expression or function identifier `a` in scope -- _CAST(toJSONString(map('user', map('name', concat('u', toString(a))))), 'JSON') AS j ... While executing File. -- Official 26.7 instead returns 0 rows (silently wrong: expected 900 rows admitted by the policy). -- Case 2: the policy is on a plain file column, and the query selects a DEFAULT -- column depending on another file column, together with a PREWHERE. CREATE TABLE t_rp_d (k UInt64, a UInt64, s String, d UInt64 DEFAULT a * 2) ENGINE = File(Parquet, 'rp.parquet'); CREATE ROW POLICY pol_d ON t_rp_d USING a != 0 TO ALL; SELECT k, d FROM t_rp_d PREWHERE s != 'val_2' ORDER BY k LIMIT 3; -- Code: 47. DB::Exception: Unknown expression or function identifier `a` in scope _CAST(a * 2, 'UInt64') AS d ... -- (the same statement without PREWHERE works and returns 1→2, 2→4, 3→6) ``` **Expected behavior** Both queries return the same result as with the row policy applied above the read (e.g. as `MergeTree` does): case 1 → 900 rows admitted by the policy computed from real `a` values; case 2 → `d` computed from `a` after prewhere filtering. **Where it comes from** `updateFormatPrewhereInfo` / `SourceStepWithFilter::applyPrewhereActions` shrink the format header to the filter DAG's outputs, dropping input columns that a `DEFAULT` expression of another (missing) column needs; `AddingDefaultsTransform` inside the source then cannot compute the default. For case 1 the policy's own input is a missing defaulted column, so its dependency `a` is never part of the read set to begin with. **Additional context** Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114262 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110970
signal.author: alexey-milovidov

signal.title: query_plan_join_swap_table changes the result of ANY INNER JOIN with OR-ed ON conditions (deterministic, max_threads = 1)
signal.text: ### Describe the bug The planner's automatic build-side swap (`query_plan_join_swap_table`, default `auto`) changes the result of an `ANY INNER JOIN` with **OR-ed conditions** in `ON`. On identical single-part tables, single-threaded, the swapped plan deterministically returns **6 rows** and the unswapped plan **3 rows** — the swapped output is a strict superset. `EXPLAIN actions = 1` shows both plans keep `Type: inner | Strictness: any | Algorithm: HashJoin` while the table read order flips, so the `ANY` deduplication is applied to opposite sides. With a single equality condition (no `OR`) both plans agree, so the multi-disjunct key path is the trigger. ### How to reproduce ```sql CREATE TABLE l (a Int32, b Int32) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY a; CREATE TABLE r (a Int32, b Int32) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY a; INSERT INTO l SELECT number % 8, number % 3 FROM numbers(12); INSERT INTO r SELECT number % 5, number % 8 FROM numbers(12); SELECT * FROM l ANY JOIN r ON l.b = r.b OR l.a = r.a ORDER BY ALL SETTINGS max_threads = 1, query_plan_join_swap_table = 'true'; -- 6 rows SELECT * FROM l ANY JOIN r ON l.b = r.b OR l.a = r.a ORDER BY ALL SETTINGS max_threads = 1, query_plan_join_swap_table = 'false'; -- 3 rows ``` Outputs, stable across 20/20 runs per arm (`clickhouse local`, one part per table, `max_threads = 1`): ``` -- swap 'true' (and the default 'auto', which swaps here): 0 0 0 0 0 2 0 2 1 1 1 1 2 2 2 7 3 0 3 3 4 1 4 4 -- swap 'false': 0 0 0 0 0 2 0 2 1 1 1 1 ``` Whatever row choice `ANY` is permitted to make per key, the two plans do not even agree on the **number** of emitted rows, and the divergence is controlled purely by a performance plan setting. Note also that both outputs emit only a small subset of the left keys that have matches (for example `l = (2, 1)` matches `r = (4, 1)` via `b` but is emitted by neither plan), so the intended `ANY` + `OR` semantics may be off in both plans — the deterministic swap-controlled difference is the unambiguous part. ### Affected versions Reproduced on master 26.8.1.1068 and on 26.7. Not bisected. ### Related Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112640 (the `ANY LEFT JOIN` + `OR` face of the swap: racy under `max_threads > 1`; this `INNER` face is deterministic and single-threaded) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111645 Found by an automatic optimizer-testing framework (differential testing of optimizer settings, query plans, and equivalent rewrites).
signal.author: zlareb1

signal.title: Inconsistent AST formatting: `view((SELECT ...))` in table-function arguments loses subquery parentheses and cannot be parsed back (STID: 1941-1bfa)
signal.text: 🕵 Found by `AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted, old_compatibility)` on an unrelated PR (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/91993, which only touches hex encoding): [CI report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=91993&sha=eae3a3cbbfb5d81bed061634d53c701167dce04a&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%2C%20old_compatibility%29). The fuzzer produced a query containing `view((SELECT ...))` as an argument of a comparison function nested inside `file(...)` table-function arguments. Formatting the AST drops the parentheses around the `view` subquery argument (`view((SELECT ...))` → `view(SELECT ...)`), and the formatted text cannot be parsed back, so the format-consistency check fails with a logical error (`abortOnFailedAssertion` in the debug build): ``` Logical error: 'Inconsistent AST formatting: the query: DESCRIBE TABLE file(concat(xor(if(indexHint(and(greaterOrEquals(alias5764._time, toLowCardinality(toNullable(1048575)) + number), lessOrEquals(alias5764._time, view((SELECT toUInt16OrDefault(65536, equals(minus(materialize(NULL, arrayElement(b)), greater(lowCardinalityIndices('\\\\', toLowCardinality(NULL)), -1)), toInt8OrZero(2147483646)))))))), a <= toInt256OrDefault(-2147483647), materialize(isNullable(NULL))), and(b >= 257, 1.1754943508222875e-38 > b)), currentDatabase(), toFixedString(toNullable('_04513.orc'), assumeNotNull(256)))) SAMPLE 100 / 5 SETTINGS input_format_orc_use_fast_decoder = 0 cannot parse query back from DESCRIBE TABLE file(concat(xor(if(indexHint(and(greaterOrEquals(alias5764._time, toLowCardinality(toNullable(1048575)) + number), lessOrEquals(alias5764._time, view(SELECT toUInt16OrDefault(65536, equals(minus(materialize(NULL, arrayElement(b)), greater(lowCardinalityIndices('\\\\', toLowCardinality(NULL)), -1)), toInt8OrZero(2147483646))))))), a <= toInt256OrDefault(-2147483647), materialize(isNullable(NULL))), and(b >= 257, 1.1754943508222875e-38 > b)), currentDatabase(), toFixedString(toNullable('_04513.orc'), assumeNotNull(256)))) SAMPLE 100 / 5 SETTINGS input_format_orc_use_fast_decoder = 0'. ``` The two texts differ only in the parentheses around the `view` subquery: the original has `view((SELECT ...))`, the re-formatted text has `view(SELECT ...)`. On a recent master-based **release** build (`clickhouse local`) the asymmetry is observable in the opposite direction — the parenthesized form is the one that does not parse inside table-function arguments: ```sql -- parses fine (special `view` handling in expression context): SELECT lessOrEquals(t, view((SELECT 1))); -- parses fine (unparenthesized subquery): SELECT * FROM file(if(indexHint(lessOrEquals(t, view(SELECT 1))), 'a', 'b')); -- SYNTAX_ERROR (parenthesized subquery inside table-function arguments): SELECT * FROM file(if(indexHint(lessOrEquals(t, view((SELECT 1)))), 'a', 'b')); ``` So whether `view((SELECT ...))` / `view(SELECT ...)` parses depends on context (plain expression vs. table-function argument) and on build/compatibility configuration, while the formatter always emits the unparenthesized form. Either the parser should accept both forms in all contexts where `view` is accepted at all, or the formatter should print the form that is guaranteed to parse back in the surrounding context. Previous distinct manifestations of this dedup bucket (STID: 1941-1bfa) were fixed individually: #109501 (back-quoted numeric type name, fixed by #109720), #106850, #106358, #100131. This `view` parenthesization case is a new one. CIDB shows this check failing on 5 unrelated PRs in the last 30 days (112921, 110886, 113533, 91993, 111061) and never on master — expected, since the AST fuzzer only runs per-PR with random queries. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Resolved by: #114658 - Merged into: `26.8.1.1436` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->
signal.author: alexey-milovidov

signal.title: Aggregating over `x IN (subquery using shardNum())` from `remote()`/`Distributed` fails: 10 NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK — initiator and shard disagree on the `__set_` id
signal.text: ## Describe the problem When a query over `remote()` or a `Distributed` table (2+ shards) aggregates over an `IN (subquery)` whose subquery uses a shard-dependent function such as `shardNum` or `hostName`, the query fails with exception 10 (`NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK`) at pure default settings. The initiator expects a column named with the `__set_` id from its own analysis, while each shard returns a column named with the `__set_` id from its own analysis of the shipped query — the shard folds `shardNum()` to its local constant, so the set hash (and hence the column name) differs — and `RemoteQueryExecutor` fails to match the block by name: ``` Code: 10. DB::Exception: Not found column sum(in(__table3.number, __set_4038495261199527788_15042459581097328311)) in block. There are only columns: sum(in(__table3.number, __set_16854109006789820482_7702020288925574204)): While executing Remote. (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK) ``` The semantically equivalent plain-`WHERE` form (`WHERE x IN (...)`) works and returns the expected per-shard-set result, so this is purely a naming/header mismatch on the projection path, not a semantics question about `shardNum` in a distributed subquery. ## How to reproduce Version: `26.8.1.653` (public master build). All settings at defaults; no DDL needed: ```sql SELECT sum(number IN (SELECT number FROM numbers(10) WHERE number = shardNum())) FROM remote('127.0.0.{1,2}', numbers(10)); ``` Observed (deterministic, 20/20 runs): ``` Code: 10. DB::Exception: Not found column sum(in(__table3.number, __set_4038495261199527788_15042459581097328311)) in block. There are only columns: sum(in(__table3.number, __set_16854109006789820482_7702020288925574204)): While executing Remote. (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK) ``` Expected: `2` (each of the two shards contributes one matching row; both the pre-analyzer path `enable_analyzer = 0` and the plan-shipping path `serialize_query_plan = 1` return `2`). The equivalent filter form works at defaults and returns the correct result: ```sql SELECT count() FROM remote('127.0.0.{1,2}', numbers(10)) WHERE number IN (SELECT number FROM numbers(10) WHERE number = shardNum()); -- 2 ``` A plain `Distributed` table triggers it identically (no `remote()` needed): ```sql CREATE TABLE t_local (x UInt64) ENGINE=MergeTree ORDER BY x; INSERT INTO t_local SELECT number FROM numbers(100); -- any 2-shard cluster works the same CREATE TABLE dist_n (x UInt64) ENGINE=Distributed(test_cluster_two_shards, currentDatabase(), t_local); -- any 2-shard cluster SELECT sum(x IN (SELECT number FROM numbers(10) WHERE number = shardNum())) FROM dist_n; -- Code: 10, same two mismatched __set_ ids ``` What is REQUIRED vs incidental: - REQUIRED: default settings only — nothing needs to be changed. - REQUIRED (query shape): 2 or more shards (a single remote shard works); a shard-dependent function inside the `IN` subquery — `shardNum()` and `hostName()` both trigger it, while a constant subquery, `rand()`, and `currentDatabase()` do not; the `IN` must be evaluated in the shard-side projection (an aggregate such as `sum`/`countIf`, or the bare expression in `SELECT`) — the same `IN` in `WHERE` is fine. - Incidental: the aggregate wrapper (`sum`, `countIf`, `ifNull(sum(...))`, `toUInt64(... != 0)` all fail the same way), row counts, whether the initiator's own shard participates (`prefer_localhost_replica = 0` and a pure-remote shard list fail identically). - Not failing on: `enable_analyzer = 0`, or `serialize_query_plan = 1` (plan shipping instead of SQL-text shipping). Note the mismatched `__set_` id in "There are only columns" also changes with which shard the offending block came from, consistent with each shard hashing the subquery after folding `shardNum()` to its own value: `remote('127.0.0.{1,2}')` and `remote('127.0.0.{1..3}')` report `__set_16854...`, `remote('127.0.0.{2,3}')` reports `__set_11166...`, while the expected id `__set_40384...` is always the initiator's. ## Additional context The bare-projection form without aggregation (`SELECT number IN (...) FROM remote(...) LIMIT 1`) fails only sporadically (a race — roughly 4 out of 5 runs with `LIMIT 1`, never without `LIMIT`), while the aggregate form is deterministic, so the aggregate form above is the reliable repro. Nearest prior reports, both closed and mechanically different: `shardNum` folding breaking the outer projection name (no sets involved), and a set-identity mismatch specific to shipped `INTERPOLATE` expression packages: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/80691 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111728
